sanskrit:
siṃha-skandhaṃ madhura-madhura-smera-gaṇḍa-sthalāntaṃ
durvijñeyojjvala-rasa-mayāścarya-nānā-vikāram
vibhrat kāntiṃ vikaca-kanakāmbhoja-garbhābhirāmām
ekībhūtam vapur avatu vo rādhayā mādhavasya
translation: Śrī Gauracandra has strong shoulders like a lion, and His beautiful cheeks are decorated by a sweet smile. His transcendental body undergoes many astonishing r a s a m a y a transformations. His complexion is more beautiful than a blooming golden lotus, and His body is the meeting place of Rādhā and Mādhava. May that Lord Gaura be pleased with us.

sanskrit:
śoṇa-snigdhāṅguli-dala-kulaṃ jāta-rāgaṃ parāgaiḥ
śrī-rādhāyāḥ stana-mukulayoḥ kuṅkuma-kṣoda-rūpaiḥ
bhakta-śraddhā-madhu-nakha-mahaḥ-puñja-kiñjalka-jālaṃ
jaṅghānālaṃ caraṇa-kamalaṃ pātu naḥ pūtanāreḥ
translation: May we always serve the lotus feet of the enemy of Pūtanā, Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Ah! How shall I describe the sweetness of those lotus feet? They are soft and reddish, with toes like the leaves of a lotus. The crimson pollen on those lotus feet is kuṅkuma powder from the budding breasts of Śrī Rādhā. The effulgences of those lotus feet are the filaments, the shanks are the stalks, and the bhaktas’ love is the honey.

sanskrit:
bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhau
carataḥ paribhūta-kāla-jāla-bhiyaḥ
bhakta-makarān aśīlita-
mukti-nadīkān namasyāmi
translation: I offer my humble obeisance unto the devotees of Śrī Gauracandra, who are like dolphins sporting in the ocean of bhakti-rasa. They have conquered their fear of the snare of death and care nothing for the river of mukti.

sanskrit:
rātryante trasta-vṛnderita-bahu-viravair bodhitau kīra-śārī-
padyair hṛdyair ahṛdyair api sukha-śayanād utthitau tau sakhībhiḥ
dṛṣṭau hṛṣṭau tadātvodita-rati-lalitau kakkhaṭī-gīḥ saśaṅkau
rādhā-kṛṣṇau satṛṣṇāv api nija-nija-dhāmny āpta-talpau smarāmi
translation: Alarmed that daylight would soon come, Vṛndādevī directed the forest birds to make a tumultuous noise to awaken Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa. Hearing all the loud chirping, along with the pleasant and unpleasant poetry of the śukas and śārikās, Yugala Kiśorī-Kiśora awakened and rose from Their pleasure bed of flowers. Then Lalitā, Viśākhā and other priya-sakhīs Girlfriends Male and female parrots arrived from their respective kuñjas full of jokes and laughter, making the Divine Couple very blissful. But then they heard the monkey Kakkhaṭī scream Jaṭilā's name and became afraid. Gazing at each other with longing eyes, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa then separated and returned home, slipping quietly into Their beds.

sanskrit:
pratisva-sevāvasara-prabodhitā-
sadātanābhyāsa-juṣo ’tha kiṅkarīḥ
nidraiva rātry antam avetya tā jahau
saiva svayaṃ jāgarayāñ cakāra kim?
translation: Realizing that the night had ended, could it be that Nidrā-devī herself had awakened Śrī Rādhā’s sakhīs, who rose just in time to perform their cherished sevās?

sanskrit:
utthāya talpāc cakitekṣaṇāḥ kṣaṇān
duhānayor nāgara-cakravartinoḥ
svāpaṃ rahaḥ-svāpam abhaṅgam aṅganā
ālakṣya tūṣṇīm adhiśayam āsata
translation: After awakening, they became alarmed that the time for sevā might have passed, so they began looking anxiously in every direction. Seeing that Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa were still asleep, they sat quietly on their beds.

sanskrit:
papracchur anyonyam imā mimānayā
rasaṃ parīhāsa-bhṛtaṃ sajṛmbhayā
girā cirāj jāgara-mūḍha-ghūrṇana-
sva-svākṣi-bhṛṅgī-tati-līḍha-vakṣasaḥ
translation: Just to tease the others, one sakhī yawned and asked, “O Sakhīs, how have you awakened, being so exhausted from your sporting with the young prince of Vraja?” Then, as they slowly became conscious, their beelike rolling eyes began to relish the nectar of Kṛṣṇa’s nail marks on each other’s lotus-bud breasts.

sanskrit:
niśānta-sevocita-mālya-vīṭikā-
kṛtyātta-cittā atha kācid āha tāḥ
anaṅga-baddhāṅga-yuva-dvayocchalat-
saurabhya-saulabhyavatī rasoccalā
translation: Because it was time for Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa’s niśānta-sevā, some of the kiṅkarīs began to string garlands and make tāmbūla. After smelling the sweet bodily fragrances of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, whose hearts are firmly bound by Cupid’s arrows, and seeing Them still holding each other in a close embrace, one kiṅkarī fled in excitement. She arrived before her sakhīs, This is the mūla verse from Govinda-līlāmṛta. The following verses describe the events in detail. Service to be performed at the end of night Maidservants, mañjarīs A preparation of betel leaves with lime, catechu, areca nut etc., which is chewed. who were still sitting in their beds, and proclaimed, “Ohe! All of you come see how those two hold each other so closely!”

sanskrit:
jānīta jālādhva-gatāsya-padmāḥ
sadmāntarālyaḥ sva-dṛśaḥ prahitya
kāntau nitāntātanu-lāsya-cuñcu
dhinoti suptiḥ parirabhya kīdṛk?
translation: “O Sakhīs! Place your lotus faces in the lattice windows of the pleasure house and cast your gaze within. You shall see how deep sleep pleasantly embraces those two who are so skillful in Cupid’s dance of love.”

sanskrit:
itas tato nyasta-maṇi-pradīpān-
aphulla-nīlotpala-campakābhān
vidhatta etau sva-mayūkha-vṛndair
anāvṛtair maṇḍana-mālya-celaiḥ
translation: Inside they saw that Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa held each other as They slumbered. Neither wore any clothing, ornaments or garlands, and the yellow and blue lusters emerging from Them caused the jewelled lamps in the cottage to appear as buds of campaka and blue lotus.

sanskrit:
sa kṛṣṇa-meghaḥ sthira-cañcalālī-
vṛto ’timādhurya-rasair amūḥ kim?
āsnāpayat svārhaṇa-kṛtya-vṛttāḥ
pratyarhaṇenādita eva dhinvan
translation: Seeing how delighted the sakhīs were to taste Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa’s sweetness, one mañjarī said to her companion, “O Sakhī! Look, look! Isn’t that a dark cloud garlanded by a lightning bolt? It showers the kiṅkarīs with mādhurya-rasa. Usually servants please their masters and then receive a reward, but today they have received it even before the sevā.”

sanskrit:
tāmbūla-mālā-vividhānulepair
aṅgāra-dhānyāguruvaiś ca dhūpaiḥ
kālocitais taiḥ pratipādyamānaiḥ
kati-kṣaṇāṃs tā gamayāṃ babhūvuḥ
translation: Somewhere else, a few mañjarīs passed the time by stringing garlands and preparing tāmbūla and various cosmetic ointments. Another dāsī began to place pieces of aguru wood in the incense burners.

sanskrit:
prabhañjano rañjayituṃ nikuñja-
A type of magnolia
rājau vyarājiṣṭa mudā tadānīm
manye prabudhya ślatha-durbalāṅgo
drutaṃ prayātuṃ na-tarāṃ śaśāka
translation: Then a gentle springtime breeze began to blow just to please Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. I think this soft breeze wafted through the air so slowly because it too had just awakened from its slumber and could barely move its tired and languid limbs.

sanskrit:
yā vṛkṣa-vallyo vyakasaṃs tadaiva tāś
cumbaṃs tadāmoda-bharair diśo daśa
prasāritaiḥ śvāsapatha-praveśitair
bhṛṅgāvalīr jāgarayāñ cakāra saḥ
translation: Kissing the flowering creepers as it drifted along, this gentle breeze bore their sweet fragrances throughout the forest. As drunken bumblebees lay sleeping in the laps of flowers, they were awakened by the pleasant aroma.

sanskrit:
āsan yad-arthaṃ prathamaṃ dvijendrāḥ
sevā-samutkaṇṭha-dhiyo ’pi mūkāḥ
vṛndā-nideśaṃ tam avāpya harṣāt
krīḍā-nikuñjaṃ paritaś cukūjuḥ
translation: The birds of the kuñja, eager for Vṛndā’s orders, had arrived earlier and were being very quiet. Now, at her signal, from all around they began to joyfully warble their mellow songs.

sanskrit:
athāli-vṛndaṃ makaranda-lubdhaṃ
ratīśitur maṅgala-kambu-tulyam
praphulla-vallī-caya-mañju-kuñje
juguñja talpī-kṛta-kañja-puñje
translation: The hungry bees emitted a humming sound like that of Cupid’s conch shell throughout the beautiful kuñja, which was adorned with blossoming creepers and a bed made of tender lotus petals.

sanskrit:
jhaṅkṛtim aṅgī-kurute
rati-maṅgala-jhallarīva govindam
bodhayituṃ madhu-mattā
madhupī-tatir udbhaṭānandā
translation: To help awaken Govinda, a group of ecstatic female bees, delirious from drinking honey, began to make a pleasant humming sound like the ringing of cymbals.

sanskrit:
pika-śreṇī manojasya
vīṇeva vyakta-pañcamam
ālalāpa svaraṃ tāraṃ
kuhūr iti muhur muhuḥ
translation: A group of cuckoos repeatedly sang “kuhū, kuhū” in the fifth note, producing a tone like that of Cupid’s vīṇā.

sanskrit:
rati-madhura-vipañcī-nāda-bhaṅgīṃ dadhānā
madana-mada-vikūjat-kānta-pārśve niṣaṇṇā
mṛdula-mukula-jālāsvāda-vispaṣṭa-kaṇṭhī
kalayati sahakāre kākalīṃ kokilālī
translation: In the mango trees, the female cuckoos, intoxicated with amorous desire, sat alongside their husbands and savored the sweet juice of the tender buds. A low, sweet sound like that of Rati’s vīṇā clearly emanated from their throats.

sanskrit:
vidrāvya gopī-dhṛti-dharmacaryā-
lajjā-mṛgīr māna-vṛkeṣv amarṣī
kapota-ghūtkāra-miṣeṇa śaṅke
garjaty ayaṃ kāma-tarakṣu-rājaḥ
translation: Meanwhile, the tiger of kāma, having frightened away the doe of the gopīs’ patience, virtue and modesty, and angry at the wolf of their pride, began to growl apprehensively under the guise of the cooing of the doves.

sanskrit:
rādhā-dhairya-dharādharoddhṛti-vidhau ke ’nye samarthā vinā
kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣṇa-sumatta-kuñjara-vaśīkāre ’py alaṃ śṛṅkhalāḥ
anyāḥ kā vṛṣabhānu-jām iha vinā dhanyām atīvādṛtāḥ
kekāḥ kiṃ samudīrayanti śikhinas tau bodhayantaḥ prage
translation: Other than Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who can diminish Śrī Rādhā’s mountain of pride? And who other He fears the coming of daylight will spoil his fun. than Śrī Rādhā can chain the drunken elephant called Kṛṣṇa? To make this known, the peacocks cried kekā, kekā at daybreak to awaken the divine couple.

sanskrit:
hrasva-dīrgha-plutair yuktaṃ
ku-kūkū-kū iti svaram
kukkuṭo ’py apaṭhat prātar
vedābhyāsī baṭur yathā
translation: Just as young brāhmaṇa boys chant the Vedas in the early morning, repeating short, long and very long vowels, in the same way, the wild cocks began to cry ku-kūkū-kū.

sanskrit:
atha pakṣiṇāṃ kalakalaiḥ prabodhitāv
api tau mitho ’vidita-jāgarau tadā
nibiḍopagūhaṇa-vibhaṅga-kātarau
kapaṭena mīlita-dṛśāvatiṣṭhatām
translation: Even though Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa were both roused by the sweet chirping of the birds, for a little while each was unaware that the other was awake. Distressed at the thought of breaking Their close embrace, They both kept Their eyes closed and pretended to remain asleep.

sanskrit:
vṛndeṅgita-jñaḥ sa ‘vicakṣaṇaḥ’ śukaḥ
śuko yathā bhāgavatārtha-kovidaḥ
‘dakṣaḥ’ prabodhe jagatāṃ prabhor ati-
premāspadatvānupamaḥ samabhyadhāt
translation: Because of his divine wisdom and incomparable love of God, Śukadeva has sung beautiful verses to enlighten the inhabitants of the world. In the same way, after getting the signal from Vṛndā, two parrots named Dakṣa and Vicakṣaṇa began to recite verses to awaken the Universal Lord.

sanskrit:
jaya smarāśeṣa-vilāsa-vaiduṣī-
niṣṇāta-gopījana-locanāmṛta!
prāṇa-priyā-prema-dhunī-mataṅgaja!
sva-mādhurī-plāvita-loka-saṃhate
translation: Dakṣa said, “O knower of all sports of love, nectar of the gopīs’ eyes, mad elephant in the stream of Your dear ones’ affection, You who soak the whole world in Your sweetness!”

sanskrit:
priyādharāsvāda-sukhe nimajjasi
prabudhyase nety ucitaṃ rasāmbudhe!
riraṃsutāyāṃ viriraṃsur eva te
kiñcādhuneyaṃ kṣaṇadā kṣaṇaṃ dyati
translation: “O ocean of rasa, as You lie lost in the pleasure of tasting Your lover’s lips, the darkness has ended. You are faultless, but please understand that the same night that has fulfilled Your desire for romance now also brings Your festival of love to a close.”

sanskrit:
jahīhi nidrāṃ ślathayopagūhanaṃ
vrajaṃ pratiṣṭhāsuraraṃ prabho! bhava
prātar babhūvānusara sva-cāturīṃ
pracchanna-kāmatvam athorarī-kuru
translation: After that, Vicakṣaṇa said, “O master, awaken now and give up the embrace of Your dear one. Morning has come and You must quickly prepare for Your return to Vraja. You’ll have to cleverly conceal Your amorous mood to prevent being exposed.”

sanskrit:
jaya vrajānandana! nanda-cetaḥ-
payodhi-pīyūṣa-mayūkha! deva!
goṣṭheśvarī-puṇya-latā-prasūna!
prayāhi gehāya dhinu sva-bandhūn
translation: “O joy of the vrajavāsīs! O moon over the milk ocean of Nanda’s heart! O master! O flower from the holy creeper called Yaśodā! Make all of Your friends happy by going home now (because if by chance Nanda Mahārāja found You here it would be a disaster!).”

sanskrit:
gokula-bandho! jaya rasa-sindho!
jāgṛhi talpaṃ tyaja śaśi-kalpam
prīty-anukūlāṃ śrita-bhuja-mūlāṃ
bodhaya kāntāṃ rati-bhara-tāntām
translation: Then the female parrot Mañjubhāṣiṇī said, “O friend of Gokula! O ocean of rasa! May You be crowned with good fortune. Please awaken and rise from Your moonlike bed. You must also rouse Your dear lover who, exhausted from the romantic evening, lies resting on Your shoulder.”

sanskrit:
udayaṃ prajavādayam ety aruṇas
taruṇī-nicaye sahajākaruṇaḥ
nibhṛtaṃ nilayaṃ vrajanātha! tatas
tvarito ’ṭa kalinda-sutā-taṭataḥ
translation: “O Lord of Vraja! The sun, which is naturally hard-hearted toward the young gopīs, quickly rises above the horizon. Therefore, You must leave the banks of the Yamunā and hastily return to Your home.”

sanskrit:
śārī ‘śubhā’ sā ’tha jagāda ‘sūkṣma-dhīḥ’
śārī yathā devana-sammata-sthitiḥ
jayeśvari! svīya-vilāsa-saubhaga-
śrī-tarṣita-śrī-mukha-mukhya-yauvate
translation: Two very rasika-śārīs named Śubhā and Sūkṣma-dhī, who are always together like a pair of dice, said to Śrī Rādhā, “O joy of Vṛṣabhānu! All glory unto You. Your charm and opulence are wished for by the most beautiful young girls of the universe.”

sanskrit:
kamala-mukhi! vilāsāyāsa-gāḍhālasāṅgī
svapiṣi sakhi! niśānte yat tavāyaṃ na doṣaḥ
dig iyam aruṇitaindrī kintu paśyāvir āsīt
tava sukham asahiṣṇuḥ sādhvi! candrā-sakhīva
translation: “O lotus face! Even though the night is over, You still lie there deeply asleep, fatigued from Your amorous affairs. O Sakhī! There is no fault in this, but please look, O virtuous one! Just like Candrāvalī, the eastern sky grows red in anger, intolerant of Your happiness.”

sanskrit:
śeṣe ’dhunā yad-rati-vallabhāsya-
rājīva-rājan madhu-pāna-mattā
asāmprataṃ tat khalu sāmprataṃ te
prātas tato jāgarayāmy ahaṃ tvām
translation: “Intoxicated from drinking the honey of Your beloved Kṛṣṇa’s lotus face, You remain sound asleep. But morning has come now and I must awaken You.”

sanskrit:
kṛṣṇo ’py anidraḥ priyayopagūḍhaḥ
kāntā ’py anidrā ’py amunopagūḍhā
talpāt prabhātākulam apy analpān
notthātum etan mithunaṃ śaśāka
translation: Even though both Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa were awake, They remained lying together, em- bracing each other. Anxious that the night was over, still They were unable to rise from Their beautiful bed of pleasure.

sanskrit:
kṛṣṇasya jānūpari-yantrita-san-nitambā
vakṣaḥ-sthale dhṛta-kucā vadane ’rpitāsyā
kaṇṭhe niveśita-bhujā ’sya bhujopadhānā
kāntā na hīṅgati manāg api labdha-bodhā
translation: Śrī Rādhā lay with Her hips confined by Kṛṣṇa’s knee, Her breasts upon His chest, and Her face touching His. Her arms, wrapped around His neck, served as a pillow. She was awake, but still She couldn’t move Her limbs even a small amount.

sanskrit:
śrī-kṛṣṇa-līlā-racanāsu dakṣas
tat-prema-jānanda-viphulla-pakṣaḥ
dakṣākhya āha śrita-kuñja-kakṣaḥ
śukaḥ samadhyāpita-kīra-lakṣaḥ
translation: The parrot named Dakṣa, an expert in describing śrī-kṛṣṇa-līlā and the teacher of countless other parrots, arrived in the cottage, spread his wings in ecstatic prema, and began to speak.

sanskrit:
ekaṃ prācyām aruṇa-kiraṇāpāṭalāyāṃ vidhatte
cakṣuḥ kānte tvaritam aparaṃ dūrage cakravākī
śaṅkākrāntās taru-kuhara-gā mūkatāṃ yānti ghūkāḥ
śaṅke bhāsvān udayam udagāt kṛṣṇa! nidrāṃ jahīhi
translation: “O Kṛṣṇa! Look! The sun is rising above the horizon. The cakravākī 15 looks toward the reddish eastern sky, and then toward her distant lover. In fear of crows, the owls quietly enter into the hollows of trees. You must quickly give up Your slumber!”

sanskrit:
jaya jaya guṇa-sindho! preyasī-prāṇa-bandho!
vraja-sarasi-ja-bhāno! sat-kalā-ratna-sāno!
iha hi rajanī-śeṣe kiṃ manā nātha! śeṣe
samayam avakalayāpīṣyate kuñja-sayyā?
translation: “O ocean of good qualities! Beloved of Rādhā! Sun who makes the Vṛndāvana lotuses bloom! Mountain of the jewels of artistic skills! Glory unto You. O master, what could You be thinking as You lie there, even though the night has ended? Why does that bower bed seem so good to You when You know it’s time for Your family to awaken?”

sanskrit:
ayam api ca śikhaṇḍī jāgaritvaiva khaṇḍī
kṛta-sulalita-kekaḥ kāla-niṣṭhā-vivekaḥ
pramilati tava nidrā-hānaye ’dhī-daridrāḥ
śiva śiva nija-sevā-kālam ujjhanti ke vā?
Female heron
translation: “The peacocks, awake and separated from their mates, are aware of the time, so they begin to cry ‘kekā’ in sweet voices. They are coming here just to end Your sleep. How could any intelligent person give up the auspicious time for his sevā?”

sanskrit:
vṛndā-vaktrād adhigata-vidyā
sārī hārī-kṛta-bahu-padyā
rādhā-snehoccaya-madhu-mattā
tasyā nidrāpanayana-yattā
translation: The śārī named Sūkṣma-dhī16 had learned everything about sevā from Vṛndā, and she wore this knowledge like a string of pearls. She was intoxicated from the honey-wine of affection for Rādhā and intent upon awakening Her.

sanskrit:
nidrāṃ jahīhi vijahīhi nikuñja-śayyāṃ
vāsaṃ prayāhi sakhi! nālasatāṃ prayāhi
kāntaṃ ca bodhaya na bodhaya loka-lajjāṃ
kālocitāṃ hi kṛtinaḥ kṛtim unnayanti
translation: She said, “O Sakhī, wake up! Give up that drowsiness and awaken Your beloved. You must immediately leave the kuñja and return to Your own homes. It is time for the working people to begin their activities and You must avoid being publicly disgraced.”

sanskrit:
vraja-pati-tanayāṅkāsaṅgato vīta-śaṅkā
vidhu-mukhi! kim-u śeṣe nirbharaṃ rātri-śeṣe?
pramada-madhupa-puñje mā paraṃ tiṣṭha kuñje
na gaṇayasi vigarhāṃ kiṃ guruṇām anarhām?
translation: “O Moon-face! Having obtained the embrace of Vrajendra-nandana, all fear is gone from Your heart. But why, even at the end of night, do You lie there sound a-sleep? Why don’t You at least move to another place in this kuñja, which is ornamented by swarms of drunken bees? Don’t You even consider what Your elders might say if they caught You here?”

sanskrit:
sudati! kumudinīnām aṅkam āsādya līnā
mada-madhukara-mālā kālam āsādya lolā
sarati kamalinīnāṃ rājim etām adīnāṃ
bhavati samaya eva glāni-harṣādidevaḥ
translation: “O Sudatī! A group of honeybees, drunk from sporting in the laps of the white water lilies, becomes restless now and engages in a love tryst with a cluster of blooming lotuses! The cause of the bees growing tired of the lilies and their excitement for the lotuses can only be the time of day.”

sanskrit:
viyad-atilaghu-tāraṃ tvad-vapuḥ kṣuṇṇa-hāraṃ
vigalita-kusumānāṃ varṣma śephālikānām
tritayam idam idānīm eka-rūpaṃ tadānīm
api yad api tathāpi tvad-vapuḥ śrībhir āpi
translation: “The stars have faded from the sky, Your necklace has fallen from Your body, and the white flowers from the śephālikā trees have dropped to the ground. Even though all three have lost their ornaments, only You have kept Your exquisite beauty.”

sanskrit:
truṭita-patita-muktā-hāravat te viyuktā
bhavad uḍu-tatir eṣā svalpa-mātrāvaśeṣā
cira-śayanam avekṣyārundhatī te vilakṣyā
bhavad iva parivakre paśya saptarṣi-cakre
translation: “Just as the pearls from Your broken necklace have fallen to the ground, the stars have disappeared from the sky and now only a few remain. Just look! Arundhatī, astonished at seeing You sleeping for so long on the chest of Your lover, hides her face within the constellation of Seven Ṛṣis.”

sanskrit:
iti kala-vacanānāṃ śārikāṇāṃ śukānāṃ

tava mukha-śaśi-bimbāloka-mātrāvalambā
translation: “O Śaśi-mukhī! The doe longs for the remnants of Your food and a drink of the water that has washed Your feet. But still, because You haven’t yet looked at her, she sadly gazes at Your moonlike face. Please open Your eyes again and cast Your sweet glance upon this poor deer, who is dependent upon You for her very life.”

sanskrit:
harir atikutukī te netra-yugmaṃ mimīte
nayana-yugam amāya-prema yasyāḥ pramāya
kim api vimala-muktā-mālayā cāru-vaktā
niyatam upamimānaḥ saṃśayaṃ nirdhunānaḥ
translation: “O Rādhe, look! After curiously measuring the wide, innocent, love-filled eyes of the doe, Hari is now doing the same with Yours. To remove any doubt of their similarity, He compares both using a spotless string of pearls, saying, ‘Very nice, indeed!’”

sanskrit:
Moonface
Lover of Kṛṣṇa
Moonface
iti nigaditavatyaḥ śārikāḥ premavatyaḥ
sukhada-pada-padārthāṃ vācam utthāpanārthām
yadi kim api viremuḥ patriṇas taṃ praṇemuḥ
samupasṛta-nikuñjāḥ prāpta-sammoda-puñjāḥ
translation: Speaking in this pleasant and meaningful way, the love-filled śārikās tried to awaken Śrī Rādhā. When they gave up, the ecstatic śukas and other birds approached the kuñja to offer their respects to Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit:
atha śayana-satṛṣṇaṃ bodhayāmāsa kṛṣṇaṃ
vitatir api śukānāṃ kṛṣṇa-harṣotsukānām
śravaṇa-sukhada-saumyaiḥ snigdha-śabdārtha-ramyaiḥ
sarasataram analpaiḥ kūjitaiḥ sīdhu-kalpaiḥ
translation: Eager to serve the sleepy Kṛṣṇa, the śukas tried to awaken Him by making sweet sounds and speaking beautiful words that were soothing to the ear, cheerful and very pleasing.

sanskrit:
praṇaya-rasa-gabhīrāś cāru-śabdārtha-dhīrāḥ
kala-sumadhura-kaṇṭhāḥ prema-jalpeṣv akuṇṭhāḥ
sati samaya-viveke bodhayāṃ cakrur eke
na khalu bata vidagdhāḥ kārya-kāle vimugdhāḥ
translation: Without hesitation, they all began to chatter with sweet voices, speaking charming words full of deep love and affection. Ah! When it’s time for the skilled to perform a task, there is no confusion!

sanskrit:
subhaga! rajani-śeṣe svāpa-gehe suśeṣe
tvam iti hi jananī te saṃśayaṃ svaṃ dhunīte
samayam atha viditvā jāgarārthaṃ tvaritvā
svayam iyam upagantrī sneha evātra mantrī
translation: “O Sundara! Thinking that You are sound asleep in Your own room, Mother Yaśodā hasn’t been concerned. But now that it is time to awaken You, her motherly affection will certainly bring her to Your bedside.”

sanskrit:
tvam asi samaya-vettā sarva-duḥkhaika-bhettā
bhavasi bhuvana-bandhuḥ sad-guṇa-grāma-sindhuḥ
vratati-bhavana-talpaṃ mūrtiman-moda-kalpaṃ
yad api tad api muñca svasti te ’smād udañca
translation: “You are the knower of time, the destroyer of all miseries, the friend to everyone and an ocean of good qualities. Even though this soft forest bed may seem like the embodiment of pleasure to You, still, for Your own good, You must rise and leave it.”

sanskrit:
mada-madhupa-yuvānaḥ prāpta-doṣāvasānaḥ
cyuta-kusuma-vanāntaḥ svāpam udyātavantaḥ
dadhati katipayathyāṃ kelim ambhoja-vīthyāṃ
sati samaya-viveke ke vimuhyanti loke?
translation: “Look! Within the flower-strewn forest, a group of drunken young bees have awakened and are now sporting in a cluster of lotuses. Who in the world would not be infatuated with such a pleasant time of day?”

sanskrit:
kvacana mukha-viṣādaḥ kvāpi hāsa-prasādaḥ
kva ca dayita-viyogaḥ kvāpi kāntasya yogaḥ
kumuda-kamala-vīthyor vaisadṛśye ’titathye
bhavati kim-u na kālaḥ kṣobha-śobhā-viśālaḥ
translation: “In one place, the white water-lilies’ faces are sad, while in another, the blue lotuses are smiling brightly. Somewhere, lovers are separating, and somewhere else, other lovers are meeting. Is it not time only that determines one’s happiness or distress in this circumstance?”

sanskrit:
jaya subhaga! namas te śrūyatāṃ satvaras te
cira-śayana-sapīḍaḥ kauty ayaṃ tāmra-cūḍaḥ
upanata-nija-sevā-kāla-sammoda-pīvā
nahi samaya-vidagdhaḥ kārya-kāle vimugdhaḥ
translation: “O fortunate one, may victory be Yours. I offer my obeisance. Now please listen to me. After seeing You asleep for so long, the red-crested cock became upset and is now loudly crying. When the appropriate time arrives for one’s personal sevā, a good servant is always joyful and prepared.”

sanskrit:
atha prabudhyaiva vidhūya pakṣān
grīvāḥ samunnīya cukūjur uccaiḥ
yat kukkuṭāḥ pañca-ṣa-vāram ādau
rādhā jajāgāra tadāpta-bādhā
translation: After awakening, the wild cocks shook their feathers five or six times, raised their necks and crowed loudly. Knowing that morning had come, Śrī Rādhā reluctantly rose from Her sleep.

sanskrit:
kṛṣṇāṇga-saṃśleṣa-viśeṣa-vādhinas
tān eva matveti śaśāpa sā ruṣā
are! paretāśu pareta-rāṭpuraṃ
tatraiva kiṃ kūjata no padāyudhāḥ?
translation: Feeling that Her pleasant embrace with Kṛṣṇa had been disturbed by all this noise, She angrily cursed the cocks. “Hey kukkuṭas! Why don’t you quickly drop dead and resume your crowing in Hell?”

sanskrit:
viśliṣya kiñcit priya-vakṣasaḥ sā
tūṣṇīṃ sthitāṃs tān upalabhya sadyaḥ
saṃśliṣya kāntaṃ dara-nidrayaiva
niṣevyamāṇā punar apy arājīt
translation: As Śrī Rādhā delivered Her curse to the cocks, Her body slightly separated from Her lover’s chest. For a while the cocks were silent and Śrīmatī thought they must have been overwhelmed and sent to hell. No longer alarmed about the coming of morning, She calmed down, once again embraced Kṛṣṇa and drifted into sleep.

sanskrit:
jālād atho dṛk-sapharī tad-ālayo
lāvaṇya-vanyā bhṛśam anvaśīlayan
krīṇanti yāḥ prāṇa-parārddha-koṭibhis
tayoḥ pramodottha-ruci-cchaṭā-kaṇam
translation: The minnow-like eyes of Lalitā and the other sakhīs, who would trade millions of their lives for even a particle of the joy shared by Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, began to sport in the flood of beauty and charm flowing through the lattice window of that cottage.

sanskrit:
ūce viśākhā kalayāli! kāntau
niraṃśukāv aṃśuka-puñja-mañjū
vihāriṇāv apy atihāriṇau svair
aṅgair anaṅgair alasau lasantau
translation: Viśākhā whispered to Lalitā, “Look, Sakhī! Even though the lovers are clothed only by Their own effulgence, They remain so captivating in Their languid embrace. And even though no necklaces adorn Their forms, They are beautifully decorated by the marks of Cupid.”

sanskrit:
anaṅgadau keli-vaśād anaṅgadau
nirañjanau hanta mitho nirañjanau
visrasta-rāgādharatābhilakṣitau
viprastarāgādharatābhilakṣitau
translation: “Even though They are an-aṅgada (without armlets), because of Their love-making They may be called anaṅga-da (increasing each other’s kāma). Even though They are nir-añjana (without ointment on Their eyes), They remain ni-rañjana (very pleasing to each other). Even though the affection for each other’s lips has diminished (visrasta-rāga-adharatā- abhilakṣitau), still, Their disheveled bed tells the story of a passionate battle of love (viprastara- agādha-rata-abhilakṣitau).”

sanskrit:
athāvabhāṣe lalitā ’vadhāryatāṃ
jayaḥ smarājau katarāśrito dvayoḥ
babhūva daṣṭādharayoḥ kaca-graha-
vyākṣipta-mūrdhnor nakhara-kṣatorasoḥ
translation: Lalitā said, “O Sakhīs, all of you decide: In last night’s love-combat, who was the victor? I can’t make any distinction because both Kṛṣṇa’s topknot and Rādhā’s braid loosened in the heat of battle and are now tangled together. Besides that, both of them have bite-marks on Their lips and nail-scratches on Their chests!”

sanskrit:
hṛdo ’nurāgaṃ kuca-kuṅkuma-cchalān-
nyadhatta rādhācyuta-pāda-padmayoḥ
yāvad ravārakta-tarālako dadhau
mūrdhnaiva so ’syāḥ padayos tam ujjvalam
translation: (Because during the night Rādhā had held Kṛṣṇa’s feet to Her breasts, His soles were marked with kuṅkuma; and because Kṛṣṇa had held Rādhā’s feet to His head, it was now reddened by lac.) Viśākhā said, “O Sakhī! Look at that! With the kuṅkuma from Her breasts, our Rādhā has deposited Her heart’s affection on Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet. And Kṛṣṇa is carrying His love for Rādhā’s lotus feet in the reddish lac smeared upon His head.”

sanskrit:
itthaṃ kṣaṇaṃ tāvad alakṣitāṅgyo
nīcaiḥ svaraṃ tāv anuvarṇayantyaḥ
bhāgyaṃ svam evātisabhājayantyo
mamajjur ānanda-mahodadhau tāḥ
translation: Remaining unseen, the sakhīs began to quietly discuss the wonder of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa’s vilāsa and celebrate their own good fortune. In this way they gradually sank deeper into the vast ocean of bliss.

sanskrit:
tataḥ punas tān atha ṭiṭṭibhādī-
nūtkūjataḥ prāha vidhūta-tandrā
haṃho! kṣamadhvaṃ śayituṃ kṣaṇaṃ me
datteti sā moṭayad aṅgam īṣat
translation: The wild cocks, partridges and other birds resumed their loud singing and once again awakened Rādhā. She stretched Her body and said to herself, “O birds, please forgive Me. Just let Me sleep a little while longer.”

sanskrit:
kādamba-kāraṇḍava-haṃsa-sārasāḥ
kapota-śārī-śuka-keki-kokilāḥ
jaguḥ kalaṃ kelivanī-jala-sthala-
pracāriṇaḥ kṛṣṇa-kathāmṛtopamam
translation: Then the geese, ducks, swans, herons and other aquatic birds living nearby joined with the doves, male and female parrots, peacocks, cuckoos and other land birds in a sweet harmony of warbling as pleasant as the nectar of kṛṣṇa-kathā.

sanskrit:
prabuddhya kāntau yugapad yathā rujaṃ
viśleṣajām ūhatur aṅga-moṭanāt
cāmpeya-nīlābja-dhanus tviṣau tathā
sāndropagūhena mudaṃ ca vakṣasoḥ
translation: Because of that, Yugala-kiśora awakened simultaneously and began stretching. Rādhā’s arched body looked just like a campaka flower bow, and Kṛṣṇa’s, a blue lotus bow. Even though They felt distressed at the separation of Their bodies, They regained Their joy by pressing Their chests together once again in tight embrace.

sanskrit:
athāsyā vayasyāḥ pramodāt smitāsyāḥ
sakhīṃ tāṃ hasantyo mithaḥ prerayantyaḥ
saśaṅkāḥ samantāt prabhātād durantāt
praviṣṭā nikuñjaṃ saśabdāli-puñjam
translation: Full of joy and bearing gentle, sweet smiles, the sakhīs urged each other to go into the kuñja first. Feeling timid because the dreaded morning had come, they finally entered along with the humming of the bees.

sanskrit:
abhilakṣya sakhīr vihasad- vadanāḥ
savidhopagatā vicalan-nayanāḥ
dayitāya mudaṃ dviguṇaṃ dadatī
dayitoruyugād udatiṣṭha-diyam
translation: Seeing Her sakhīs arrive with their smiling faces and restless eyes, Śrīmatī became even happier and rose from Kṛṣṇa’s lap to meet them.

sanskrit:
tvarotthitā sambhrama-saṃgṛhīta-
pītottarīyeṇa vapuḥ pidhāya
pārśve priyasyopaviveśa rādhā
salajjam āsāṃ mukham īkṣamāṇā
translation: She quickly covered Herself with Kṛṣṇa’s yellow cloth and sat beside Him, shyly looking toward the coming sakhīs.

sanskrit:
athānuraktāly anumodanāñcitā
mudā tayor aidhata rūpa-mañjarī
saiva svayaṃ keli-vilāsinor dvayos
tadātva-ramyāpacitau paṭīyasī
translation: Then, seeing that Their affectionate sakhīs were so joyful to see them, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa became even happier and the flower of Their beauty (rūpa-mañjarī) fully blossomed. That rūpa-mañjarī proved itself to be very expert in the art of yugala-sevā (because even though Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa had no clothing or ornaments, when the sakhīs saw Their extraordinary beauty they became ecstatic).

sanskrit:
pṛṣṭhopadhānaṃ nidadhe kayācana
pyadhād athānyā mṛdulāṃśukena tau
pīyūṣa-vaṭy-ārpitayāsyayoḥ parā
nirasya ghūrṇāṃ vikasad dṛśau vyadhāt
translation: One kiṅkarī leaned over the bed to place a pillow behind the young couple, while another covered Their bare bodies with a soft cloth. When another mañjarī placed in Their mouths a ball of soft, juicy nectar to remove Their drowsiness, Their eyes opened wide and all dizziness disappeared.

sanskrit:
kācit prasūnāmbu-darārdra-vāsasā
vyatyasta-rāgāñjana-yāvakādikam
mṛṣṭvā pratisvekṣaṇa-siddhaye tayor
mukha-dvayaṃ darpaṇatāṃ nināya kim
translation: Another kiṅkarī moistened a small piece of fine, soft cloth with rose water and cleaned the collyrium, lac and tāmbūla stains left here and there on Their bodies. They became so lustrous that They could use each other’s face as a mirror.

sanskrit:
tāmbūla-vīṭīr nidadhe parāsminn
ekā paṭimnā maṇi-dīpa-pālyā
tan-maṅgalārātrikam āśu cakre
nīrājayanty eva nijāsu-lakṣaiḥ
One kiṅkarī offered tāmbūla, while another performed maṅgala-ārātrika with a jeweled
translation: lamp, showing such care and love that it appeared she was giving her life a million times over to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit:
madhye ’cyutāṅga-ghana-kuṅkuma-paṅka-digdhaṃ
rādhāṅghri-yāvaka-vicitrita-pārśva-yugmam
sindūra-candana-kaṇāñjana-bindu-citraṃ
talpaṃ tayor diśati keli-viśeṣam ābhyaḥ
translation: In the center of the pleasure bed the sakhīs noticed some spots of kuṅkuma paste that had fallen from Kṛṣṇa’s body. On both sides of that they saw marks left by the lac from Rādhā’s lotus feet, and here and there around the bed were sprinkles of sindūra, candana powder and collyrium. In the eyes of the sakhīs, all this betrayed a very special type of love-making.

sanskrit:
pramliṣṭa-puṣpoccaya-sanniveśāṃ
tāmbūla-rāgāñjana-citritāṅgīm
vyaktībhavat-kānta-vilāsa-cihnāṃ
śayyām apaśyan svasakhīm ivālyaḥ
translation: They saw that the pleasure bed, like their dear sakhī Rādhā, was adorned with withered flowers, painted with tāmbūla stains and spots of collyrium, and marked by the caresses of an affectionate lover.

sanskrit:
kvacana ghusṛṇa-paṅkaḥ kvāpi sindūrajo ’ṅkaḥ
kṣata-viraha-vipakṣa-prasnutāsṛk-sapakṣaḥ
kvacana kusuma-dāma-cchinna-kodaṇḍa-dhāma
kva ca vilulita-hāraś chinna-maurvī-prakāraḥ
translation: Here and there on the bed were reddish spots of kuṅkuma and sindūra, making it appear as though drops of blood had fallen from the wounded enemy called viraha. Somewhere else a flower garland lay like a broken bow, and a crushed necklace like a severed bowstring.

sanskrit:
kvacana mṛgamadāṅkāḥ kutracit kajjalāṅkāḥ
smara-narapati-danti-ccheda-kalpāḥ sphuranti
sa hi ratiraṇa-raṅgaḥ kautukodyat-taraṅgaḥ
samajani sumukhīnām āgatānāṃ sakhīnām
translation: Spots of musk and kajjala, scattered by that mad elephant, the king of love-making, were seen in various places around the bed. Thus, this battlefield of pleasure presented quite a curiosity to the sakhīs gathered round.

sanskrit:
vakṣaḥ svaṃ darśayaṃs tābhyo
dṛg bhaṅgyovāca tā hariḥ
didṛkṣuḥ svapriyā-vaktra-
bhāva-śābalya-mādhurīm
vidhuṃ prayāsyantam avekṣya kāntaṃ
viśleṣa-bhītoṣasi paśyatālyaḥ
didṛkṣayevāmbara-citra-paṭyāṃ
rādhendulekhā-śatam ālilekha
translation: Hoping to see the sweetness of Rādhā’s bhāva-śābalya, with an eye gesture Kṛṣṇa directed the attention of the sakhīs to His chest and said, “O Sakhīs, just look! Seeing her lover, the moon, eager to leave her in the early morning, Rādhā, pained by viraha, has painted hundreds of moonbeams on the canvas of the sky.” (In other words, “Rādhā, seeing Me about to leave and feeling sick with viraha, has bestowed hundreds of nail-marks on My broad, sky-blue chest.”)

sanskrit:
iti nigadati kṛṣṇe vīkṣya sāgre vayasyāḥ
prahasita-vadanās tāḥ saṅkucal lola-netrā
vikasad amala-gaṇḍaṃ dolitārecita-bhrūḥ
priyam anṛju-kaṭākṣaiḥ paśyati sma ghnatīva
translation: When Rādhā heard Kṛṣṇa’s taunting remark and saw Her sakhīs laughing, Her restless eyes contracted in embarrassment and Her flawless cheeks began to tremble. Frowning, She hurled a piercing sidelong glance as if to impale Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit:
helollāsādara-mukulitā vāspa-sāndrāruṇāntā
lajjā-śaṅkā-capala-cakitā bhaṅgurerṣyābhareṇa
smera-smerā dayita-vadanālokanotphulla-tārā
rādhā-dṛṣṭir dayita-nayanānandam uccair vyatānīt
translation: Śrīmatī’s eyes were radiant with erotic feelings, slightly closed, full of tears and reddish with anger. They moved restlessly and appeared timid from Her fear of being embarrassed. Then She saw Kṛṣṇa’s lotus face and Her eyes began to widen as Her gentle smile reappeared. Seeing this, Kṛṣṇa’s eyes also blossomed with joy.

sanskrit:
itthaṃ mithaḥ prema-sukhābdhi-magnayoḥ
pragetanīṃ vibhrama-mādhurīṃ tayoḥ
nipīya sakhyaḥ pramadonmadās tadā
tadātva-yogyācaraṇaṃ visasmaruḥ
translation: In this way, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa were soon drowned in the ocean of love. The sakhīs, delirious with pure happiness from drinking the sweetness of these morning pastimes, had completely forgotten what they should be doing now (such as returning to their own homes).

sanskrit:
vilokya līlāmṛta-sindhu-magnau
tau tāḥ sakhīś ca praṇayonmadāndhāḥ
vṛndā prabhātodaya-jāta-śaṅkā
nijeṅgita-jñāṃ nidideśa sārīm
translation: Vṛndā saw that Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa were immersed within the ocean of līlāmṛta and the sakhīs had been blinded by the madness of prema. Considering that daybreak had arrived, she gestured an order to one of her sārikās (female parrots).

sanskrit:
guru-lajjā-bhartṛ-bhīti-
loka-hāsa-nivārikā
‘śubhākhyā’ sārikā prāha
rādhikā-bodha-sādhikā
translation: In order to bring Rādhā back to consciousness and prevent Her from alarming Her husband, being embarrassed before Her elders and laughed at by the villagers, the sārikā named Śubhā began to speak in a very clever way.

sanskrit:
āgantā grāhayitvā tava patir adhunā goṣṭhataḥ kṣīra-bhārān
uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha rādhe tad iha kuru gṛhe maṅgalāṃ vāstu-pūjāma
itthaṃ yāvad dhavāmbā tava nahi śayanād utthitā vāvadīti
tāvac chayyā-niketaṃ vraja sakhi nibhṛtaṃ kuñjataḥ kañja-netre!!
translation: “O lotus-eyed one! Your mother-in-law will soon rise from bed and say, ‘Śrī Rādhe! Your husband and the servants are on the way from the pasturing ground carrying their loads of milk. You must quickly get up and clean the house.’ O Sakhī! Before she can say these words, please leave this kuñja and secretly return to Your sleeping room.”

sanskrit:
śaṅkā-paṅkā-kalita-hṛdayā śaṅkate ’syā dhavāmbā
chidrānveṣī patir atikaṭuḥ sārthanāmābhimanyuḥ
ruṣṭābhīkṣṇaṃ parivadati sā hā nanandāpi mandā
prātar-jātaṃ tad api saralāṃ kṛṣṇa naināṃ jahāsi
translation: “O Kṛṣṇa! The heart of Rādhā’s mother-in-law is covered with the ointment of fear and therefore she is always suspicious. Rādhā’s husband Abhimanyu lives up to his name by always being angry, speaking harshly and continually finding fault. Her dull-headed sister- in-law is always grouchy and very critical. Why are You not leaving this simple-hearted girl even though the night has ended?”

sanskrit:
sārī-vaco-mandara-śaila-pāta-
saṃkṣubdha-hṛd-dugdha-payodhir eṣā
athodbhraman netra-navīna-mīnā
viyoga-dīnā śayanād udasthāt
translation: The sārī’s words were like Mandara Mountain falling into Rādhā’s milk-ocean heart. She became very agitated and Her eyes began to whirl like two young fish swimming about. Feeling great pain at the thought of leaving Kṛṣṇa, She finally rose from the bed.

sanskrit:
kṛṣṇo ’pi kāntaṃ vṛṣabhānu-jāyāḥ
paśyan mukhaṃ bhīti-vilola-netram
nīlaṃ sucīnaṃ dayitā-nicolaṃ
gṛhṇan svatalpāt tvarayodatiṣṭhat
Seeing Rādhā’s anxious, restless eyes and Her beautiful face, Kṛṣṇa picked up Śrīmatī’s
translation: fine blue scarf and also quickly rose from the bed.

sanskrit:
parivartita-saṃvyānau
mithas tāv atha śaṅkitau
paraspara-karālambau
niragātāṃ nikuñjataḥ
translation: Wearing each other’s cloth and feeling very fearful, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa held hands as They emerged from the kuñja.

sanskrit:
rādhā-pāṇiṃ savye ’savye
pāṇau bibhrad veṇuṃ kṛṣṇaḥ
reje kuñjān niryan yadvad
vidyun-mālāśliṣṭāmbhodaḥ
translation: As Kṛṣṇa left the kuñja, holding Śrīmatī’s hand in His left hand and His flute in His right, it appeared as though a beautiful raincloud was embracing a flash of lightning.

sanskrit:
haimaṃ bhṛṅgāram ekā vyajanam atha parā svarṇa-daṇḍaṃ dadhānā
kāpy ādarśaṃ sudarśaṃ ghusṛṇa-malayajā ’matram anyā vicitram
kācit tāmbūla-pātraṃ maṇi-citam aparā sārikāṃ pañjarasthām
itthaṃ sakhyaḥ kiyat yāḥ pramudita-hṛdayā niryayuḥ kuñja-gehāt
translation: Then, as the devoted sakhīs joyfully left the kuñja house, someone carried a golden pitcher, someone held a whisk with a golden handle, and someone else held a freshly cleaned mirror. One sakhī carried a multicolored container for kuṅkuma and candana, another carried a jewelled container for tāmbūla, and someone else held a caged sārikā.

sanskrit:
māhendra-kānta-cchadanaṃ sakāñcanaṃ
dāntaṃ sasindūra-samudgakaṃ parā
āpanna-satvā-kuca-kuṭmalopamaṃ
kuñjād gṛhītvā niragān mṛdu-smitā
translation: Another sakhī noticed by the bed an ivory sindūra box, inlaid with precious sapphires and gold. Seeing that the top part of the box resembled two budding breasts, she smiled softly and took it from the kuñja.

sanskrit:
āśleṣa-sañchinna-guṇāt paricyutaṃ
hārāl lasan-mauktika-sañcayaṃ mudā
vicitya kācit svapaṭāñcale dṛḍhaṃ
nibadhnatī kuñja-gṛhād viniryayau
translation: Because of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa’s firm embrace, Their pearl necklaces had broken and scattered about. One sakhī found them all, happily tied them tightly in the border of her own cloth and brought them out of the cottage.

sanskrit:
tāṭaṅkaṃ keli-vibhraṣṭaṃ
talpād ādāya satvarā
nirgatya sveśvarī-karṇe
yuyoja rati-mañjarī
translation: Rati Mañjarī found an earring that had fallen off during the couple’s love-making, so she picked it up from the bed, took it outside and placed it once again on her Prāṇeśvarī’s ear.

sanskrit:
talpa-prāntād upādāya
kañculīṃ rūpa-mañjarī
priyanarma-sakhī sakhyai
nirgatya nibhṛtaṃ dadau
translation: The priyanarma-sakhī named Rūpa Mañjarī took Rādhā’s bodice from the edge of the bed and secretly returned it to Her outside the kuñja.

sanskrit:
patadgrāham upādāya
dāsikā guṇa-mañjarī
tāmbūlaṃ carvitaṃ tābhyo
vibhajantī bahir yayau
translation: The dāsī named Guṇa Mañjarī took the spittoon from the cottage, removed the tāmbūla that Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa had chewed and shared it among all the other sakhīs.

sanskrit:
mañjulālī tayor aṅgāc
Vermilion
cyuta-mālyānulepanam
talpād ādāya sarvābhyaḥ
prayacchantī vinirgatā
translation: Mañjulālī Mañjarī collected the garlands and candana that had fallen from Rādhā- Kṛṣṇa’s bodies and distributed them to everyone.

sanskrit:
vilokyāgre meghāmbara-vṛta-śarīraṃ priyatamaṃ
vayasyāṃ tāṃ pītāmbara-parivṛtāṅgīṃ pramuditām
hasantyas tāḥ sakhyaḥ kara-pihita-mukhyaḥ pratidiśaṃ
diśantyaś cānyonyaṃ kuṭila-cala-dṛgbhir mumudire
translation: When the sakhīs noticed that Kṛṣṇa was wearing Rādhā’s blue cloth and Rādhā was wearing Kṛṣṇa’s yellow cloth, they had to cover their mouths with their hands to conceal the laughter. They had great fun using subtle eye gestures to point out to each other that the exchange had occurred.

sanskrit:
samīkṣya tāsāṃ parihāsa-bhaṅgīm
anyonya-vaktrārpita-phulla-netrau
samucchalat-prema-sukhābdhi-magnau
citrārpitāṅgāv iva tāv abhūtām
translation: Seeing the sakhīs trying to hide their laughter, Yugala-kiśora emerged from Their ocean of love and gazed with wide eyes at each other’s face, standing motionless as though figures in a painting.

sanskrit:
ghanaśyāmaṃ cīnaṃ vasanam abhilīnaṃ priya-tanau
kṣamā nāsīt kāntā svam api paricetuṃ ghana-rucau
svam ajñāsīt sphītaṃ harir api na pītaṃ priyatamā-
tanau līnaṃ cīnaṃ kanaka-ruci kambāv iva payaḥ
translation: Just as it is difficult to immediately distinguish milk within a white conchshell, in the same way, it was almost impossible to see Rādhā’s fine blue cloth on Kṛṣṇa’s dark body, or Kṛṣṇa’s yellow cloth on Rādhā’s golden form.

sanskrit:
tayor līlā-sudhā-pāna-
pratyūhāmarṣa-saṅkulā
nindanty aruṇam udyantam
athāha lalitā sakhīm
translation: Considering the rising sun to be an impediment to their drinking līlāmṛta, Lalitā began to angrily criticize it, speaking to her sakhī Rādhā.

sanskrit:
ūṣasi vara-vadhūnāṃ paśya rādhe ’ruṇo ’yaṃ
ramaṇa-sahita-līlā-bhaṅgataḥ pāpa-rugbhiḥ
galita-pada-yugo ’py adyāpi tan no jahāti
dhruvam iti vacanaṃ yad-dustyajaḥ sva-svabhāvaḥ
translation: “Rādhe! Just look. This early morning sun is interfering with the intimate pastimes of beautiful women with their lover. Even if he got leprosy because of his crime and both of his feet melted off, still he wouldn’t be able to give up his bad habit. Therefore, when the ṛṣis say, ‘It is very difficult to give up one’s nature,’ it is certainly true.”

sanskrit:
aruṇāruṇe nidadhatī tato ’mbare
rati-keli-bhaṅgaja-ruṣā ’ruṇāṃ dṛśam
lalitopahāsa-janita-smitānanā
vṛṣabhānujāha mṛdu-mañjubhāṣiṇī
anūrur apy astamayan kṣaṇārddhān
nabho vilaṅghyodayam eti so ’yam
cet sorum enaṃ sa vidhir vyadhāsyad
vārttāpi rātrer na tadābhaviṣyat
translation: After hearing the taunting words of Lalitā, Vārṣabhānavī47 Śrī Rādhā smiled sweetly and began to speak in a soft, slow voice. Her eyes reddened with anger from having Her rati-keli disturbed, She looked up toward the crimson morning sky and said, “The sun, even though having no thighs, sets below the horizon and travels across the sky. But within half a moment it is once again time for him to rise at dawn. Perhaps if Lord Brahmā had created thighs for him, we wouldn’t have ever even heard of the night.”

sanskrit:
manoramāṃ vīkṣya vibhāta-lakṣmīṃ
nipīya tasyā vacanāsavaṃ ca
mudonmanā vismṛta-goṣṭha-yānaḥ
prāṇeśvarīṃ tām avadan mukundaḥ
inaṃ prabhātopagataṃ samīkṣya
kānteva kāntāntara-bhukta-kāntam
paśyānya-dik-saṅga-kaṣāyitāṅgaṃ
prācīyam īrṣyāruṇiteva jātā
translation: Beholding the splendor of the early morning and delirious with joy from drinking the nectar of Rādhā’s words, Śrī Kṛṣṇa forgot about going to the pasturing grounds. He said to His prāṇeśvarī, “Look Priyā! Just as a young girl becomes red with jealousy when her boyfriend arrives in the morning bearing love-marks from another girl, in the same way, the eastern sky reddens in jealousy when she sees her husband Sūrya arrive at dawn colored by the touch of the other directions.”

sanskrit:
paśyonmatte dvijeśo ’py akhila-jana-tama-stoma-hantāpi śāntaḥ
The daughter of Vṛṣabhānu
kānto ’yaṃ te samantāt sapadi nipatito vāruṇīṃ saṃniṣevya
itthaṃ svīyena-saṅga-pramudita-nalinī-hāsa-sañjāta-lajjā
śaṅke vaktraṃ pidhatte hy uṣasi kumudinī saṅkucadbhir dalaiḥ svaiḥ
translation: “And there, the lotus says to the white lily, ‘O Kumudinī, look! Your lover the moon, chief of the twice-born, destroys the darkness of the whole world and is very peaceful. But because he has become so fond of Vāruṇī, the western sky, he has now quickly fallen from his position.’ Hearing the joking words of the lotus, who is now joyful in the company of her lover the sun, the white lily has hidden her face in shame within her own withered petals.”

sanskrit:
dṛṣṭvā tamaḥ-kṣayam amī vidhunānyapuṣṭā
naktaṃ tamaś-caya-nibhāś cakitāḥ prabhāte
mitraṃ tad-āśrayatayā tamasā carantīṃ
grastaṃ kuhūr iti kuhūṃ svagirāhvayanti
translation: “When the black kokilas see that the darkness of night is destroyed by the light of the moon, they think that, like the darkness, they will also be destroyed. Fearful, they call out to the new moon with a sound of ‘kuhū, kuhū.’ The reason for this is that at the time of the new moon, both the sun and moon are together in the same place. If Rāhu appeared and swallowed them both, then neither the darkness nor the kokilas would have any reason to worry.”

sanskrit:
vasanta-kānta-saṃsarga-
jātānanda-bharāṭavī
kapotī-ghūtkṛti-miṣāt
śītkarotīva sonmadā
translation: “Just as a girl sometimes emits a breathy sound while making love with her paramour, in the same way this forest, in union with her lover the springtime and maddened with pleasure, utters the same sound disguised as the cooing of doves.”

sanskrit:
paśyānusarati cañcala-bhṛṅgaḥ
kairaviṇī-kula-keli-piśaṅgaḥ
nalinī-koṣe niśi kṛta-saṅgāṃ
bhṛṅgīṃ śaśimukhi! kṛta-natibhaṅgām
translation: “O Moonface, look! A restless yellow bumblebee now leaves the cluster of white waterlilies he has been sporting with and begins to follow his mate, who has been confined within a lotus flower all night and who makes him lose all modesty.”

sanskrit:
kāntam āyāntam āśaṅkyā-
ruṇāṃśu-dviguṇāruṇam
kokī koka-nadaṃ cañcvā
cumbaty ānanda-vihvalā
translation: “Waiting eagerly for the arrival of her husband, a female heron becomes so overwhelmed with joy that she kisses a red lotus, whose color has been deepened by the rays of the sun.”

sanskrit:
kalasvanākhyaḥ kalakaṇṭhi! haṃsaḥ
samīkṣya nau sammada-phulla-pakṣaḥ
riraṃsum apy eṣa visṛjya haṃsīṃ
taṭaṃ taṭinyāḥ purataḥ sameti
translation: “O Kalakaṇṭhī! Seeing us, that sweet-voiced swan has left his mate even though she longs for his companionship. Now he has come to the bank of the Yamunā and is spreading his wings wide in ecstasy.”

sanskrit:
svasahacara-visṛṣṭaṃ svāmibhuktaṃ mṛṇālaṃ
madakala-kalakaṇṭhī vibhratī paśya cañcvā
ramaṇam anu sameti tvan mukhābjārpitākṣī
sarasija-mukhi nāmnā ‘tuṇḍikerī’ marālī
translation: “Look, Padma-mukhī! The goose named Tuṇḍikerī is holding within her beaks the half-eaten lotus stalks given by her husband. With her eyes fixed upon Your lotus face, she now approaches with her mate, uttering a low, sweet warbling sound.”

sanskrit:
malaya-śikhara-cārī paṅkajāmoda-dhārī
vratati-naṭa-kumārī-lāsya-śikṣādhikārī
vahati jala-vihārī vāyur āyāsa-dārī
sa ramaṇa-vara-nārī-sveda-jālāpahārī
translation: “The cooling breeze drifting down from the peaks of the Malaya hills carries the sweet fragrance of the lotus flowers as he dallies with the waters of the Yamunā. He also teaches the creepers how to dance, removes everyone’s fatigue and dries the perspiration of the lovers.”

sanskrit:
itīśayoḥ sumadhura-vāg vilāsayoḥ
One who has a very charming voice
Lotus face
samīkṣya tāṃ svabhavana-yāna-vismṛtam
sakhīś ca tāḥ smita-rucirā mudonmadā
vaneśvarī divasa-bhiyāsa sonmanāḥ
translation: In this way, seeing Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa engaged in sweet conversation and forgetting to go to Their respective homes, and seeing the sakhīs adorned with gentle smiles and overwhelmed with joy, Vṛndādevī became very anxious about the coming daylight.

sanskrit:
kāntā udīyur vikasan mukhendavo
rātrir gatā cāstam apāsta-candrikā
vilāsa-bhaṅgaḥ katham astu nāstu vā
kṣaṇaṃ hṛdaiveti parāmamarśa sā
translation: Vṛndā began to consider whether vilāsa had actually ended or not, since the bright moon-faced Rādhā and Her starlike sakhīs remained, but the dark night had gone.

sanskrit:
tamāṃsya naśyann abhito yathā yathā
tadā prakāśaś ca yathā yathaidhata
tathā tathā hṛd-rujam eva sānvabhūd
vrajasya rītiṃ śrutayo ’pi no viduḥ
translation: All the śāstras say that the amount of light (wisdom) one has is directly proportional to the amount of darkness (ignorance) destroyed. And the more wisdom one has, the more sorrow and grief are driven away. But in Vṛndā’s case, the opposite has happened. (The more the darkness disappears, the more the sunlight appears. The lighter the day becomes, the more anxious Vṛndā becomes about Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa’s impending separation.) This is not so astonishing though, because this natural characteristic of Vraja is unknown to even the śrutis.

sanskrit:
atha vṛndeṅgitābhijñā
samaya-jñā taru-sthitā
padyam udyotayāmāsa
kakkhaṭī vṛddha-markaṭī
translation: Realizing what time it was, and understanding a signal from Vṛndā, the old monkey named Kakkhaṭī began to recite poetry as she sat above everyone on the branch of a tree.

sanskrit:
raktāmbarā satāṃ vandyā
prātaḥ-sandhyā tapasvinī
ūrdhva-prasarpad arkāṃśur
jaṭileyam upasthitā
translation: Since the moon(-faced Rādhā) still shone brightly, surely the nightly pastimes were still happening. But, on the other hand, the night had obviously come to an end, so how could vilāsa still be going on? Hmm. “An ascetic who is worshipped by the morning prayers of the virtuous has now arrived. She wears reddish clothing and has matted hair (jaṭilā) that appears like rays of light emanating from her head.”

sanskrit:
ākarṇya tābhir jaṭileti varṇa-
trayīṃ vivarṇatvam adhāri sadyaḥ
vilāsa-ratnākaram udbhavantī
śaṅkaiva tāsāṃ culukī-cakāra
translation: Upon hearing the three syllables ja-ṭi-lā, Śrī Rādhikā and the other vraja-gopīs became pale and overcome with terrible fear. The ocean of vilāsa they had been happily sporting in was immediately swallowed up by their anxiety.

sanskrit:
pathi piśuna-matibhyaḥ śaṅkamānau gurubhyaḥ
cala-cakita-taraṅgau nikṣipantāv apāṅgau
parama-guṇa-gabhīrau kāma-saṃgrāma-dhīrau
yayatū rati-vitandrau rādhikā-kṛṣṇacandrau
translation: Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, valiant but tired warriors in Cupid’s battle, were very solemn as They walked carefully on the path. Fearful of Their slanderous elders, They cast restless, timid glances here and there from the corners of Their eyes.

sanskrit:
na pathi na bhavane vā lakṣitau tau vane vā
sahaja-sad-anuraktyā svīyayānanda-śaktyā
parijana-nayanānām utsavānādadhānāv
atha pathi viharantau rejatur loka-kāntau
translation: No one saw Them in the forest, on the path or at Their homes. Because of the naturally affectionate quality of the hlādinī-śakti, They had both become the delight of everyone’s eyes. Therefore, even the dangerous walk home was an enjoyable adventure for Them.

sanskrit:
bhraśyad dukūla-cikura-srajam unnayantau
bhītau pṛthag gahana-vartmani cāpayāntau
tau vīkṣya bhīti-taralau jaṭileti nāmnā
sakhyas tatas tata itaś cakitā nirīyuḥ
translation: Hearing the name of Jaṭilā, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa stole away in fear upon separate forest paths, holding up Their loosened clothing, hair and garlands. Alarmed by seeing this, the sakhīs also fled in every direction.

sanskrit:
vāme candrāvali-parijanān ghoṣa-vṛddhān purastāt
kṛṣṇaḥ paścāt kuṭila-jaṭilām āgatāṃ manyamānaḥ
yāntīṃ kāntāṃ sabhaya-caṭulāṃ dakṣiṇe draṣṭum utkaś
cañcad-grīvaṃ diśi diśi dṛśau prerayan goṣṭham āyāt
translation: To Kṛṣṇa’s left were Candrāvalī and her sakhīs, and in front of Him, the elderly people of the cowherd village. He feared that the deceitful Jaṭilā may sneak up on Him from behind. Craning His neck in eagerness, He looked here and there on His right side, trying to see His anxious lover as She left for home. In this way, Kṛṣṇa carefully made His way toward the pasturing grounds.

sanskrit:
mlānām utkṣipya mālāṃ truṭita-maṇisaraḥ kajjalaṃ vibhrad oṣṭhe
saṃkīrṇāṅgo nakhāṅkair diśi diśi vikiran ghūrṇite netra-padme
paśya mlānāṅga-yaṣṭiḥ sphuṭam aparicito gopa-goṣṭhībhir agre
goṣṭhe goṣṭhendra-sūnuḥ praviśati rajanau dhvaṃsam āsādayantyām
Seeing Kṛṣṇa’s movement, one sakhī said to another, “Look, Vrajendra-nandana returns
translation: to His home before the Vrajavāsīs awaken at daybreak. Though He has thrown away His vaijayantī-mālā, withered and crushed from being pressed against Rādhā’s firm breasts, He holds it yet within His heart. During Cupid’s battle, His jewelled necklace was broken to pieces, His lips became smeared with the kajjala from Śrīmatī’s eyes, and His body was covered with the marks from Her fingernails. Afraid of being seen, He sends His tired eyes in every direction and then, unnoticed, sneaks quickly into His house.”

sanskrit:
anugatā jaṭilety abhiśaṅkinī
guru-nitamba-kucodvahanākulā
druta-vilambita-valgu yayau vrajaṃ
kara-dhṛtāmbara-keśacayeśvarī
translation: Śrī Rādhā was also afraid that Jaṭilā may be approaching from behind. Burdened by Her heavy breasts and hips, and holding up Her loosened dress and locks of hair, She walked with a fluid, slow and graceful movement on the path toward Vraja.

sanskrit:
na vyālād api sambibheti purataḥ sthāṇor yathā dūrato
nodvignā kari-garjitād api yathā kākāvalī-nisvanāt
naiveyaṃ timire ’pi muhyati-tarāṃ kāmaṃ prakāśe yathā
tan manye virahe ’pi naiva vidhurā kāntasya yoge yathā
translation: Seeing a venomous snake before Her didn’t cause as much fear as seeing a branchless tree trunk in the distance. Hearing the roaring of an elephant caused Her less concern than hearing the cawing of crows, and the dense darkness didn’t bewilder Her as much as the bright daylight. Therefore it seemed that today Rādhā had been more troubled by being with Kṛṣṇa than being without Him.

sanskrit:
Garland of forest flowers
Collyrium, eye ointment
bhayānurāgoccaya-dhūmra-lola-dṛk-
tiras-kariṇyā pihite manorathe
nije niveśyaiva hi rūpa-mañjarī
gṛhaṃ ninīṣuḥ pathi tāṃ tad anvayāt
Wanting to help Rādhā get home safely, Rūpa Mañjarī, feeling both fear and affection,
translation: placed Śrīmatī within the chariot of her own heart to protect Her. Walking closely behind Her on the path, Rūpa concealed Her with the curtain of her smoke-colored eyes.

sanskrit:
itas-tataḥ kṣipta-calekṣaṇāśugair
bhī-dustha-hṛd-vṛtti-cayair bhaṭair iva
agresarais tāṃ rati-mañjarī ca sā
nivārayanty anya-janāṃs tadānvayāt
translation: Like a soldier walking in front of his king, shooting arrows all around to ward off the enemies ahead, Rati Mañjarī, worried that some unfriendly people might come and see Rādhā, walked along with Her, casting restless glances here and there.

sanskrit:
tābhir vṛtā vraja-janair avilokitaiva
veśma praviśya nija-talpam athādhyatiṣṭhat
preyo-viyoga-vidhurā hi sakhīm athāsau
hṛd-vedanāṃ prakaṭam āha sagadgadāśru
translation: In this way, surrounded by Her sakhīs, the affectionate Rādhā entered Her home and lay down in bed, unseen by any of the Vrajavāsīs. Aggrieved in separation from Kṛṣṇa, Her voice choked with emotion and eyes full of tears, Śrīmatī revealed the pain in Her heart to Lalitā Sakhī.

sanskrit:
niḥsārya gehāl lalite ’dhunaiva māṃ
praveśayasy apy adhunaiva tat punaḥ
kṛṣṇāṅga-saṅgāmṛta-sindhu-majjana-
pralobhanaivādya vṛthā kṛtā tvayā
translation: “Lalitā! You led Me to believe that when I met with Kṛṣṇa I would be drowned in the ambrosial ocean of His loving embrace. By this allurement you led Me from My home and then immediately brought Me back. What sin have I committed that has kept Me from this sea of nectar?”

sanskrit:
astācalaṃ yann adhunā vyaloki yaḥ
sa tigma-raśmiḥ sakhi! pūrva-parvatam
translation: Rūpa cautiously watches both sides of the path as they walk along. āroḍhum ākāṅkṣati kiṃ vibhāvarī kha-puṣpatām adyatanī jagāma kim? “O Sakhī! We just watched the sun setting in the western sky and now it’s already about to rise above the eastern mountains. Has the nighttime become imaginary like a flower growing in the sky?”

sanskrit:
dhiṅ me śrutiṃ dhig rasanāṃ dṛśaṃ ca dhik
sadātanautkaṇṭhya-bhara-jvarāturam
prāpur na pātuṃ lavam apy amuṣya yāḥ
sausvarya-saurasya-surūpatāmṛtam
translation: “Sakhī! My ears, tongue and eyes have been afflicted by the intense fever of constant longing. But fie upon them a hundred times over, for today they don’t allow Me to drink even a drop of the nectar of Śyāmasundara’s sweet voice, sweet lips or sweet form.”

sanskrit:
nirveda-paddhatim apīpaṭhad eva pūrvaṃ
yogo ’dhunā tu sarale bhavatīṃ viyogaḥ
ādyo ’cyutāmṛtam adarśayad artham asyā
anyo ’nubhāvayati hā kaṭu-kālakūṭam
translation: Lalitā replied, “Rādhā! Last night, Your union with Kṛṣṇa caused You to study the nirveda- paddhati. Now, in separation from Him, You recite it again by cursing Yourself. Being with Acyuta caused You to taste the sweetness of His words, lips and form, but Your separation now tortures You like a deadly poison.”

sanskrit:
itthaṃ sakhī-giram api pratiboddhum eṣā
naivānurāga-para-bhāgavatī śaśāka
svapne punaḥ kalayituṃ hṛdayādhināthaṃ
suṣvāpa sā ’tha śayane vṛṣabhānu-putrī
translation: Overwhelmed by love, Vārṣabhānavī Śrī Rādhā was not able to understand Lalitā’s words. Hoping to see the lord of Her heart again in Her dreams, Śrīmatī lay down in bed and fell asleep.

sanskrit:
srastaṃ srastam udañcayaty adhiśiraḥ śyāmaṃ nicolāñcalaṃ
hastena ślatha-durbalena lulitākalpāṃ vahantī tanum
muktārdhām avarudhya veṇim alasa-syande kṣipantī dṛśau
kuñjāt paśya gṛhaṃ praviśya nibhṛtaṃ śete sakhī rādhikā
translation: One gopī who wasn’t part of the night’s lovers’ tryst said to another, “Look Sakhī! Rādhā Because this paddhati (guide book or manual) transgresses the codes of dharma, it is called nirveda, or outside of the Vedas. has returned from the nikuñja and is secretly entering Her home to go to bed. Her blue scarf keeps slipping from Her head and She wearily tries to replace it again and again. Her clothes and ornaments are all disheveled due to Cupid’s sporting, and as She looks all around with tired eyes, She weakly tries to retie Her loosened braid.”

sanskrit:
nirvartya vibhrama-bharaṃ samaye svadhāmni
supte ’cyute pratilayaṃ śrutayo yatheśam
līlā-vitāna-nipuṇāḥ saguṇāḥ samīyuḥ
sakhyo ’palakṣya-gatayaḥ sadanaṃ yathā-svam
translation: During each yuga, the Ādi-puruṣa performs His līlā of creating, maintaining and destroying the universes. Then He enters into His own abode and lies down upon Ananta- śeṣa. At that time, the personified śrutis, who are very expert in helping to expand the Lord’s līlā, enter unseen into His transcendental body. In the same way, after performing His nikuñja-vilāsa, Śrī Kṛṣṇa returned to His own home in the early morning and lay down in bed. Then the sakhīs, whose beauty, wit and amorous gestures continually enrich vraja-līlā, also entered secretly into their respective homes.

sanskrit:
rādhāṃ snāta-vibhūṣitāṃ vraja-payāhūtāṃ sakhībhiḥ prage
tad-gehe vihitānnapāka-racanāṃ kṛṣṇāvaśeṣāśanām
kṛṣṇaṃ buddham avāpta-dhenu-sadanaṃ nirvyūḍha-godohanaṃ
susnātaṃ kṛta-bhojanaṃ sahacarais tāṃ cātha taṃ cāśraye
translation: I offer my most humble obeisances unto the lotus feet of Śrī Rādhikā. After being bathed and decorated in the early morning, She and Her sakhīs are called by Mother Yaśodā to cook for Kṛṣṇa, and afterwards, they all eat the food remnants left by Him. I also offer my sincere prayers unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who awakens in the morning and goes to the cow shed to milk the cows, then returns, bathes and eats breakfast along with His dear friends.

sanskrit:
snātānulipta-vapuṣaḥ pupuṣuḥ svabhās tan
nirmālya-mālya-vasanābharaṇena dāsyaḥ
prāsya svakāmam anuvṛtti-ratās tayor yāḥ
śrī-rūpa-mañjari-samāna-guṇābhidhānāḥ
translation: After Śrī Rādhā arrived home and fell asleep, Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī and the other kiṅkarīs bathed and smeared their bodies with candana and ointments. Then, to make themselves even more beautiful, they donned Śrīmatī’s prasādī garlands, clothing and ornaments. All of these maidservants, equal in splendor, charming qualities and good name, have long ago given up all personal desires in order to devote themselves to the loving service of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit:
vaidagdhya eva kila mūrti-bhṛtas tathāpi
yūtheśvarītvam api samyag arocayitvā
dāsyāmṛtābdhim anu sasnur ajasram asyāḥ
translation: Even a single ray of effulgence from the tips of their toes is more brilliant than a bolt of lightning. They are the embodiment of cleverness, and even though each is worthy to be a yūtheśvarī, they are disinterested and would rather continuously bathe in the nectarous ocean of service to Śrī Rādhā.

ref: K ṛ ṣ ṇ a - bhāvanāmṛtam 3.3
sanskrit:
Food remnants
Maidservants
Group leader
śvaśrū-purāntara-gatottara pārśva-varti
bhrājiṣṇu dhāma vara-śilpa-kalaika-dhāma
tātena vatsalatayā vṛṣabhānunaiva
nirmāpitaṃ tad upamāpi tad eva nānyat
translation: Out of affection for his daughter Śrī Rādhā, Vṛṣabhānu Mahārāja had a beautiful palace constructed for Her residence. Sitting on the northern side of Jaṭilā’s home, this mansion is incomparably radiant and exquisitely decorated with artistic ornaments.
_raw_title: K ṛ ṣ ṇ a - bhāvanāmṛtam

sanskrit:
sthūṇā-praghāṇa paṭalāṅgaṇa-toraṇālī-
gopānasī-vividha-koṣṭha-kapāṭa-vedyaḥ
rājanti yatra maṇi-dīpa-tati-pradīpta-
vaicitrya-nirmita-janekṣaṇa-citra-bhāvāḥ
translation: Within that magnificent palace are ornate columns, verandas, roofs with curved support beams, courtyards, various kinds of rooms, doors and sitting platforms. When anyone sees this amazing building, its features illuminated by rows of jeweled lamps, their eyes are bathed in wonder.

sanskrit:
yatrendranīla-maṇi-bhūr-valabhī ghanābhā
haṃsālir apy upari rājati rājatī sā
ye vīkṣya bandhu-ripu-bhāna-bhṛto vitatya
saṅkocayanti śikhinaḥ svaśikhaṇḍa-paṅktīḥ
Atop Śrī Rādhā’s mansion sits a cloud-like sapphire turret crowned with a flock of radiant
translation: silver swans. When the peacocks see this bluish turret they surmise it is their friend the rain cloud, so they spread their tail feathers wide in welcome. But when they see the silver swans upon the turret they take them as their enemies and quickly withdraw their opened plumage.

sanskrit:
tatropaveśa-śayanāśana-bhūṣaṇādi-
vedīr vimṛjya parilipya viśodhya tās tāḥ
āstīrya rāṅkavam upary upayukta-muktam
ullocam unnata-mudo militā babandhuḥ
translation: Here and there around the palace are raised platforms for sleeping, eating, sitting, etc. Rādhā’s kiṅkarīs carefully cleansed them with water and then smeared candana and other fragrant ointments upon them. When the platforms were dry, the mañjarīs spread soft deerskins upon them and joyfully tied pearl-inlaid canopies above each.

sanskrit:
ekā mamārja maṇi-kāñcana-bhājanāni
Various services offered to Her
kācit payaḥ samaya-yogyam upānināya
citrāṃśukāpihita-ratna-catuṣkikāyām
ālambanīyam adadhād aparopabarham
One kiṅkarī polished a golden, gem-inlaid pot, while another brought water appropriate for
translation: the season (cool in summer and warm in winter). Another dāsī placed fluffy pillows upon a jeweled seat covered with colorful cloth.

sanskrit:
pūrvedyur aṃśuka-maṇimaya-bhūṣaṇāni
mṛṣṭāni yatra nihitāny atha sampuṭaṃ tat
uccair jhanad-valaya-rāji samudghaṭayya
kācij jagharṣa vidhu-kuṅkuma-candanāni
translation: The previous day, one mañjarī had cleaned and placed within a chest Rādhā’s fine dress and ornaments. Now, with bangles jingling, she opened the chest for a look and then began to grind camphor, kuṅkuma and sandalwood.

sanskrit:
anyā vyadhatta sumanāḥ sumanobhir eva
citraiḥ kirīṭa-kaṭakāṅgada-hāra-kāñcīḥ
jātī-lavaṅga-khadirādibhi rajyamānāḥ
kācid babandha surasāḥ phaṇivallī-vīṭīḥ
Another pure-hearted kiṅkarī fashioned a crown, bangles, necklaces and a sash out of
fresh, multicolored flowers. Someone else lovingly prepared tāmbūla (pāna) from nutmeg,
cloves, catechu and other savory substances. (Kṛṣṇa-bhāvanāmṛtam 3.9)
Description of Morning, Mukharā’s Entrance into Rādhā’s Bedroom, etc.
translation: anyā vyadhatta sumanāḥ sumanobhir eva citraiḥ kirīṭa-kaṭakāṅgada-hāra-kāñcīḥ jātī-lavaṅga-khadirādibhi rajyamānāḥ kācid babandha surasāḥ phaṇivallī-vīṭīḥ Another pure-hearted kiṅkarī fashioned a crown, bangles, necklaces and a sash out of fresh, multicolored flowers. Someone else lovingly prepared tāmbūla (pāna) from nutmeg, cloves, catechu and other savory substances.

sanskrit:
atrāntare pratidiśaṃ dadhi-manthanottha-
rāvair avārita-mahīsura-veda-ghoṣaiḥ
hambā-dhvani-vyatividhāna-mitho ’vadhāyi-
dhenvāli-tarṇaka-ghaṭā valad antarāyaiḥ
translation: Throughout the village, the sounds of people churning milk began to rise, while the local brāhmaṇas chanted Vedic mantras. Their loud chanting interfered with the cows who were calling for their calves, so in competition, both the brāhmaṇas and the cows gradually got louder and louder.

sanskrit:
vṛndiṣṭha-vandi-jana-vṛnda-vitāyamāna-
śrī-kṛṣṇa-kīrti-virudāli-sudhā-taraṅgaiḥ
śārī-śuka-vraja-kalaiḥ kalaviṅka-keki-
kolāhalaiḥ kramata eva samedhamānaiḥ
translation: The best of the vandīs spread waves of ambrosia by singing the glories of Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes, and the sweet warbling of the śukas, śārīs, sparrows, peacocks and other birds One who sings in praise gradually became a tumult of noise.

sanskrit:
jāgratsu loka-nicayeṣv atha vāsareti
kartavya-bhāvana-pareṣv adhiśayam eva
kṛṣṇekṣaṇa-kṣaṇa satṛṣṇatayā purandhrī-
vṛndeṣu nanda-gṛha-sandita-mānaseṣu
translation: As all the Vrajavāsīs began to awaken, they sat upon their beds and planned their day. Even the married women could think of nothing but going to Nanda Mahārāja’s house for a glimpse of Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit:
naptrī-mukhāmbuja-vilokana-jīvitāyāṃ
tatropasṛtya sahasā mukharābhidhāyām
vātsalya-ratna-paṭalī-bhṛta-peṭikāyāṃ
rādhe! kva putri! bhavasīti samāhvayantyām
translation: At this time, Rādhā’s grandmother Mukharā, who is like a treasure chest full of the precious jewels of motherly affection, arrived at Śrīmatī’s home. Seeing Rādhikā’s beautiful face is the elixir that sustains her life. Coming inside, she began to call out, “Rādhā! My daughter! Where are You?”

sanskrit:
svabhāva-kuṭilāpy ātma-
suta-sampatti-kāṅkṣayā
vyākulā jaṭilā gatvā
nikaṭaṃ tām athābravīt
sūnoḥ prajāyur dhana-vṛddhaye ’sau
tvayā snuṣā jñe! niyataṃ niyojyā
sumaṅgala-snāna-vibhūṣaṇādau
go-koṭi-hetos tapanārcanāya
ājñānavajñā nija-goṣṭha-rājñyāḥ
kāryānabhijñoktiṣu te ’py avajñā
ity ādiśaty anvaham artha-vijñā
vijñāpitā me kila paurṇamāsī
asmāt tvam ārye svāṃ naptrīṃ
sarva-maṅgala-maṇḍitām
vidhehi sarva-sampattir
yathā sūnor bhaven mama
translation: Even though Jaṭilā is by nature very deceitful, in hopes of increasing her own son’s wealth, she said to Mukharā, “Every day, the all-knowing Paurṇamāsī tells me, ‘O wise one, to increase your son’s offspring, lifespan and riches, and to help Him acquire countless numbers of cows, please have your daughter-in-law take Her auspicious bath and decorate Herself with ornaments so She may perform sūrya-pūjā. Never neglect the order of goṣṭheśvarī Śrī Yaśodā, but don’t bother listening to the words of the ignorant.’ Therefore, O honorable Mukharā, to help my son become wealthy in every way, please adorn your granddaughter with all blessings of good fortune.”

sanskrit:
vadhūm athābhāṣasata putri! talpād
uttiṣṭha tūrṇaṃ kuru vāstu-pūjām
tvaṃ maṅgala-snāna-vidhiṃ vidhāya
pūjopahāraṃ savitur vidhehi
translation: Jaṭilā addressed her daughter-in-law (Rādhā), “O daughter! Please rise from bed now and quickly clean the house. Then take Your bath and prepare the ingredients for sūrya-pūjā.”

sanskrit:
prabhātam āyātam aho tathāpi
nidrāti naptrīti muhur vadantī
sneha-drutāṅgī mukharā praviśya
śayyālayaṃ tām avadat tadedam
uttiṣṭha vatse śayanāt pramugdhe
vyasmāri vāro ’dya raves tvayā kim?
snātvā prabhātārghya-vidhānam asmai
pūjopahāraṃ racayāsya cāśu
translation: Mukharā exclaimed over and over, “How astonishing! Morning has come and my granddaughter is still sleeping!” Her heart softened by love, she entered Rādhā’s bedroom and said, “My darling child! Please get out of bed. Have You forgotten that today is Sunday? After You bathe, make the morning offering to Sūryadeva and then quickly prepare for his pūjā.”

sanskrit:
tad-vacaḥ pratibuddhātha
viśākhotthāya sālasā
sakhi! tūrṇaṃ samuttiṣṭhot-
tiṣṭheti prāha satvarā
translation: Hearing the old woman’s words, Viśākhā awakened from her sleep. Even though she felt very tired, she quickly rose and said to Śrīmatī, “Sakhī! Get up! Get up now!”

sanskrit:
tāsāṃ vacobhiḥ śayane ’tha mugdhā
muhuḥ prajāgaryya punar nidadrau
vicālitā vīcicayais taḍāge
sā rājahaṃsīva ratālasāṅgī
translation: Being awakened again and again by the words of Jaṭilā, Mukharā, and then Viśākhā, Rādhā felt as bewildered as a swan being tossed about on a choppy lake. Exhausted from making love, She fell back into slumber.

sanskrit:
tadaivāvasarābhijñā
jagrāha rati-mañjarī
sakhī vṛndāvaneśvaryāḥ
śrīmac-caraṇa-paṅkajam
Seizing the opportunity, Rati Mañjarī affectionately placed her hands upon
Vṛndāvaneśvarī Śrī Rādhā’s lotus feet. (Govinda-līlāmṛtam 2.52)
translation: tadaivāvasarābhijñā jagrāha rati-mañjarī sakhī vṛndāvaneśvaryāḥ śrīmac-caraṇa-paṅkajam Seizing the opportunity, Rati Mañjarī affectionately placed her hands upon Vṛndāvaneśvarī Śrī Rādhā’s lotus feet.

sanskrit:
ittham iyaṃ bahubhiḥ kṛta-bodhā
svāc-chayanād udatiṣṭhad analpāt
tām atha vīkṣya supīta-paṭāṅgīṃ
śaṅkita-hṛn-mukharedam uvāca
druta-kanaka-savarṇaṃ sāyam etan murārer
vasanam urasi dṛṣṭaṃ yat sakhī te bibharti
kim idam ayi viśākhe! hā pramādaḥ pramādo
vyavasitam idam asyāḥ paśya śuddhānvayāyāḥ
translation: In this way, Rādhā was awakened by Her sakhīs and got up from Her very expensive bed. When Mukharā saw Her dressed in yellow clothing, she became suspicious and said, “Ayi Viśākhā! Look! Last evening I saw on Kṛṣṇa’s chest that same lustrous golden cloth that your sakhī is now wearing! Hāy! What a calamity! What a disaster! What kind of behavior is this for a girl born of a pure family?”

sanskrit:
tad-vacaś cakita-dhīr hṛdi sakhyā
vīkṣya pīta-vasanaṃ cala-dṛṣṭyā
hā kim etad iti tāṃ ca diśantī
drāg uvāca jaratīṃ ca viśākhā
svabhāvāndhe! jālāntara-gata-vibhātodita-ravi-
cchaṭā-jāla-sparśocchalita-kanakāṅga-dyuti-bharaiḥ
vayasyāyāḥ śyāmaṃ vasanam api pīti-kṛtam idaṃ
kuto mugdhe śaṅkāṃ jarati kuruṣe śuddha-matiṣu
translation: Startled by Mukharā’s words, Viśākhā noticed the yellow cloth on her anxious sakhī’s bosom. “Hāy! What’s this!” she gasped and quickly said to Mukharā, “Oh, silly old woman! You’re blind as a bat! It’s just the morning sun rays shining through the window upon Rādhikā’s golden skin that make Her blue dress appear to be yellow. Why do you needlessly doubt the pure-hearted Rādhā like this?”

sanskrit:
lalitā-pramukhās tāvat
sakhyas tāḥ sva-sva-gehataḥ
ājagmus tvaritāḥ sakhyāḥ
praskhalad gatayo ’ntikam
translation: Just then, Lalitā and the other sakhīs all staggered in from their respective homes and approached Śrī Rādhā.

sanskrit:
tāsāṃ vākyair gatāyāntu
kṛta-vañcana-sañcayaiḥ
mukharāyāṃ tato ’nyāsu
draṣṭu-kāmāsu tatra tām
ekaikaśo ’tha militāsu sakhīṣu sarvā-
sv anyonya-hāsa-parihāsa-parāsu tāsu
suśliṣṭa-maṇḍalatayaiva kṛtopaveśā-
sv ārūḍha-ratna-maṇi-hema-catuṣkikāsu
translation: After hearing the deceptive words of Viśākhā and the other sakhīs, Mukharā turned and left the room. One by one, more sakhīs arrived and they all sat upon vedis inlaid with gems and gold, surrounding Rādhā as they joked and laughed in great fun together.

sanskrit:
śrī-rādhikā-milanam eva samasta-harṣa-
śasyaika-varṣam iti yad-dhṛdi niścikāya
tat śyāmalaitya samayā samayābhivijñā
śliṣṭā tayā suṣamayeva tadāsa tatra
translation: Then Śyāmalā, aware of the intrigue, arrived and Śrīmatī warmly embraced her and offered a seat. As She did so, it appeared as though Rādhā’s own halo extended to surround Her friend. Meeting with Rādhikā makes Śyāmalā’s heart bloom with joy, just as a field of grain blooms luxuriantly after a refreshing rain.

sanskrit:
śyāme! tvam evam adhunaiva vicintyamānā
man-netra-vartma-gamitā vidhinā yathaiva
tadvat sa tarṣa-viṭapī phalayiṣyate ced
adyaiva tarhi gaṇayāny api suprabhātam
translation: Rādhā, overwhelmed by love, forgot Her previous night’s affair with Kṛṣṇa and exclaimed, “Śyāmalā! Sakhī, I was just thinking of you. As though by destiny, you have appeared before My eyes. If the tree of My desires bears fruit in the same way, I’ll indeed consider this a fine morning!”

sanskrit:
hantaiṣa santatam atīva samedhamānaḥ
śaśvat sakhībhir api sundari! sicyamānaḥ
nādyāpi yat phalam adhād ayi! ko ’tra hetur
hā tat kadātirabhasād avalokayiṣye
translation: “O beautiful Śyāmā! This desire tree of Mine is growing large and My sakhīs water it continuously, but still it produces no fruit. What could be the cause? Hāy! When, in great Sitting platforms joy, shall I see the fruit of this tree?”

sanskrit:
rādhe! sa te na phalito yadi tat phaliṣyaty
āścaryam asya phalam apy alasāṅgi! buddhye
āsvādyamānam api saurabha-māditāli
pratyāyayaty ananubhūtam iva svam uccaiḥ
translation: Śyāmalā, understanding that Rādhā indirectly referred to enjoying with Kṛṣṇa, replied, “Rādhā! If Your tree has not yet borne fruit, surely it soon will. O tired one, I understand the fruit of this tree is astonishing. Its sweet fragrance maddens the bees (and sakhīs), and even though You have personally tasted it, it causes You to believe You haven’t.”

sanskrit:
pakṣmāvalī bata yadīya-rasena śoṇe-
nārañji kañja-mukhi! tan na tad apy apaśyaḥ
yat-svādana-vyatikarād adharo vraṇitvam
āgāt tathāpi tad aho! na kadāpy abhuṅkthāḥ
translation: “This is amazing, lotus-faced one! You’ve never even seen the very fruit whose juice has reddened Your eyelashes. You’ve never tasted the fruit by whose touch Your lips have been repeatedly bruised!”

sanskrit:
śyāme! tvam apy alam alakṣita-man-nitānta-
svānta-vraṇā hasasi māṃ yad ato bravīmi
vidyud vihanti timiraṃ niśi yad dṛśos tat
sadyaḥ punar dviguṇayed iti bhoḥ pratīhi
translation: Hearing this, Rādhā responded, “Śyāmā! You are making jokes about Me without understanding the depth of My heartache. Therefore I say to you: Just as after a brilliant flash of lightning the night seems even darker than before, in the same way, after having Kṛṣṇa’s embrace for only half a moment, the pain of my separation from Him has now doubled in strength.”

sanskrit:
rādhe! kalā-nidhir ayaṃ vidhinopanītas
tvāṃ santatāmṛtamayair adhinot karāgraiḥ
yat tat-kalāḥ svayam aho kucayor vibharṣi
vidyun-nibhatva-parivādam athāpi datse
translation: Śyāmalā replied, “Sakhī! That which You have criticized as being like lightning is actually a bright moon placed before You by Providence. The continuous falling of His ambrosial rays upon You makes You very happy. Indeed! Some of His crescent-shaped artwork is present upon Your breasts right now!”

sanskrit:
śyāme! sa me sakhi! dadau na kalaṅkam eva
satyaṃ kalānidhir asāv iti vaḥ pratītaḥ
datte kadāpi mama dṛṣṭi-cakorikā yair
jyotsnā-kaṇaṃ yad api tan na punar nikāmam
translation: Rādhā: “My friend Śyāmalā, to Me this so-called artwork of the moon is nothing but a stain. Even if He sometimes gives a particle of moonlight to My cakora-like eyes, that’s still not enough to satisfy Me.”

sanskrit:
rādhe! sphuṭaṃ vada bhavan-mukha-paṅkajottha-
naktan-tanehita-sudhā-dyudhunī vidhūya
tāpaṃ nimajjayatu māṃ svam anu prabhāte
kṛtyāntaraṃ mama kathaṃ tad-ṛte susidhyet
translation: Śyāmalā: “Rādhā, be straightforward with us and say what You really mean. If I can’t bathe in the nectarous Gaṅgā of Your nightly pastimes with Kṛṣṇa, I don’t feel like doing anything. Just like without taking an auspicious morning bath, no work can be undertaken, in the same way, if I don’t hear from You about Your affairs with Mādhava, all my actions are useless.”

sanskrit:
śyāme ’dhikuñja-nilayaṃ nava-nīla-kānti-
dhārā yadā snapayituṃ niśi māṃ pravṛttā
tarhy eva pañcaśara-sañcaya-nāṭya-raṅga-
bhūmiṃ ca kena ca kāñcana yāpitā ’sam
translation: In this way, seeing that Śyāmalā was very eager to hear the news of Her romance, and having already compared Kṛṣṇa to a streak of lightning, Rādhā affectionately replied, “O Śyāmā, when, in My forest cottage last night, I was bathed by a cascade of bluish splendor, somehow I was transported to an indescribable dancing stage surrounded by thousands of Cupids.”65

sanskrit:
alasa-valitam aṅgaṃ svāvasādaṃ vyanakti
glapitam iva mṛṇālī-kandalaṃ dordvayaṃ te
daśana-vasanam etan nīrasaṃ gaṇḍa-pālī
lulita-lalita-patrā prakramaḥ kas tavaiṣaḥ
translation: She asked Rādhā, “Sakhī, what’s wrong with You? Your listless body clearly shows You “In other words, simply from seeing the splendor of Kṛṣṇa’s nails, I was pierced by Cupid’s arrows and became bewildered.” are very tired. Your arms look like withered young lotus stalks and Your lips are pale. Your cheeks have no beautiful decorations painted upon them.”

sanskrit:
abhinava-latikeva vāta-rugnā
nava-nalinīva mataṅgajena bhugnā
mṛdutara-nava-mālikeva dhūtā
mada-madhupena vilakṣyase tvam adya
translation: “Today You appear to be like a young creeper who has been tortured by a strong wind, a tender lotus bud crushed by an elephant, and a soft, fresh garland abandoned by a drunken black bee.”66

sanskrit:
api ciram abhilaṣyamāṇa evaṃ
praṇayini ko ’pi sudurlabho hi labdhaḥ
atha katham iyam anyathā ’smad ādeḥ
phalita-vatī sakhi! bhāgya-kalpa-vallī
translation: “O Sundarī! You have certainly obtained something rare from Your long-cherished lover. Otherwise, how has our creeper of good fortune become so fruitful? Consider that.”

sanskrit:
kvāhaṃ sthitā kva calitā kva ca vā sa panthā
nītāsmi kena nalinākṣi tadīya pārśvam
kiṃvā babhūva mayi tatra sametavatyāṃ
jānāmy ahaṃ yadi tadā bhavatī na vetti
translation: “O lotus-eyed one! If I know where I was, where I went, on what path I walked with Him, or how I arrived in such and such a place, how is it that you don’t know? After all, I never do anything without consulting you.”

sanskrit:
vyāpāro manasaś ca yatra na gataḥ sambhāvanābhāvato
yat svapnaḥ kim athendra-jālam athavā bhrāntiḥ sudīrghaiva me
tat kiṃ hlādi kim ārtidaṃ kim ubhayaṃ kiṃvā na tan nāpi tac-
translation: “In other words, Your dress is disordered and dirty, Your lips and breasts have tooth and nail wounds on them, and You long to enjoy with Your lover.” ceto-vidruti-kārakaṃ ca manaso mūrchākaraṃ cābhavat “If one never contemplates a particular idea, one can’t develop an opinion about it. Whether it was a dream, a magic spell, or my long-continuing delusion, or whether it caused Me joy or pain, or both, or neither, I cannot say. But I do feel that that which causes the heart to melt and that which causes the mind to swoon are one and the same.”

sanskrit:
kelī-kalādhyayana-kauśalam ekadaiva
na syād ataḥ kim api no bhavatī viveda
bhūyas tataḥ sakhi! vilāsa-guroḥ sakāśād
yatnād adhīṣva yadi vijñatamāsi bhūṣṇuḥ
