translation: Hearing this, Śyāmalā replied, “You can’t be an expert in the amorous arts while You’re still a mere student. Therefore, You don’t know very much. If You really want to be a wise person, You should once again approach Your vilāsa-guru and try to learn more.”

sanskrit:
mātaḥ paraṃ sumukhi! yāmi tadīya-pārśvaṃ
dūrād asau nayana-vartma-nivartanīyaḥ
adhyetu nāma bhavatī tata eva tat te
pāṇḍityam eva manaso rasadaṃ mama syāt
translation: Rādhā responded, “O Sumukhī, from now on I won’t go anywhere with Him; I won’t even look at Him from a distance. You are very intelligent and have studied with Him many times before, so you should continue to do so. I’m very happy that you’ve become such an expert.”

sanskrit:
bhrājante vara-danti! mauktika-gaṇā yasyollikhadbhir nakhaiḥ
kṣiptāḥ puṣkara-mālayāvṛta-rucaḥ kuñjeṣu kuñjeṣv amī
śauṭīryābdhir uroja-pañjara-taṭe saṃveśayantyā kathaṃ
sa śrīmān hariṇekṣaṇe! harir abhūn netreṇa baddhas tvayā?
translation: Śyāmalā: “O Vara-dantī! When Kṛṣṇa scratches the breasts of the gopīs, the luster of their beautiful pearl necklaces is covered by His lotus garland. Now those shining pearls lie scattered from bower to bower. O doe-eyed one, how have You captured that ocean of manliness with only Your eyes and brought Him to rest upon Your chest?”

sanskrit:
ko ’yaṃ kṛṣṇa iti vyudasyati dhṛtiṃ yas tanvi karṇaṃ viśan
rāgāndhe! kim idaṃ sadaiva bhavatī tasyor asi krīḍati
hāsyaṃ mā kuru mohite! tvam adhunā nyastāsya haste mayā
One with a beautiful face
One with nice teeth
satyaṃ satyam asau dṛgaṅganam agād adyaiva vidyun-nibhaḥ
translation: Śrī Rādhā said, “O slender one! Who is this person ‘Kṛṣṇa’? When the two syllables of His name simply enter within our ears, all our patience is destroyed!” Śyāmalā replied, “O Rāgāndhā! What are you saying? You always dally on His broad chest!” Rādhā: “Please don’t laugh, My friend.” Śyāmalā: “I have now placed You in His hands.” Rādhā: “True; but it feels like today is the only time in My life that I’ve seen My restless, lightning-like Lord.”

sanskrit:
priya-sakhi! mama vṛttaṃ pṛccha mā bhāgyam īdṛk
kva nu mama kathayeyaṃ tvayy ahaṃ tān vilāsān
dhṛtavati karam eva śyāmale kvāsa kāhaṃ
kim iva ca karako ’sau kiṃ vyadhān na smarāmi
Rādhā said, “Priya-sakhī, you shouldn’t ask any more questions about My affairs. Alas,
translation: such is My fortune! How can I possibly describe My pastimes to you? I don’t remember anything about Śyāmasundara taking My hand, or where I was, or even who I was, what to speak of what His hand was like, or what He did!”

sanskrit:
veṇīṃ gumphati divya-puṣpa-nicayaiḥ sīmanta-sīmany aho
sindūraṃ nidadhāti kajjala-mayīṃ nirmāti rekhāṃ dṛśoḥ
divyaṃ vāsayate dukūlam asakṛt tāmbūlam apy āśayed
itthambhūta-ratiḥ sakhā tava na māṃ talpe nidhatte ’ṅkataḥ
translation: “Aho! Your friend tied a fragrant flower garland within My braid and placed vermilion on the part of My hair. He then painted a thin line of collyrium around My eyes and had Me don a very beautiful dress. After this He gave Me tāmbūla to chew. Feeling great affection for Me, He held Me on His lap rather than placing Me on the bed again.”

sanskrit:
Blinded by love
nityaṃ manmukha-sammukhaṃ mukha-vidhuṃ dhatte ’nimiṣekṣaṇo
nityaṃ manmukham eva paśyati mayaivājasra-goṣṭhī-paraḥ
ādhāyaiva śayīta māṃ hṛdi mayaivāvartayet pārśvakaṃ
sakhyus te sakhi! sarva-nāgara-maṇeḥ prītiḥ kathaṃ varṇyatām?
translation: “Every day He places His moonlike face before Mine and with unblinking eyes He gazes at Me. Every day the two of us spend countless hours alone together. He places Me in His heart and then lies alongside Me. O Sakhī! How can I describe My affection for that friend of yours, the jewel of all lovers?”

sanskrit:
vilāsa-ceṣṭā sakhi! keśi-nāśino
halāhalābhā pradahanti me manaḥ
kṛntanti marmāṇi guṇā ghuṇā iva
premā vikārī hṛdi hṛd-vraṇo yathā
translation: “O Sakhī, Keśava’s romantic movements burn My heart like poison. His good qualities cut through My core like a wood mite destroys a tree. His love creates unbearable agitation in My heart, as though it has been somehow wounded.”

sanskrit:
no vidmaḥ kim u gauravaṃ gurukule kaulīnya-rakṣā-vidhau
na śraddhā kim u durjanokti-garala-jvālāsu kiṃ no bhayam
udvegādan avasthitaṃ mama manaḥ kasyāpi megha-tviṣo
yūnaḥ śrotra-gatair ghuṇair iva guṇair antaḥ kṛtaṃ jarjaram
translation: “Do you think I don’t know how important family is? Do you think I have no regard for My family’s honor, or I don’t fear the poisonlike criticism of slanderous people? But what can I do? My mind is agitated and full of anxiety, and when I hear of the wonderful qualities of that cloud-colored young man, My heart is shattered!”

sanskrit:
rādhe! yad-āsya-sarasī-ruha-gandha evam
andhīkaroti kulajā-kulam āli! dūrāt
tan-madhv atīva surasaṃ sarasaṃ pibantyāś
citta-bhramas tava madād iti naiva citram
translation: After hearing Rādhā’s words, Śyāmalā replied, “Sakhī! You’ve drunk too much of that sweet nectar from Kṛṣṇa’s lotus mouth, so it’s no wonder You’re bewildered. Even smelling the aroma of that lotus mouth from a distance can cause the gopīs to go blind in ecstasy!”

sanskrit:
atrāntare madhurikā militātha pṛṣṭā
tābhir jagāda madhuraṃ śṛṇutaitad ālyaḥ
kasyaicid eva kṛtaye vrajarāja-veśma
prāptādya kautukam aho yad uṣasy apaśyam
Meanwhile, the sakhī named Madhurikā arrived and everyone inquired about any news.
translation: She said, “O Sakhīs! Today, to complete some work, I went to the house of Nanda Mahārāja at daybreak. I saw something very curious there. Listen.”

sanskrit:
paurṇamāsī bhagavatī sarva-siddhi-vidhāyinī
kāṣāya-vasanā gaurī kāśa-keśī darāyatā
kṛṣṇaṃ draṣṭu-manās talpād udatiṣṭhad dvija-dhvanaiḥ
translation: “Eager to see Kṛṣṇa, Bhagavatī Paurṇamāsī (who can bless one with all success, wears a reddish garment, has a golden complexion, strawlike gray hair and a slightly tall body) rose from her bed with the singing of the birds.”

sanskrit:
atha prabhāte kṛta-nitya-kṛtyā
prītyācyutasyātivihasta-cittā
premendu-pūrṇā kila paurṇamāsī
tūrṇaṃ vrajendrālayam āsasāda
translation: “Paurṇamāsī, in whose heart prema always shines like the full moon, quickly finished her morning duties and hurried to Nanda’s house, eager to see her beloved Kṛṣṇa.”

sanskrit:
kṣaumaṃ vāsaḥ pṛthu-kaṭi-taṭe bibhratī sūtra-naddhaṃ
putra-sneha-snuta-kuca-yugaṃ jāta-kampaṃ ca subhrūḥ
rajjv-ākarṣa-śrama-bhuja-calat-kaṅkaṇau kuṇḍale ca
svinnaṃ vaktraṃ kavara-vigalan-mālatī nirmamantha
translation: “As Mother Yaśodā churned butter, her brow, wet with perspiration, was very beautiful. She wore a fine dress, with a colorful sash tied around her broad hips. Her breasts, wet with milk because of affection for her son, were trembling as she pulled the churning rope. The bangles on her tired arms jingled, and her earrings swung to and fro. A garland of mālatī flowers had fallen from her braided hair.”

sanskrit:
rajani-vipariṇāme gargarīṇāṃ garīyān
dadhi-mathana-vinodād udbhavann eṣa nādaḥ
amara-nagara-kakṣā-cakram ākramya sadyaḥ
smarayati sura-vṛndāny abdhi-manthotsavasya
translation: “The loud sounds of all the churning pots together rose up to the heavenly planets and reminded the gods and goddesses of the great churning of the ocean.”

sanskrit:
manthānoddhṛta-gavya-vindu-nikara-vyākīrṇa-ramyāṅganaṃ
prema-snigdha-janānvitaṃ bahu-vidhai ratnair vicitrāntaram
kṣīrormy ucchalitaṃ mudāhi-vilasac-chayyā-prasuptācyutaṃ
śveta-dvīpam ivālayaṃ vraja-pater vīkṣyāsa sānanditā
translation: “Lord Acyuta, decorated with beautiful jewels, lies happily asleep upon the soft belly of Ananta-śeṣa, accompanied by affectionate devotees, surrounded by waves of milk risen from the churning of the ocean around Śveta-dvīpa. In the same way, Paurṇamāsī became overjoyed seeing Kṛṣṇa, also adorned with beautiful gems, lying contentedly on His soft bed in Nanda’s house, surrounded by His loved ones, with waves of milk rising from the cooking pots in the nearby kitchen.”

sanskrit:
tām āgatām abhiprekṣya
sākṣād iva tapaḥ-śriyam
vraja-rajñī parābhijñā
sthiti-jñābhyudyayau mudā
translation: “When Yaśodā Mā, who is very wise and knowledgeable about the traditional customs, saw that Paurṇamāsī, who is just like the ‘power of austerity’ incarnate, had arrived, she went joyfully out to meet her.”

sanskrit:
ehi bho bhagavatīti vraja-vandye
svāgatāsi bhavatīṃ praṇamāmi
ity udīrya savidhe praṇamantīṃ
sā mukunda-jananīṃ parirebhe
translation: “‘Hello Bhagavatī! Please come. Are you doing well? You are highly respected in Vraja. I offer obeisance at your feet.’ Saying this, Yaśodā bowed down and then Paurṇamāsī embraced her.”

sanskrit:
āśīrbhir abhinandyāmūṃ
govinda-darśanosukā
papraccha kuśalaṃ cāsyāḥ
sadhavātmaja-go-tateḥ
translation: “Eager to see Govinda, Paurṇamāsī expressed her happiness by giving blessings, and then asked about the welfare of Yaśodā, her husband, son and cows.”

sanskrit:
nivedya kuśalaṃ cāsyai
tayotkaṇṭhitayā saha
utkā śayyā-gṛhaṃ sūnoḥ
praviveśa vrajeśvarī
translation: “Yaśodā told her they were all well and then the two of them eagerly entered Kṛṣṇa’s bedroom.”

sanskrit:
ḍorī-jūṭita-vakra-keśa-paṭalā sindūra-bindūllasat-
sīmanta-dyuti-raṅga-bhūṣaṇa-vidhiṃ nātiprabhūtaṃ śritā
govindāsya-nisṛṣṭa-sāśru-nayana-dvandvā navendīvara-
śyāma-śyāma-rucir vicitra-sicayā ‘goṣṭheśvarī pātu vaḥ’
translation: May Yaśodā Mā, queen of the cowherds, protect you all. Her dark, curly locks have been tied back and the line of vermilion in the part of her hair shines radiantly. She is modestly decorated with ornaments, and her eyes fill with tears as she gazes at Govinda’s face. Her bodily complexion is dark blue, like a newly grown blue lotus, and she wears a beautiful and colorful dress.

sanskrit:
paryaṅke nyasya savyaṃ tad-upari nihita-svāṅgabhārātha pāṇiṃ
kṛṣṇasyāṅgaṃ spṛśantītara-kara-kamaleneṣad-ābhugna-madhyā
siñcanty ānanda-bāṣpaiḥ snuta-kuca-payasāṃ dhārayā cāsya talpaṃ
vatsottiṣṭhāśu nidrāṃ tyaja mukha-kamalaṃ darśayety āha mātā
translation: “Placing her left hand on the bed above Kṛṣṇa for support, she leaned over and gently touched His body with her right hand. Moistening the bed with tears of joy and the milk oozing from her breasts, she said to Him, ‘My child! Get up quickly. Wake up and show us Your lotus face.’”

sanskrit:
gāndharvike! śṛṇu yad anyad abhūd vicitraṃ
nīlāṃśukaṃ svatanayor asi vīkṣyamāṇām
tām āha saiva bhagavaty ayi goṣṭha-rājñi!
rāmāmbareṇa parivartitam asya vāsa
translation: Madhurikā said, “Listen Gāndharvikā! Now here’s where it gets interesting. When Vrajeśvarī saw Your blue cloth on her son’s chest, she said, ‘Why has Gopāla taken off His yellow cloth and put on a blue one?’ Thinking about this for a moment, Bhagavatī Paurṇamāsī said, ‘O Queen of the Pasturing Grounds, Gopāla must have exchanged clothes with Balarāma.’”

sanskrit:
tāṭaṅkagāruṇa-maṇi-pratibimba eva
gaṇḍe vibhāti tava mādhava! śoṇa-śociḥ
ity ukta eva sa tayā nija-pāṇinā taṃ
sadyo jagharṣa bhavad-ādhara-rāga-bhāgam
translation: “Seeing the red tāmbūla stains from Your lips on Kṛṣṇa’s cheeks, Paurṇamāsī said, ‘Hey Mādhava, it seems the rubies in Your earrings are reflecting on Your cheeks with a reddish glow.’ Hearing this, Kṛṣṇa immediately began rubbing His cheeks with His hand.”

sanskrit:
uttiṣṭha tāta rajanīyam agād virāmaṃ
paśyāṃśumantam udayodyamanābhirāmam
pratyūṣa-sevana-vidhau vilasad-vilāsāḥ
śayyālayaṃ tava viśanti kumāra-dāsāḥ
translation: “Then Yaśodā said, ‘Dear boy, get up now; the night is over. Just look at how beautiful the rising sun is. Your young servants have arrived to perform their morning sevā.’”

sanskrit:
saṅkīrtayan jaya jayeti girā suvṛttas
tvāṃ tāta jāgarayituṃ praṇayāt pravṛttaḥ
kīras tavaiṣa nija-pāṇi-talena puṣṭaḥ
sanmañju-vāk kanaka-pañjara-vāsa-hṛṣṭaḥ
translation: “‘My child, this parrot, whom You have fed with Your own palm, and who lives joyfully within a golden cage, is trying to lovingly awaken You with his sweet voice, saying jaya, jaya.’”

sanskrit:
khedas tavaiṣa śayanālasa-bhāra-mūlaḥ
svāpaṃ jahīhi bhava jāgaraṇānukūlaḥ
itthaṃ kareṇa mṛdunā muhur aṅgam aṅgam
āspṛśya bāhu-yugalena tam āliliṅga
translation: “‘You’re feeling lazy because You’ve been asleep. But now it’s time to wake up.’ Saying this, Mother Yaśodā gently rubbed Kṛṣṇa’s body for a little while and then embraced Him.”

sanskrit:
mātuḥ kalāṃ giram atipraṇayopagūhaṃ
śrutvānubhūya ca tadaiva sa samyag ūham
gātrāvamoṭana-puraḥsara-jṛmbhaṇena
jāgrad-daśām abhinināya kutūhalena
translation: “Hearing His mother’s affectionate words and feeling her touch, Kṛṣṇa thought for a moment and then rubbed His body, yawned and pretended that He had just awakened.”

sanskrit:
kālociteṣu paricāraṇa-kauśaleṣu
gāḍhānurāga-parabhāga-nirākuleṣu
dakṣaṃ samakṣam anuśāsya kumāra-dāsī-
dāsaṃ vrajendra-gṛhiṇī sva-gṛhānayāsīt
translation: “Among the many skilled and devoted servants were a very talented group of young boys and girls. While instructing them in their duties, Mother Yaśodā then took them to her own room.”

sanskrit:
tāvad gobhaṭa-bhadrasena-subala-śrī-stokakṛṣṇārjuna-
śrīdāmojjvala-dāma-kiṅkiṇi-sudāmādyāḥ sakhāyo gṛhāt
āgatya tvaritā mudābhimilitāḥ śrī-sīriṇā prāṅgaṇe
kṛṣṇottiṣṭha nijeṣṭa-goṣṭham aya bho ity āhvayantaḥ sthitāḥ
translation: “At that time, Gobhaṭa, Bhadrasena, Subala, Stokakṛṣṇa, Arjuna, Śrīdāma, Ujjvala, Dāma, Kiṅkiṇi, Sudāma and Kṛṣṇa’s other friends began to quickly arrive from their own homes. Joining with Baladeva in the courtyard, they all began to call, ‘Hey Kṛṣṇa, get up! Let’s all go to Your beloved cow shed!’”

sanskrit:
hī hī prabhātaṃ kim u bho vayasyā
adyāpi nidrāti kathaṃ sakhā naḥ
tad bodhayāmy enam itīrayan sva-
talpād udasthān madhumaṅgalo ’pi
translation: “Then Madhumaṅgala laughed with a hee hee sound and said, ‘Ohe friends! Is it morning already? I wonder why our pal Kṛṣṇa is still asleep. I’m going to wake Him now.’ Saying this, Madhumaṅgala rose from his own bed.”

sanskrit:
samuttiṣṭha vayasyeti
jalpaṃs talpālayaṃ hareḥ
nidrālasa-skhalad-yānaḥ
prāviśan madhumaṅgalaḥ
translation: “Calling ‘Hey buddy! Get up! Get up!,’ Madhumaṅgala stumbled sleepily into Kṛṣṇa’s bedroom.”

sanskrit:
tad-vāg-vigata-nidro ’yam
uttiṣṭhāsur apīśvaraḥ
utthātum īśvaro nāsīd
ghūrṇā-pūrṇekṣaṇaḥ kṣaṇam
translation: “Though awakened by Madhumaṅgala’s words, Kṛṣṇa was still drowsy and His eyes began to roll. He tried to get up, but wasn’t able to, even for a moment!”

sanskrit:
uttiṣṭha kuryāṃ mukha-mārjanaṃ te
balasya vāsaḥ kim iha tvad-aṅge
iti bruvāṇāpanināya nīlaṃ
vāsas tad-aṅgād avadac ca sāryām
translation: “Yaśodā Mā said, ‘My child, get up now. Let me wash Your face. And why is Baladeva’s blue cloth on Your body?’ Then she removed the cloth and spoke to Bhagavatī Paurṇamāsī.”

sanskrit:
ayi bhagavati! paśyācoṭitaṃ me ’sya sūnoḥ
kamala-mṛdulam aṅgaṃ malla-līlāsu lolaiḥ
khara-nakhara-śikhābhir dhātu-rāgāticitraṃ
capala-śiśu-samūhair hā hatā kiṃ karomi?
translation: ‘O Bhagavatī! Just look at that! My son’s soft, tender body is covered with red mineral powder and nail-marks made by His restless boy friends as they wrestled and rolled about. Ayi! What can I do?’

sanskrit:
sneha-bharaiḥ svajananyāś
citra-padām api vāṇīm
tām avadhārya murārir
hrī-cakitekṣaṇa āsīt
translation: “Hearing these surprising words from His loving mother, Kṛṣṇa became ashamed and alarmed.”

sanskrit:
kṛṣṇaṃ saśaṅkam āśaṅkya
parihāsa-paṭur baṭuḥ
sneha-klinnāntarām ambām
avadan madhumaṅgalaḥ
satyam amba! vayasyālī
vāritāpi mayāniśam
reme ’nenātilubdhena
kuñjeṣu keli-cañcalā
translation: “Then Madhumaṅgala, the jokester brāhmaṇa boy, alarmed Kṛṣṇa even further by saying to the soft-hearted Yaśodā, ‘Mother! What you say is true. Every day, Kṛṣṇa eagerly sports in the forest with His restless friends, even against my protests.’”

sanskrit:
atha prakāśī-kṛta-bālya-vibhramo
yatnāt samunmīlya vilocanaṃ muhuḥ
paśyan puraḥ svāṃ jananīṃ hariḥ punar
nyamīlayat sa smita-vaktra-paṅkajaḥ
translation: “When Kṛṣṇa heard Madhumaṅgala’s double-edged description of His boyish pastimes, He struggled to open His eyes slightly, saw His mother before Him, and then, with a lotus- like smile, closed them again.”

sanskrit:
ākarṇya vācaṃ vraja-rāja-patnyāḥ
samīkṣya kṛṣṇasya ca bālya-ceṣṭām
bhāvāntarācchādakarīṃ jananyās
taṃ paurṇamāsī smita-pūrvam āha
translation: “After hearing Yaśodā’s affectionate words and carefully observing Kṛṣṇa’s reaction, Paurṇamāsī smiled gently and spoke to Kṛṣṇa in a way that concealed the fact that she wasn’t speaking as a mother.”

sanskrit:
sakhīnāṃ sandohair niravadhi mahākeli-tatibhiḥ
pariśrāntas tvaṃ yat svapiṣi sumate yogyam iha tat
anālokya tvāṃ bhos tṛṣitam api no tarṇaka-kulaṃ
dhayaty ūdhaḥ kintu vraja-kula-pate jāgṛhi tataḥ
translation: ‘O intelligent one! You’re enjoying the happiness of sleep because You played so hard with Your friends. That’s all right, but without seeing You, the thirsty calves won’t drink their mother’s milk. So wake up, O leader of the Vrajavāsīs!’

sanskrit:
uttiṣṭha goṣṭheśvara-nandanārāt
paśyāgrajo ’yaṃ saha te vayasyaiḥ
goṣṭhaṃ pratiṣṭhāsur api pratīkṣya
tvām aṅgane tiṣṭhati tarṇakaiś ca
translation: ‘Vrajendra-nandana! Please get up quickly! Look there: Your friends, as well as Your elder brother and the calves, have all gathered in the courtyard, waiting to go to the cow shed.’

sanskrit:
sa-muṣṭi-pāṇi-dvayam unnamayya
vimoṭayan so ’tha rasālasāṅgam
jṛmbhā-visarpad-daśanāṃśu-jālas
tamāla-nīlaḥ śayanād udasthāt
translation: “Hearing this, Kṛṣṇa awoke and stretched His clenched fists into the air. After rubbing His dark, tired limbs, He yawned, revealing His sparkling teeth, and then rose from the bed.”

sanskrit:
unmīlana-pratinimīlanayor bahutve
jāgrac-chayāna-daśayor iva miśritatve
sā nidrayā viraha-kātarayā dhṛteva
tasyotthitasya nayana-dvitayī dideva
translation: “Kṛṣṇa’s eyes were very beautiful as they opened and closed many times, as though He were half awake and half asleep. Nidrādevī70 seemed unable to leave them due to the pain of separation.”

sanskrit:
khaṭvaika-deśe tv atha sanniviṣṭo
vinyasta-pādābja-yugaḥ pṛthivyām
The goddess of sleep.
namāmy ahaṃ tvāṃ bhagavaty ayīti
jagāda jṛmbhodgama-gadgadaṃ saḥ
translation: “Then, sitting on the bed, Kṛṣṇa put His lotus feet on the floor, and as He yawned widely, He muttered to Paurṇamāsī, ‘Bhagavatī, I offer My obeisance to you.’”

sanskrit:
ā-pāda-śīrṣam atha pāṇi-talābhimarśe-
‘nāvyādajo ’ṅghrim’ iti mantram udāharantī
saṃrakṣya tūrṇam akhilāṅgam athordhva-dṛṣṭyā
kiñcit sa-kāku-bharam arthayate sma rājñī
translation: “Then Mother Yaśodā touched Kṛṣṇa from head to toe with her palms as she recited the mantra ‘avyādajo ’ṅghrim’ for His protection. Looking upward, she began to pray in a plaintive voice.”

sanskrit:
devādhideva! bhavataiva cirāt suto ’yaṃ
dattaḥ sva-bandhu-jana-jīvanatām upetaḥ
pālyo ’pi nātha! bhavataiva kṛpā-bhareṇa
svenaiva kām apacitiṃ tava vedmi kartum
translation: “‘O Supreme God! After a long time You mercifully gave this son to me. He is the very life of His friends and family. Even though I don’t know the proper way to worship, O Lord, please be satisfied and protect my child in every way.’”

sanskrit:
ārātrikeṇa maṇi-maṅgala-dīpa-bhājā
vibhrājitena jita-saubhagavat samājāḥ
ādhāya paṇi-sarasī-ruhayor mudāsya-
nīrājanaṃ vidadhire ’sya kumāra-dāsyaḥ
translation: “Then the very fortunate kumāra-dāsīs performed ārātrika, joyfully waving a beautiful ghee lamp inlaid with auspicious jewels before Kṛṣṇa.”

sanskrit:
uṣṇīṣa-bandha-sumanojñatamottamāṅgāḥ
pāthoja-keśara-susaurabha-sundarāṅgāḥ
śyāmāḥ sitāś ca haritā aruṇāś ca pītā
ye ke ’pi ke ’pi mahanīya-guṇaiḥ parītāḥ
tair eva kevala-sukhānubhava-svarūpair
naisargikānudina-divya-kumāra-rūpaiḥ
dāsī-gaṇair api ca dāsa-gaṇair udāraiḥ
sevā vyadhāyi vividhāsya vilola-hāraiḥ
translation: “The blissful young male and female servants began to intently engage in Kṛṣṇa’s sevā. Young servant girls The boys had beautiful turbans tied upon their heads, and necklaces dangled on everyone’s chests. Their bodies were as fragrant as lotus flowers, and they wore clothing of dark blue, white, green, red and yellow colors. They were all adorned with the noblest of qualities.”

sanskrit:
paryaṅkataḥ samadhiruhya maṇī-catuṣkaṃ
śrī-pāda-pīṭha-mahasā vilasad-vapuṣkam
cārūpaviṣṭam atihṛṣṭa-hṛdo gṛhītvā
cārūpacāram atha bhejur amī militvā
translation: “Rising from His bed, Kṛṣṇa then sat gracefully upon a beautiful footstool that was illuminated by four kinds of jewels. Then, all the dāsas and dāsīs together began to serve Him.”

sanskrit:
tair āhitāṃ karatale vinidhāya dhārāṃ
karpūra-saurabhavatām aticāru-vārām
gaṇḍūṣa-puram upaklṛptas utthopajoṣaṃ
kṛṣṇaḥ śanair abhiṣiṣeca mukhābja-koṣam
translation: “As the young dāsas poured very fragrant, camphor-scented water into His cupped palms, Kṛṣṇa leisurely washed His lotus-bud face.”

sanskrit:
āmṛjya cāru-mṛdu-sūkṣma-balakṣa-vāsaḥ-
khaṇḍena pāṇi-vadanaṃ nirupādhi-hāsaḥ
tair āhitaṃ karatale mṛdu danta-kāṣṭhaṃ
pratyagrahīn mradimaniṣṭham atho laghiṣṭham
translation: “After drying His face and hands with a soft, fine piece of white cloth, Kṛṣṇa, smiling brightly, accepted a light and supple tooth-brushing twig from the servants.”

sanskrit:
kalpa-drumasya mṛdunā viṭapena tena
ratnāṅgulīyaka-mahobhir alaṅkṛtena
dantāvaliṃ vihita-vīkṣaka-netra-harṣam
ālola-kuṇḍala-yugaṃ śanakair jagharṣa
translation: “With that soft kalpa-druma twig, He began to gently brush His teeth, which were painted with the luster from His jeweled ring. His earrings swung back and forth as He brushed, and the eyes of all who watched were filled with joy.”

sanskrit:
aṅguṣṭha-tarjanikayor dhṛtayā vitastyā
jihvā-vilekhanikayā maṇi-hemamayyā
rājan maṇīndra-valayaṃ vyalikhan manojñāṃ
A tree that fulfills all desires
tāmbūla-rāga-parabhāgavatīṃ rasa-jñām
translation: “With His thumbs and forefingers, Kṛṣṇa held the two ends of His jeweled, golden tongue-scraper and began to clean His tongue, which was reddened by the tāmbūla He’d been chewing. On His wrist, He wore a beautiful diamond bracelet that shone brilliantly.”

sanskrit:
bhūyaḥ payobhir amalair vadanaṃ nineja
bhūyo mamārja ca kadāpi na codviveja
śrī-darpaṇaṃ kṛta-samarpaṇa-cañcalākṣi-
lakṣmyā cakāra mukha-dhāvana-śuddhi-sākṣi
translation: “Then Kṛṣṇa again calmly washed His face with pure water and dried it. With a glance from His restless eyes, He caused the elegant mirror before Him to bear witness to all this.”

sanskrit:
māṇikya-kaṅkatikayā kara-padma-koṣaṃ
samprāptayā valaya-kaṅkati-cāru-ghoṣam
keśa-prasādhanam athānabhisandhi-hāsī-
bhūtānanā vyadhita kāpi kumāra-dāsī
translation: “Holding a ruby-inlaid comb with her lotus-bud hand, one smiling dāsī began to selflessly dress Kṛṣṇa’s hair. The comb and her bangle jingled sweetly together as she moved her hand.”

sanskrit:
naktantanaṃ vasanam asya nirāsya kaścid-
vāso ’ntaraṃ suparidhāpya kalā-vipaścit
uṣṇīṣa-bandham atha mūrdhni babandha pādau
prakṣālya vārbhir abhimṛjya ca vāsarādau
translation: “As the day began, one servant who was very expert in the fine arts removed Kṛṣṇa’s nightclothes and helped Him put on some fresh ones. He then washed and dried Kṛṣṇa’s feet and carefully wrapped a turban around His head.”

sanskrit:
gā dogdhum uddhura-dhiyo ’pi vṛthodyamās te
gopā babhūvur atha tarṇaka-maṇḍalāś ca
cūṣanta eva na payaḥ kaṇa-mātram āsām
āpīnato ’dya yad avāpurato viṣeduḥ
translation: “Meanwhile, one of the cowherd men arrived and said, ‘O Prince, the skillful gopas have been unable to milk the cows, and the calves have become depressed because they can’t suck even a drop of milk from their mothers’ teats.’”

sanskrit:
gāvas tavādhvani dhṛtāśru-bhṛtākṣi-yugmā
na prasravanty apagatān na lihanti vatsān
hambādhvani-dhvanita-dig-valayā vilambaṃ
soḍhuṃ darāpi na hi samprati śaknuvanti
translation: ‘With tearful eyes, the cows all look toward Your pathway. They neither allow their milk to flow nor lick their nearby calves. They moo loudly in all directions, unable to bear waiting a moment longer for You to arrive.’

sanskrit:
ity eva kenacid upetya sa goduhokto
mātṛr nijāsya-dara-hāsya-sudhābhiṣekaiḥ
svānanda-śaṃsibhir asau sukhayan mukhābjaṃ
tāmbūla-rañjitam alaṃ kalayann udasthāt
translation: “Hearing the cowherd man speak like this, Kṛṣṇa was filled with joy and showered His mothers with the nectar of His smiling face, making them all very happy. Finishing the tāmbūla He was chewing, Kṛṣṇa then got up to leave.”

sanskrit:
dohaṃ samāpya balabhadra! sahānujas tvaṃ
mallājiraṃ vrajasi cet kuru mā vilambam
nirmañcanaṃ tava bhaje kṣaṇa-mātreva
sārdhaṃ vihṛtya sakhibhir drutam ehi bhoktum
translation: “Mother Yaśodā said to Balabhadra, ‘O Balarāma, after milking the cows, if You go to the wrestling place with Your younger brother, don’t stay there too long. I’ll do Your pūjā, but after playing for a short while with Your friends, You come on home to eat.’”

sanskrit:
śrutveti mātṛ-giram āha harir na mātaḥ
pratyeṣi māṃ yad amum eva vadasy athaivam
śiṣṭo ’graṇīḥ punar amīṣv aham eka eva
no ced amuṣya vaśatāṃ kim uri kariṣye?
translation: “Kṛṣṇa argued, ‘Mā, you just don’t trust Me. You’re talking to My older brother but saying nothing to Me. Among our friends I am the most well-behaved, so why should I have to do what Balarāma says?’”

sanskrit:
śiṣṭo yathā tvam asi vatsa! nijātibālyam
ārabhya tat khalu vidanty akhilāḥ purandhryaḥ
yāḥ svālayāpacaya-vedanayā purāsāṃ
phut-kartum āpur iha no katidheti soce
translation: “Mother Yaśodā retorted, ‘My child! From Your infancy all the Vraja housewives have known about Your so-called good behavior. Many, many times they came to yell at me about Your conduct in their homes.’”

sanskrit:
saudāminī-tati-vibhā-jayi-dāmanī-dyud
vibhrāji-savya-kara-korakitāravindaḥ
sa grāhita-pramita-kānaka-dohanīko
mātrā tayā sakhi! rayād adhikaṃ vireje
translation: “Yaśodā Mā then quickly placed a small golden milking pot in Kṛṣṇa’s right hand, and in His left, a shining rope for tying the hind legs of the cows while milking. O Sakhī Rādhā! Kṛṣṇa then looked even more beautiful than before.”

sanskrit:
stambe-rama-vraja-viḍambi-vilambi-pāda-
vinyāsa-jhañjhana-jhaṇat-kṛta-kiṅkiṇīkaḥ
lolālakāli-maṇi-kuṇḍala-kānti-veṇī-
vīcī-bhara-snapita-vaktra-sudhāṃśu-bimbaḥ
translation: “Kṛṣṇa’s ankle bells jingled sweetly as He slowly walked, like a drunken elephant, toward the cow shed. The dark blue Yamunā of His curling locks joined with the whitish Gaṅgā of His diamond earrings to bathe Kṛṣṇa’s moonlike face with waves of their beauty.”

sanskrit:
pītottarīya-capalelita-keli-nṛtya-
rājad-ghanāṅga-kiraṇocchalanocchrita-śrīḥ
preṅkhola-hāra-paridhi-śrita-kaustubhodyad-
bhānuḥ svanac-caraṇa-bhūṣaṇa-cumbi-dāmā
translation: “As Kṛṣṇa’s yellow cloth moved to and fro upon His dark chest, it appeared as though a bolt of lightning were dancing playfully upon a beautiful new raincloud. His swinging pearl necklace surrounded the kaustubha jewel upon His chest just as a halo encircles the rising sun. The garland of forest flowers round His neck reached down to kiss His jingling ankle bells again and again.”

sanskrit:
niṣkramya ramya-purataḥ purato ’bhigacchan
yacchan mudaṃ svajananī-jana-locanebhyaḥ
dāsaiḥ pradhāritam avārita-rocir aśnaṃ
tāmbūla-pulakam avāpa sa gopurāgram
translation: “In this way, as Kṛṣṇa left His own pleasant home, He filled the eyes of His mother and everyone present with great joy. Chewing some tāmbūla given by the servants, He soon reached the town gate.”

sanskrit:
tad-bāhya-kuṭṭima-taṭīm avalambamānaḥ
kā kutra kiṃ kuruta ity anusandadhānaḥ
vyāpārayan nayanam aṭṭa-ghaṭāsu narma-
preṣṭhair miladbhir abhitaḥ sa rarāja mitraiḥ
translation: “Kṛṣṇa rested on the edge of a terrace just outside the gate, looking very handsome as He sat amongst His best friends. His eyes wandered from building to building as He wondered, ‘Where is such-and-such girl? What is she doing now?’”

sanskrit:
tan nirmitānupada-karṇa-kathā-rasajña-
syāsyāmbuje kim api yat-smitam udbabhūva
tasyārtha-jātam api kiṃ vivarītum īśe
ceto ’lir eva tava sakhy anusandadhātu
translation: “Then, as each of His other friends arrived, they whispered secrets into His ears, and as He listened closely to each one, a smile appeared upon His lotus face. Sakhī, I’m not able to tell You what they said; You’ll have to let Your beelike mind figure that out.” 75

sanskrit:
uṣṇīṣa-vakrima-mahāmadhurimṇi tasya
tātkālike kila na kasya mano nyamāṅkṣīt
tatraiva śekharita-kānaka-sūtra-jāla-
rājan-maṇi-dyuti-bharāḥ kim u varṇanīyāḥ
translation: “While Kṛṣṇa was chewing the tāmbūla and listening in great delight to His friends’ whispers, His turban tilted a little to the side. When the vraja-gopīs saw that, they all sank into His ocean of sweetness and forgot everything else. Upon that turban a net of golden threads had been artistically arrayed and the jewels upon it shone brilliantly. Who can describe such beauty?”

sanskrit:
taiḥ saurabhaiḥ prasṛmarair anu nūpurādi-
dhvānair balena valabhīm adhirohitābhiḥ
gośāla-vartmani calal lalanāvalībhir
netrāmbujaiḥ sa katidhā nahi pūjyate sma
translation: “As Kṛṣṇa walked toward the cow shed, the sound of His jingling ankle bells and the aroma of His body spread everywhere, pulling by force all the girls from their housework and making them climb atop their roofs, where they worshipped Him again and again with their lotus eyes.”

sanskrit:
tat-tad-vilāsa-balitā suṣamā-rasālā
preṣṭhasya sā madhurikā pariveśyamānā
vaiśleṣika-jvaram aśīśamad apy athāsyās
tene ca taṃ śata-guṇaṃ tṛṣam edhayantī
translation: In other words, the boys were reminding Kṛṣṇa of His pastimes with Rādhā, and as He remembered each in detail, a smile came across His face. Rādhā would have to figure out for Herself what those secrets were. In this way, Madhurikā somewhat soothed Rādhā’s burning heart by serving Her the rasālā76 of Kṛṣṇa’s sweet pastimes with His friends. But after a short while, Śrīmatī’s anguish returned a hundred times greater.

sanskrit:
harṣonnatiḥ stimitatāṃ śravasor vyatānīt
tarṣottha-saṃjvarabharas tu dṛśor viveśa
ākasmikī nirupamā prativeśi-sampat
tāpaṃ tanoti sahavāsa-bhṛtāṃ sadaiva
translation: Even though Her ears were calmed and filled with joy, the burning fever of separation made its way into Her eyes. When a neighbor unexpectedly gains great wealth, it always causes pain to those living nearby.

sanskrit:
prāhānurāga-parabhāgavatī tataḥ sā
tā eva cāru-mukhi! dhanyatamā ramaṇyaḥ
yāḥ khelayanti satataṃ sudṛśas tadīya-
lāvaṇya-keli-jaladhau kala-dhauta-gātryaḥ
translation: Then, with deep love, Śrīmatī said to Madhurikā, “O Cāru-mukhī! Those golden damsels whose beautiful minnowlike eyes always sport in the ocean of Śyāmasundara’s charming pastimes are indeed the most fortunate.”

sanskrit:
janmaiva hanta kim abhūn mama gokule ’smiṃs
tan mādhurīṃ na yad urī-kurute kadāpi
tat śyāmale ’ticapale hṛdi leśa-mātrī
no sambhaved iha bhave dhṛtir ity avehi
translation: In a sorrowful voice, Rādhā then said to Śyāmalā, “O Śyāmalā, why was I born in Gokula? I’m unable to at any time taste even a drop of Kṛṣṇa’s sweetness. Therefore I never feel any peace within My restless heart. Please try to fathom this.”

sanskrit:
śyāmāha yāmi! lalite! śṛṇu yāmi gehaṃ
sampraty amūṃ prati mamāstu girāṃ virāmaḥ
tvaṃ padminīṃ vraja-purandara-sadmanīmāṃ
kṛṣṇekṣaṇālini samarpaya baddha-tṛṣṇe
Understanding Rādhā’s deep love, Śyāmalā then said to Lalitā, “O sister, I’m going home
translation: now; my conversation with Rādhā is over for today. Take this padminī 78 to the king of Vraja’s home and place Her before that thirsty honeybee Kṛṣṇa.”

sanskrit:
atha nikhila-sakhīnāṃ svālibhiḥ snāpitānāṃ
dhṛta-samucita-vastrālaṅkṛtīnāṃ tatiḥ sā
mathita-śarad-udañcac-candrikā-sindhu-jātāṃ
śriyam api nija-pādāmbhoja-bhāsā vijigye
translation: Then Lalitā and the other sakhīs were bathed, dressed and ornamented by their maidservants. The luster of their lotus feet outshone even the Goddess of Fortune as she rose from the churning of the ocean, showered by the clear light of the autumnal moon.

sanskrit:
kācin maṇīndramayam āsanam ājahāra
śrī-pāda-pīṭham aparā tad adho dadhāra
kāpy ānayad vadana-dhāvana-bhājanāni
kāpy ādadhe daśana-śodhana-sādhanāni
One sakhī brought to Rādhā a seat inlaid with diamonds; another brought a beautiful foot-
translation: rest and placed it on the floor. Others brought vessels of water for washing Her face, along with the ingredients and implements for brushing Her teeth.

sanskrit:
utthāya talpa-talataḥ kanakāsana-sthā
nidrāvasāna-vigalan-niyata-vyavasthā
sā pāda-pīṭham adhi datta-padāravindā
babhrāja sat-parijanair vihitābhinandā
translation: Śrīmatī then rose from bed and sat upon a golden seat. Because She had just awakened, Her clothing and hair were disheveled. When She placed Her lotus feet upon the foot-rest, all Her friends were delighted by such a beautiful sight.

sanskrit:
bhṛṅgāra-nāla-śikhareṇa samarpitābhiḥ
sandhāya vaktra-vivare culukī-kṛtābhiḥ
tat-saurabhasya rabhasādhika-saurabhābhiḥ
śrī-pāṇi-padma-tala-saṅgama-lohitābhiḥ
nikṣepaṇe priya-sakhī-karayoḥ kṛtābhiḥ
karpūra-pūra-rajasā ’bhisuvāsitābhiḥ!
vyāptālibhiḥ sakala-keli-kalā-suhṛdbhiḥ
sā sādhu śodhitavatī mukha-padmamadbhiḥ
translation: From a golden pitcher, Rādhā’s lotus-faced sakhīs, who are very helpful in the amorous arts, then poured water perfumed with camphor into Her hands, where it assumed a slightly reddish color. She then rinsed Her mouth with the water, increasing its fragrance by Her touch.

sanskrit:
kara-talād asakṛc-culukī-kṛtaṃ
salilam ā-rada-tālv anu cālitam
cala-kapola-yugonnati-mañjula-
dhvani-bhṛtaṃ nibhṛtaṃ kṣipati sma sā
translation: Taking sip after sip of water from Her palm, Rādhikā swished it around between Her teeth and palate. As She did this, Her cheeks puffed out a bit and a soft, sweet sound came from Her mouth. Then She carefully spat the rinse water into a golden pot.

sanskrit:
visṛmarān alakān kiratī śirasy
upari savya-karāṅguli-ghaṭṭanaiḥ
alika-gaṇḍa-dṛg-ādy atha sāmita-
dyutim itaṃ timitaṃ trir adīdhavat
translation: As Rādhā began to cleanse Her lotus face, some locks of hair fell across Her forehead. With the fingers of Her left hand, She pushed the curls back atop Her head and washed Her forehead, cheeks and eyes three times, making Herself even more radiant than before.

sanskrit:
viṭapikāṃ dyutaros tata-rociṣaṃ
rada-hitāṃ nihitāṃ sva-vayasyayā
mukulitāmbujatāṃ bhajatāñjasā
mṛdutareṇa kareṇa sudṛg dadhe
translation: One of Śrīmatī’s girlfriends offered Her a lustrous kalpa-vṛkṣa twig to use as a toothbrush. Accepting it in Her soft, lotus-bud hand, She began to brush Her teeth.

sanskrit:
pratisarodita-dolanam asvanad-
valayam uccala-kuṇḍalam etayā
vyadhita sā mṛjatī radanāṃś chaviṃ
kaṇavad ucchalitāṃ lalitāṃ śritān
translation: As Rādhā brushed, Her teeth sparkled beautifully. The pratisara on Her hand dangled and Her earrings swayed back and forth. Despite the rapid movement of Her hand, somehow Her bangles remained silent.

sanskrit:
atha dadhe sudatī dhanur-ākṛtiṃ
maṇimayīṃ rasanā-pariṇejinīm
mṛdula-pāṇi-yugāṅguli-yugmakāṃ
sahacarī-karato ’dara-toṣataḥ
translation: Another sakhī offered Her a jeweled, bow-shaped tongue scraper, the ends of which She held between the thumbs and forefingers of Her soft hands.

sanskrit:
navadalopamitāṃ rasanāṃ mṛjaty
atha tayā nata-kampita-mastakam
mukham iyaṃ skhalitair alakair vṛtaṃ
vidadhatī dadhatī smitam ābabhau
translation: She began to clean Her delicate tongue, which resembles a tender new lotus leaf. Because Her head was bowed slightly and shaking somewhat, locks of hair fell across Her face. Seeing Her sakhīs smiling at this, Śrīmatī also began to smile.

sanskrit:
niraṇijad bahir-antaram apy araṃ
mukha-vidhor atha dhauta-kara-dvayā
parijanārpita-mañjula-vāsasā
jala-kaṇāpanayaṃ sanayaṃ vyadhāt
translation: After rinsing Her moonlike face and mouth several times, Rādhā then washed Her hands. With a soft, fine cloth given to Her by a sakhī, She dried the remaining drops of water from Her face.

sanskrit:
sahacarī-vidhṛte maṇi-darpaṇe
tad-abhinandana-sākṣiṇi vīkṣya sā
smita-sudhābhir adhāvayad ānanaṃ
priyatama-kṣaṇa-lakṣaṇa-lakṣakam
translation: Another sakhī then held a jeweled mirror before Rādhā, and when She saw that Her incomparable beauty would be a festival for Kṛṣṇa’s eyes, Her face was again washed with the ambrosia of Her smile.

sanskrit:
gopālo ’pi svagośālaṃ
sarāma-madhumaṅgalaḥ
sakāvya-gīṣpatiḥ sāyaṃ
śaśī-vāmbaram āviśat
translation: “Just as Candra rises in the evening sky along with Śukra and Bṛhaspati, in the same way, Kṛṣṇacandra entered His cowshed with Balarāma and Madhumaṅgala.”

sanskrit:
dadhāra dyuṣadāṃ rāmo
dhavalāvali-veṣṭitaḥ
kailāsa-gaṇḍa-śailālī-
madhyasthairāvata-bhramam
translation: “When I saw Balarāma there, surrounded by many white cows, for a moment it appeared that the elephant Airāvata was standing among boulders fallen from Mount Kailāsa.”81

sanskrit:
madhye ’cyuto ’ñcan dhavalāvalīnām
udānanānāṃ paritaḥ sthitānām
dadhau janānāṃ sphūṭa-puṇḍarīka-
śreṇy-antar-añcad-bhramara-bhramaṃ saḥ
translation: “And when everyone saw Kṛṣṇa surrounded by the cows, with their heads raised high, they assumed He was a black bee sporting amongst a cluster of blooming white lotuses.”

sanskrit:
hihī gaṅge! godāvari! śabali! kālindi! dhavale!
hihī dhūmre! tūṅgi! bhramari! yamune! haṃsi! kamale!
hihī rambhe! campe! kariṇi! hariṇīti vraja-vidhur
muhur nāma-grāhaṃ nikhila-surabhīr āhvayad asau
translation: “One by one, Kṛṣṇa joyfully called each cow by name: ‘Hey Gaṅgā! Godāvarī! Śabalī! Kālindī! Dhavalā! Hey Dhūmrā! Tūṅgī! Bhramarī! Yamunā! Haṃsī! Kamalā! How are you Rambhā, Campā, Kariṇī and Hariṇī?’”

sanskrit:
nyastāṅgaḥ prapadopari praghaṭayan jānu-dvaye dohanīṃ
kāścid dogdhi payaḥ svayaṃ tv atha parāḥ svair dohayaty unmukhīḥ
anyāḥ pāyayati svatarṇaka-gaṇān kaṇḍūyanaiḥ prīṇayann
itthaṃ nanda-sutaḥ prage svasurabhīr ānandayan nandati
translation: “Squatting so His body weight rested upon the balls of His feet, Kṛṣṇa placed a milk pail between His knees and personally milked some of the cows, while His gopa friends milked others. He affectionately scratched and petted some cows, giving them great delight, encouraging them to nurse their calves. By giving joy to the cows, Kṛṣṇa also felt great happiness.”

sanskrit:
pādāgre kṛta-pādukaṃ trika-samullāsollasat-pārṣṇikaṃ
madhye nyasya ghaṭīṃ paṭonnam anataḥ prodyat tviṣor jānunoḥ
gotunda-vyatiṣaṅga-sundara-dara-kṣobha-ślathoṣṇīṣakaṃ
pāṇibhyāṃ krama-kuḍmalāṅguli-puṭaṃ gāṃ dogdhi dugdhaṃ hariḥ
translation: “Sitting balanced on His toes, heels upward, with a milk pail between His feet, Kṛṣṇa milked the cows with His lotus-bud fingers. His yellow cloth was pulled up somewhat, exposing His beautiful knees. Because of bumping His head against the bellies of the cows, His turban had become loosened and fallen off.”

sanskrit:
vatsād apy adhika-priyo bhagavataḥ pāṇy-ambuja-sparśana-
sneha-srāvi-payaḥ-payodhara-puṭā gaur duhyamānā svayam
dhārābhiḥ sugabhīra-ghoṣa-gahanam āpūrya sā dohanīṃ
dohany antaram eti yāvad avanīṃ tāvat samāpupluvat
translation: “When a cow’s udder was touched by the hands of Kṛṣṇa, who is even more precious to her than her own calf, out of affection milk began to spontaneously flow from her teats. Her milk sprayed into bucket after bucket with a deep, low-pitched sound, overflowing and drenching the earth beneath.”

sanskrit:
aṅguṣṭhāgrima-yantritāṅgulir asau pādārddha-nīruddha-bhūr
āpīnāñcala-mardayann iha puro dvitraiḥ payo-bindhubhiḥ
nyag-jānu-dvaya-madhya-yantrita-ghaṭī-vaktrāntare praskhalad-
dhārā-dhvāna-manoharaṃ sakhi! payo gāṃ dogdhi dāmodaraḥ
translation: “Hey Sakhī! As Dāmodara sat with only the front half of His feet on the ground, a milk pot placed between His knees, He moistened the cow’s udder with two or three drops of milk from her teats. Then, grasping those teats with His thumbs and other fingers, He began to milk, the stream creating a pleasant sound as it struck the pot.”

sanskrit:
tatra kāñcanamaye mṛdu-pīṭhe
cīna-cela-pihite viniviṣṭām
sevane parijanā nipuṇā drāk
tām upāyana-karāḥ parivavruḥ
translation: Then Rādhā sat upon a golden seat covered with a soft, fine cloth. Her sakhīs, who are very expert in sevā, gathered round, holding bottles of oil and other articles for Her bath.

sanskrit:
sāvātārayad-ābharaṇa-nicayaṃ
lalitā svasakhī-tanutaḥ sadayam
kanaka-vratater iva sapraṇayaṃ
pallava-kusuma-stavaka-pracayam
translation: As Lalitā removed the ornaments from Rādhā’s body, it appeared as though she were gathering delicate leaves and flowers from a beautiful golden creeper.

sanskrit:
āmṛjya cela-śakalena tanūttamena
sarvāṅgam aṅkitam anaṅga-raṇāṅkakena
abhyaṅga-saṅgi-vasanaṃ paridhāpya naktaṃ
vāso ’bhyamūmucad anuttama-gandha-yuktam
translation: With a piece of fine cloth, Lalitā cleaned from Rādhā’s body all the marks left from Cupid’s battle. Then she had Her remove Her sweet-smelling nightclothes and put on a garment to cover Her while being massaged with oil.

sanskrit:
ākṛṣya mugdham avaguṇṭhanam uttamāṅgād
unmocya kuntala-tatīḥ sughanottamāṅgāḥ
ratna-prasādhanikayā cala-kaṅkaṇāliḥ
saprema sādaram aśūśudhad uttamāliḥ
translation: Another dear sakhī removed the veil from Rādhā’s head and loosened Her glistening black hair. As the bangles on her arms jingled together, the sakhī began to affectionately arrange Śrīmatī’s tresses with a jeweled comb.

sanskrit:
prakṣālya pāda-yugalaṃ mukuraṃ purastād
ādarśya kācana kalā-kuśalatva-śastā
tailena satsurabhiṇā lasatāruṇimnā-
bhyānañja kañja-vadanāṃ praṇayena bhūmnā
translation: After washing Śrīmatī’s feet, one skillful sakhī placed a mirror before Her lotus face, and with a sweetly fragrant reddish oil, lovingly massaged Her body.

sanskrit:
aṅgād yato yata udasyati cāru-celaṃ
tat-tan-nirīkṣya hriyam ṛcchati sānuvelam
tenāktam aktam avadhāya sakhīyam aṅgaṃ
tasyāḥ pyadhāt tad-akhilaṃ kṛta-hrī-vibhaṅgam
translation: Whenever the sakhī would see a part of Rādhā’s beautiful form after removing some clothing, she would sometimes become bashful. Therefore, after rubbing that part of Śrīmatī’s body with oil, the sakhī would then immediately cover it.

sanskrit:
abhyajya rajyad-atiśuddha-hṛdo vayasyā
āpāda-mūrdha-kṛta-mardanam aṅgam asyāḥ
udvartanaṃ vidadhire ghanasāra-pūrṇaiḥ
kastūrikā-ghusṛṇa-candana-cāru-cūrṇaiḥ
translation: After rubbing Rādhā’s body with oil, Her affectionate, pure-hearted girlfriends massaged Her from head to toe and then anointed Her with a beautiful powder composed of camphor mixed with musk, saffron and sandalwood.

sanskrit:
gandhānubandhi-vimalāmalakī-kaṣāyaiḥ
keśān vighṛṣya katamā vividhair upāyaiḥ
bhṛṅgāra-nāla-galitair lalitaiḥ kabandhair
ukṣāṃ cakāra sahaja-praṇayānubandhaiḥ
translation: Then one sakhī rubbed pure, fragrant āmalakī82 juice into Śrīmatī’s locks of hair for cleansing, and after that, she affectionately bathed Her with a gentle stream of water poured from a golden pitcher.

sanskrit:
kālocitena ghanasāra-suvāsitena
nānā-maṇīśvara-ghaṭī-ghaṭayā bhṛtena
dvābhyāṃ śanair ubhayataḥ pratipāditena
dve pārśvayoḥ siṣicatuḥ sumukhīṃ jalena
translation: Lalitā and Viśākhā stood on each side of Sumukhī Rādhā83 and slowly bathed Her with camphor-scented water (which was the appropriate temperature) from pots inlaid with rows of diamonds.

sanskrit:
saṃveṣṭya cāru-cikurān sicayena bāḍhaṃ
niṣpīḍya bhūri galad-ambu nigālya gāḍham
Emblic myrobalan
Rādhā with the beautiful face
bhūyaḥ prasārya calad-aṅgulibhir vikīrya
bhūyo babandha katamā sicayaṃ vitīrya
translation: Another sakhī wrapped Śrīmatī’s beautiful tresses with a cloth and squeezed out the excess water. Then she removed the cloth, and after spreading Rādhā’s hair out with her fingers, she wrapped it once again.

sanskrit:
kācin mukhendum aparā gala-mūlam anyā
karṇau mamārja mṛdunā vasanena dhanyā
vakṣo visāri katamā katamā ca pṛṣṭhaṃ
bāhu-dvayaṃ ca katamā suṣamā-variṣṭham
One fortunate sakhī rubbed Rādhikā’s moonlike face with a soft cloth, while others dried
translation: Her neck and ears. Other sakhīs did the same with Her plump breasts, beautiful back and lovely arms.

sanskrit:
saṃveṣṭya śuṣka-vasanena nirāsanīyaṃ
śroṇyā jahāra vigalaj-jalam antarīyam
āmṛjya pāṇi-yugalena śanair udāram
arddhorukaṃ kaṭi-taṭe ghaṭayāṃ cakāra
Someone else wrapped a dry cloth around Śrīmatī’s hips and removed Her wet
translation: undergarment. After drying Rādhā’s hips completely by gently rubbing the cloth with her hands, the sakhī then replaced it with a charming petticoat.

sanskrit:
āmṛṣṭayor vara-payodharayor alolaṃ
kācit kalāsu kuśalātha babandha colam
paṭṭāṃśukena racitaṃ sva-sakhī-janena
nānā-vidhātiśaya-śilpa-viśāradena
translation: When Rādhikā’s splendid breasts had been dried, another talented sakhī carefully tied around them a fine silk bodice that had been crafted by some of Her other artistic girlfriends.

sanskrit:
tasyopari pratanu śoṇataraṃ suvīci-
caṇḍātakād udayad uccala-sanmarīci
śrī-pāda-padma-nakha-candra-cayāgra-cumbi
celaṃ babandha tapanīya-guṇānubandhi
translation: Śrīmatī’s delicate, crimson, ruffled petticoat was effulgent like the sun. Upon that She donned a golden-threaded dress that kissed the tips of the toes on Her lotus feet.

sanskrit:
lamba-pralamba-yugalena supaṭṭa-dāmnā
muktā-maṇīndra-mahasā vilasad-garimṇā
ākuñcana-krama-vaśāt kamalānukārāṃ
jagrantha nīvim abhinābhi suśilpa-sārām
translation: Then someone tied around Her waist a beautiful silk cloth adorned with two pendants made of sparkling pearls and diamonds. Drawn together in places, its shape resembled that of a lotus flower.

sanskrit:
kanaka-bindumatī nava-śāṭikā
ghana-rucis tad-upary atididyute
yad-abhiveṣṭanam eva mukunda-dṛṅ
niranurodhana-rodhanam ucyate
translation: A fine cloth the color of clouds sprinkled with particles of gold was then wrapped around Her just to capture Mukunda’s roaming glance.

sanskrit:
ārohya tām atha mahāmaṇi-pīṭha-pṛṣṭhe
vistāritātimṛdu-cela-kṛta-pratiṣṭhe
prakṣālya pāda-kamala-dvitayaṃ satoṣāḥ
sakhyo vyadhur vividha-maṅgala-veṣa-bhūṣāḥ
translation: The sakhīs then sat Rādhā upon a jeweled seat covered with a soft cloth. After happily washing Her feet, they adorned Her with various kinds of auspicious ornaments.

sanskrit:
bhūyaḥ prasārya bahuśo bahuśaḥ prasādhya
ratna-prasādha-nikayāṅgulibhir viśodhya
kālāguru-prabhava-dhūpa-dhurā-pracāram
ālī-janaḥ kaca-bharaṃ surabhī-cakāra
translation: Then, with their fingers and jeweled combs, the girls repeatedly spread Rādhā’s tresses and perfumed them with the smoke of incense made from black sandalwood.

sanskrit:
snānād ṛjuṃ sad-alakālim arālayitvā
kastūrikābhir alike tilakaṃ likhitvā
sindūra-bindu-rucire ’kṛta bālapāśyāṃ
sīmanta-sīmani maṇīndra-mayūkha-rasyām
translation: After Her bath, Śrīmatī’s hair had become straight, so the sakhīs curled it once again. Then someone painted charming musk tilaka upon Her forehead and vermilion in the part of Her hair. Upon that someone placed a beautiful ornament, effulgent with the splendor of diamonds.

sanskrit:
kastūrī-patravallī-samudaya-khacitaṃ pārśvayor ākapolaṃ
bhāle śrīkhaṇḍa-bindūtkara-vṛtam abhitaḥ kāma-yantrābhidhānam
antaḥ kastūrikodyan-malayaja-śaśabhṛl-lekhayādhaścitaṃ sā
cakre sīmanta-rekhānvitam atha tilakaṃ sāndra-sindūra-paṅkaiḥ
translation: Along with the sīmantakam, Viśākhā painted upon Rādhikā’s forehead the tilaka known as kāma-yantra, consisting of a dot of vermilion paste above a star of musk and a candana crescent moon. Encircling these marks were dots of sandalwood paste. Extending on each side were tiny leaves of musk, arrayed around both eyes and onto Her cheeks.

sanskrit:
maulau babandha katamā sumaṇi-pravekaṃ
sanmālatī-kusuma-garbhaka-kānti-sekam
dhammillam ullasita-lohita-paṭṭa-dāmnā
lamba-pralamba-yugalena maṇīndra-dhāmnā
translation: Another sakhī tied upon Śrīmatī’s head a diamond bathed by the hue of a chaplet of fresh mālatī flowers. With a red silken string, she then bound Her hair into a bun, brightened by the sparkling diamond and two pendulant strings of pearls.

sanskrit:
sūkṣmordhva-randhra-gata-hema-śalākikāyā
mūlāgra-saṅga-lalite vidadhe sukāyā
śrī-cakrikā-bakulike śruti-madhya-deśe
ratna-prabhā-bhara-dhurā vihitopadeśe
translation: One sundarī87 then placed upon each of Rādhā’s ears a beautiful ornament made of a large circular pin fastened to a small golden pin piercing the middle of Her ear. The colorful precious jewels upon this charming ornament sparkled brightly.

sanskrit:
muktākalāpa-kalayā lalita-prakāśyāṃ
kācid vyadhād alaka-sīmani patrapāśyām
kācin maṇīndramaya-kuṇḍalam atyudāram
ekaikaśaḥ śruti-yuge ghaṭayāṃ cakāra
translation: Another sakhī then placed a radiant and artistically crafted ornament on Rādhā’s forehead just below the edge of Her hair. Someone else then placed an elegant diamond earring upon each of Her lovely ears.

sanskrit:
kācid vibhūṣya nayane dalitāñjanena
smārau śarāv iva nighṛṣṭa-rasāñjanena
nāsāpasavya-puṭake vitatāra muktāṃ
netrāñjanādhara-vibhā-bhara-nīla-raktām
translation: A line of red vermilion painted in the part of a woman’s hair. Sandalwood paste The Sanskrit word for this is dhammilla, meaning ‘the braided and ornamented hair of a woman tied over the head and intermixed with flowers, pearls, etc.’ A beautiful girl Śrīmatī’s eyes, decorated with a mixture of ground collyrium and rasāñjana, appeared just like a pair of Cupid’s arrows. In Her right nostril was fastened a single pearl, tinted with the red and blue reflections of Her lips and eye cosmetic.

sanskrit:
makarike likhatī mṛdu-gaṇḍayor
makara-ketanam āhvayad eva sā
yam adharāruṇa-pallavam arpayan
rasamaye samaye harir arcayet
translation: After that, Lalitā Sakhī painted pictures of dolphins upon Rādhikā’s soft cheeks, as if to invite Cupid by saying, “Hey Kandarpa, please come and sit upon this altar. If you do this, at some romantic time Śrī Hari will worship you by offering His reddish, lotus-bud lips.”

sanskrit:
rucira-cibuka-madhye ratna-rājac-chalākā-
kalita-kara-viśākhā-nirmito ’syāś cakāsti
nava-mṛga-mada-binduḥ śobhayan śrī-mukhenduṃ
bhramara iva dalāgre sanniviṣṭaḥ sarojam
translation: With a jeweled pencil in hand, Viśākhā carefully painted a dot of musk on the middle of Rādhā’s delicate chin, just like a bumblebee resting on the tip of a lotus leaf, making Her lovely moonlike face even more beautiful.

sanskrit:
karpūrāguru-kāśmīra-
paṅka-miśrita-candanaiḥ
samālipya viśākhā ’syāḥ
pṛṣṭhaṃ bāhu-kucāv uraḥ
translation: Then she smeared a mixture of camphor, aguru, saffron and sandalwood paste upon Śrīmatī’s back, arms, breasts and chest.

sanskrit:
puṣpa-gucchendulekhābja-
makarī-cūta-pallavam
lilekha citraṃ kastūryā
citrā tat-kucayos taṭe
translation: On the slopes of Rādhā’s breasts, Citrā Sakhī painted, with musk, tiny pictures of flower clusters, crescent moons, lotuses, dolphins and mango leaves.

sanskrit:
mīnī-prasūna-nava-pallava-candralekhā-
Vitriol of copper
translation: Another name for Cupid, besides Kandarpa, is Makara-ketana, which means ‘one who has a dolphin (some call it a shark) as his emblem.’ A kind of fragrant wood vyājāt svacihna-śara-kunta-dhanūṃṣi kāmaḥ tad-bhrū-dhanur-dhuvana-mātra-nirasta-karmā manye nyadhatta nija-tat--kuca-koṣa-gehe It seemed as though simply by causing a slight movement of Rādhā’s bowlike eyebrows, Cupid, who has no other duty, had deposited his own symbols (a male dolphin, an arrow, a spear, and a bow) upon the treasure house of Rādhā’s breasts, only under the guise of female dolphins, flowers, leaves and crescent moons.

sanskrit:
citrārpitāneka-vicitra-ratna-
muktācitā rakta-dukūla-colī
kucau bha-jālendra-dhanur-vicitrā
tastāra śailāv iva sāndhya-kāntiḥ
translation: Just as the evening twilight, decorated with a rainbow and garland of stars, shrouds a pair of mountains, in the same way, a fine, scarlet bodice, adorned with precious jewels and pearls, and given by Citrā Sakhī, covered Śrīmatī’s charming pair of breasts.

sanskrit:
upari khacita-nānā-ratna-jālaiḥ sphuranta
vimala-puraṭa-patryā kaṇṭham asyā viśākhā
hari-kara-dara-cihna-śrī-haraṃ puṣkarākṣyāḥ
sapadi hari-bhiyeva chādayāmāsa madhye
vajrācitākhaṇḍala-ratna-citra-
susthūla-madhyo guṇa-baddha-cañcuḥ
lalāsa tasyā upakaṇṭha-kūpaṃ
dattas tayā hāṭaka-citra-haṃsaḥ
Viśākhā quickly placed upon the center of lotus-eyed Rādhā’s throat a lustrous ornament,
translation: bedecked with sparkling jewels and pure gold leaf, to cover the beauty-stealing mark left by the conch shell impressions on Hari’s hands. This large, golden swan, adorned with diamonds and sapphires, and bound by a thread tied through the beak, glittered brightly as it hung near the hollow of Her neck.

sanskrit:
suvarṇa-golī-yuga-madhyagollasan
masāra-golī-gilito ’ntarāntarā
susūkṣma-muktāvali-gumphitas tayā
nyayoji hāro hṛdi gostanābhidhaḥ
Upon Rādhikā’s bosom Viśākhā placed a necklace known as gostana. Interspersed here
translation: and there amongst the delicate pearls were small sapphire globes strung between pairs of small balls of lustrous gold.

sanskrit:
masāra-candropala-padmarāga-
suvarṇa-golī-grathitāntarālaiḥ
muktā-pravālaiḥ parigumphitāṃ sā
ratna-srajaṃ tad-dhṛdaye yuyoja
translation: She then placed upon Śrīmatī’s chest another necklace of sapphires, moonstones, rubies, golden orbs, pearls and coral.

sanskrit:
vaidūrya-yugmācita-hema-dhātrikā-
bījā-bha-golī-gilito ’ntarāntarā
vicitra-muktāvali-citra-gucchako
rarāja tasyā hṛdaye ’rpitas tayā
translation: Along with those necklaces, Viśākhā placed another necklace known as a gucchaka, which was made of elegant pearls, interspersed with golden globes that resembled āmalakī seeds, strung between pairs of lapis lazuli.

sanskrit:
rāse niśīthe saha-nṛtya-gāna-
tuṣṭena dattāṃ hariṇā svakaṇṭhāt
tasyaiva sākṣād iva rāja-lakṣmīṃ
guñjāvalīṃ tad-dhṛdi sā yuyoja
translation: During the night of rāsa-līlā, pleased by the gopīs’ singing and dancing, Hari had removed the necklace called guñjāvalī93 from His neck and given it as a gift to Śrīmatī. Viśākhā now placed that necklace, which was Kṛṣṇa’s royal treasure, upon Rādhā’s breasts.

sanskrit:
sthūla-tārāvalī-ramyā
san-nāyaka-vibhūṣitā
tasyā ekāvalī-jyotsnī
hṛd-ambaram amaṇḍayat
translation: Just as the evening sky is adorned with clusters of twinkling stars and the brilliant full moon, in the same way, Śrī Rādhā’s bosom was then bedecked with the ekāvalī necklace, strung with large, effulgent pearls and a resplendent pendant.

vibhūṣyamāṇā vṛṣabhānu-putrī
urogate nīlamaṇīndra-hāre

translation: When the sakhīs placed the necklace of sapphires upon Vṛṣabhānu-nandinī’s chest, She became very agitated, and trembling, perspiration and goose bumps appeared all over Her body.

sanskrit:
pṛṣṭhāntaḥ krama-lambamānam amalaṃ grīvānta-hārāvalī-
vīṭī-bandhana-paṭṭa-sūtra-camarī-jālaṃ tadāsyā babhau
manye cāru-nitamba-śailakaṭakān mūrdhnādhirohārthakaṃ
sopānaṃ vidhinā kṛtaṃ karuṇayā veṇī-bhujaṅgyāḥ sphuṭam
translation: At the bottom of Rādhā’s neck, all these beautiful necklaces were individually tied with silken threads of pure camarī, each bundle hanging in succession upon the other down the center of Her back. It seemed as though Lord Brahmā had created a staircase to allow Śrīmatī’s snakelike braid of hair to easily climb from Her sloping, mountain-like hips to the top of Her head.

sanskrit:
madhye-pragaṇḍam atulāṅgadam-unmaṇīni
madhye-prakoṣṭham atulāni ca kaṅkaṇāni
tat-sīmni kāpya-kṛta maṅgala-paṭṭa-sūtraṃ
ratna-prakāśi maṇi-bandha-rucāticitram
Another sakhī placed jeweled armlets midway upon Rādhikā’s upper arms and other
translation: jeweled bracelets midway upon Her forearms. Then, around Her wrist the sakhī tied a beautiful, multicolored “lucky thread,” spun of silk and illuminated by the jewels from Her bracelet.

sanskrit:
muktāvalī-khacita-hāṭaka-kaṅkaṇābhyāṃ
saṃveṣṭitaḥ sa valayāvali-sanniveśaḥ
bimbair-vidhor-milita-bhāskara-maṇḍalābhyāṃ
tasyāś cakāsti nitarām iva saiṃhikeyaḥ
The sapphire bracelets inserted between bracelets of pearl-inlaid gold looked just like
translation: Rāhu seated between the sun and the moon.

sanskrit:
nija-nāmāṅkitā nānā-
ratna-dyuti-karambitā
Listed as verse 5.359 in Purīdāsa edition
Yak tail
babhāv aṅguli-mudrāsyā
vipakṣa-mada-mardanī
translation: A splendorous jeweled ring with the name “Rādhā” engraved upon it was then placed upon Her finger. This ring was so beautiful that it crushed the pride of all of Śrīmatī’s female rivals.

sanskrit:
tundāntike maṇi-vinirmita-tunda-bandhaṃ
kāñcī-guṇaṃ ca tad adho maṇi-vṛnda-bandham
pādāṅgulīṣu vara-ratnamayormikālīm
ā-gulpham ādhṛta suhaṃsaka-yugmam ālī
Around Rādhikā’s waist one sakhī tied a beautiful jeweled sash, and below that a slender
translation: cord also decorated with jewels. On Her toes she placed precious toe-rings, and on Her ankles, splendid ornaments called haṃsakas.

sanskrit:
nakha-śikhāṅghritalādy uru-śoṇimā-
py ahaha yāvaka-rañjitatām agāt
bhavati kiṃ dara-dīpaja-rociṣā
dina-kṛto na kṛto manujair mahaḥ
translation: Although the nail-tips and soles of Śrīmatī’s feet are already a very reddish color, the sakhīs still painted them with red lac. “Why?” you ask. But is it not true that people worship the effulgent sun by offering a tiny lamp?

sanskrit:
vṛthā ’kṛthā yāvakam aṅghri-paṅkaje
sva eva rāgo ’sya dṛśāṃ rasāyanaḥ
kintv eka evāsti guṇo ’sya rādhike
yaḥ keśavasyāpi ca keśa-rañjanaḥ
translation: Another sakhī then said, “Ayi Rādhā! You’ve made them paint Your feet with red lac when their natural crimson glow is already the elixir for everyone’s eyes. Still, there is one interesting result of doing that: this lac becomes the dye for Keśava’s hair!”

sanskrit:
mañjīra-yugmam atimañjula-ratna-siddhaṃ
pādāmbujopari cakāra ca kāpi baddham
tat-tat-svaśilpa-kuśalatva-nidarśanāya
kācin maṇīndra-mukuraṃ purato nināya
translation: Then one sakhī tied elegant jewel-studded ankle bells on the upper part of Śrīmatī’s feet, while someone else brought a diamond mirror before Her so She could see each of the sakhīs’ fine artistry.

sanskrit:
asyā nyadhād uṣasi narmadayā svasakhyā
mālākṛtas tanujayopahṛtaṃ viśākhā
smerāravinda-vadanātha karāravinde
līlāravindam aravinda-vilocanāyāḥ
translation: After that, Viśākhā, smiling brightly, placed in Śrī Rādhā’s lotus hand a līlā-kamala brought earlier in the morning by Narmadā, the daughter of a garland maker.

sanskrit:
sā kṛṣṇa-netra-kutukocita-rūpa-veśaṃ
varṣmāvalokya mukure pratibimbitaṃ svam
kṛṣṇopasatti-taralāsa varāṅganānāṃ
kāntāvalokana-phalo hi viśeṣa-veṣaḥ
translation: When Śrīmatī saw Her reflected form in the mirror, Her body and dress decorated just to attract Kṛṣṇa’s eyes, She became restless to meet with Him. If a beautiful girl’s excellent dress and makeup are noticed by her lover, she attains success.

sanskrit:
godohanād atha viramya sa ramya-līlaiḥ
sārdhaṃ nija-priya-sakhaiḥ svasamāna-śīlaiḥ
abhyāyayau kutuka-malla-vilāsa-nityā-
bhyāsālayaṃ maṇimayaṃ sakalaikamatyā
translation: “When Kṛṣṇa and all His closest friends, who are similar in nature to Him, finished milking the cows, they all headed to the jewel-bedecked wrestling arena, eager to engage in their cherished daily pastime, joking and laughing all the way.”

sanskrit:
pratyekam eva sakhibhiḥ savayobhir etair
malla-kriyām atha bhujābhuji vīta-bhītaiḥ
svasvaujasaḥ prakaṭanena saroṣa-darpaiś
cakre ’pasarpa-parisarpa-visarpa-sarpaiḥ99
translation: A līlā-kamala is a lotus held in the hand as a plaything. Chant this śloka; it’s a fun one. :-) “Then Kṛṣṇa and His friends, all about the same age and all fearless, began to fight, hand to hand, arm to arm. With great displays of individual strength, anger and boasting, they wrestled with each other, sometimes jumping in front, sometimes attacking from the side, sometimes circling around, darting forward and back with amazing skill.”

sanskrit:
viśramya kiñcid atha sañcita-puṇya-vṛndais
tair eva kaiścana mahāguṇa-vṛkṣa-kandaiḥ
abhyañjanārtham anurañjana-mañju-hāsair
abhyaṅga-maṅgala-gṛhaṃ praviveśa dāsaiḥ
translation: “After resting for a short while, Kṛṣṇa and a few of His most fortunate and virtuous friends entered a house to be massaged with oil by His affectionate, sweetly-smiling servants.”

sanskrit:
nānā-prabandha-bahubandha-vidhau vidagdhair
abhyaṅga-maṅgala-viśeṣa-kalāsu mugdhaiḥ
tailena sādhu śubha-gandha-subāndhavena
prārambhi yat tad urarīkṛtam apy anena
translation: “Then these charming servants, who are very expert not only in the art of massage but also in the clever use of words, began to massage Kṛṣṇa with a very fragrant type of oil, which He gladly accepted.”

sanskrit:
āpāda-mastakam anasta-samasta-bhāgyais
tailena taiḥ priya-samāja-sabhāja-yogyaiḥ
nātiślathaṃ ca na dṛḍhaṃ ca sumaṅgalāni
prītyā ciraṃ mamṛdire ’tha tad aṅgakāni
translation: “For a long while, those fortunate and dear servant boys, who are worthy of praise, lovingly massaged Mādhava’s entire body from head to toe, always careful to rub neither too firmly nor too gently.”

sanskrit:
te kauṅkumena rajasā ghanasāra-cūrṇaiḥ
pūrṇena cāru-mṛdunā paripeṣa-śīrṇaiḥ
vimlāna-bhāvam atha taila-kṛtaṃ harantaḥ
kṛṣṇasya tān avayavān udavartayanta
translation: “After His fatigue had been dispelled by the oil massage, Kṛṣṇa was then massaged with a soft, finely ground mixture of fragrant saffron and camphor.”

sanskrit:
kenocitena ghanasāra-suvāsitena
nānāvidha-sphaṭika-hema-ghaṭī-bhṛtena!
keśān kaṣāya-kaṣitān kalayan kumāra-
dāsī-gaṇo ’mbuja-dṛśaṃ snāpayāṃ cakāra
translation: “Some of the young servant girls then washed lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa’s hair with a decoction of āmalakī and curds, after which they bathed Him with camphor-scented water poured from crystal and golden pots.”

sanskrit:
kācit kaṣāyita-kacān bahuśaḥ kaṣantī
kācin mṛdūn avayavān mṛdu mārjayantī
bhṛṅgārakeṇa katamā salilaṃ kirantī
lebhetarām atitarām anurāga-kāntī
translation: “One graceful and affectionate dāsī repeatedly squeezed the decoction from Kṛṣṇa’s hair with a piece of cloth; someone else rubbed His soft limbs with her gentle hands; and another girl poured water from a pitcher with a spout.”

sanskrit:
evaṃ samāpya katame snapanaṃ śubhena
śaṅkhodakena śirasi pratipāditena
aṅgoñchanāṃśukam anekam athopanīya
saṃmārjanaṃ vidadhur asya bhṛśaṃ vinīya
translation: “After that, some of the male servants completed Kṛṣṇa’s bath by pouring water upon His head from an auspicious conch shell, and then modestly dried His body with towels.”

sanskrit:
ādau sucela-śakalair mṛdulair aśuṣkaiḥ
paścāt krameṇa mamṛjuḥ sita-sūkṣma-śuṣkaiḥ
āpāda-kuntala-bharam pratisandhi-sandhi
te mārjanaṃ vidadhire praṇayānubandhi
translation: “First, they affectionately rubbed Him with soft, fine, moist pieces of cloth, and then afterward with delicate, white, dry pieces.”

sanskrit:
kaścit kacān gata-jalān dvividhena vāsaḥ-
khaṇḍena sādhu vidadhe mṛdu-manda-hāsaḥ
kaścit paṭuḥ kaṭitaṭād galad ambu-celaṃ
celāntareṇa vinināya kṛtāvahelam
translation: “Using both kinds of cloth, one gently smiling servant skillfully dried the water from Kṛṣṇa’s hair, while another easily replaced the wet towel on Mādhava’s hips with a dry one.”

sanskrit:
kenāpi nūtanam atitvarayopanītaṃ
kauṣeya-cela-yugalaṃ druta-hema-pītam
kenāpi pāṇi-kamale kramataḥ pradattam
utsārya pūrva-paṭam āśu sa paryadhatta
translation: “Then someone immediately brought two fresh yellow silken garments, the color of molten gold, and gave them to another servant who quickly placed them upon Kṛṣṇa’s body after removing the towel from His hips.”

sanskrit:
tasyāsthitasya ramaṇīya-maṇī-catuṣkaṃ
prakṣālitāṅghri-kamalasya lasad-vapuṣkam
paścād-gatena katamena kumāra-bhṛtye-
nāsevi kuntala-bharaḥ kuśalena kṛtye
translation: “After washing Kṛṣṇa’s feet, they sat Him upon a beautiful jeweled bench. Then one servant stood behind Him and began to expertly dress His locks of hair.”

sanskrit:
bhūyaḥ prasārya parimṛjya muhuḥ prasādhya
ratna-prasādhanikayā bahuśo viśodhya
āvṛtya cela-śakalena satā dviphāla-
baddhaḥ sa kuntala-bharaḥ prabhayā paphāla
translation: “Over and over, in various ways, the servant stroked and arranged Mādhava’s lustrous hair with a jeweled comb. Then he parted it and bound the halves with a strip of silken cloth.”

sanskrit:
anyonya-pālana-kṛtā kaca-mecakimnā
sūkṣmātisūkṣma-vasanasya ca pāṇḍarimṇā
nirmoka-moka-parabhogi-nibho ’sya keśa-
vinyāsa eṣa na hi kasya dṛśor viveśa
translation: “The rich blackness of His hair and whiteness of the fine cloth nourished each other such that together they appeared like a black snake who had just shed his outer skin.”

sanskrit:
snānād-ṛjūn sad-alakān atha kuñcayitvā
cāru-svabhāva-kuṭilān api rañjayitvā
bhāle lilekha tilakaṃ śaśi-maṇḍalābhaṃ
śrīkhaṇḍa-kuṅkuma-rasena sujāta-śobham
translation: “Even though Kṛṣṇa’s radiant hair is naturally curly, after bathing, His locks had straightened, so one of the servants again formed them into elegant ringlets. Then, with a mixture of sandalwood paste and saffron, he painted upon Kṛṣṇa’s forehead a beautiful circular tilaka mark that looked just like the full moon.”

sanskrit:
gārutmatendramaṇi-hīraka-padmarāga-
pradyotanaṃ vidhurayantyam ivāpy anāgaḥ
anya-prabhāva-raṇakāri-mayūkha-sāndraṃ
śrī-kaustubhābhidham adhatta mahāmaṇīndram
translation: “After that, Kṛṣṇa donned His beautiful deep-blue Kaustubha gem, the king of all jewels, which is even more splendid than an emerald, sapphire, diamond or ruby.”

sanskrit:
sthūlena mauktika-phala-prakareṇa k¬ptān
hārān dadhāra gir-agocaratām avāptān
kañcid viśālatara-vakṣasi nābhikūle
kañcit pralambam atha kañcana jānu-mūle
translation: “Then Mādhava put on several necklaces strung with large pearls, one upon His broad chest, another hanging to His navel and another that reached to His knees.”

sanskrit:
śrī-kuṇḍale maṇimaye makarānukāre
kānti-prabhākṛta-kapola-mahaḥ-pracāre
śrī-karṇayor upanināya jaloparuddhe
snānotsavena virahayya sa pūrva-siddhe
translation: “After that, Kṛṣṇa once again attached His jeweled, dolphin-shaped earrings, whose splendor increased the luster of His cheeks. He had previously worn these earrings, but during the festival of His bathing, they had gotten wet, so they were removed, dried and again brought to Him.”

sanskrit:
sat-paṭṭa-sūtra-kṛta-mañjutara-pralambau
sad-ratna-paṭṭamaya-maṅgala-sūtra-cumbau
gārutmatādi-nava-ratnaja-bāhu-bandhau
kaścid babandha valayau maṇi-bandha-sandhau
translation: “One of the servants then adorned Kṛṣṇa with a splendid jeweled pendant hung upon a silken maṅgala-sūtra. He also bedecked Him with armlets inlaid with emeralds and other stones, as well as bracelets upon His wrists.”

sanskrit:
divyāṅgulīyakam udāram anāmikāyāṃ
tat-padmarāga-mahasāṃ pariṇāmikāyām
pṛṣṭhopasanna-maṇimudram avarjanīyaṃ
datte sma kaścid adhi-tarjani rañjanīyam
translation: “Upon Kṛṣṇa’s ring finger, another servant placed an excellent ruby ring, its reddish hue transformed by the bluish luster of His skin, and upon His forefinger, an elegant and colorful jeweled seal-ring.”

sanskrit:
nānā-maṇīndra-ghaṭayā ghaṭitānubandhaṃ
pītāṃśukodara-taṭīm anu tunda-bandham
māṇikya-kiṅkiṇi-guṇaṃ ca kaṭīra-mūle
kaścid babandha paridhatta-lasad-dukūle
translation: “Another servant tied around Kṛṣṇa’s waist a yellow, diamond-studded cummerbund, and around His hips, a string of bells adorned with sparkling rubies.”

sanskrit:
pādāmbujopari maṇīndra-ghaṭānuk¬ptaṃ
mañjīra-yugmakam atho nakha-candra-dīptam
ādhāya ko ’pi maṇi-darpaṇam atyudāram
āsyendu-bimbam adhi saspṛham ādadhāra
translation: “After that, just above Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet, another servant placed a pair of tinkling ankle bells, inlaid with diamonds and illumined by the luster from His moonlike toenails. Then he lovingly held a splendid jeweled mirror before Mādhava’s shining, moonlike face.”

sanskrit:
atrāntare vraja-purandara-sannideśam
ādāya kaścana tad asya gṛhaṃ viveśa
ūce ca kṛṣṇa! janakasya girā bahubhyas
tvaṃ dātum arhasi gavām ayutaṃ dvijebhyaḥ
translation: “Meanwhile, one servant bearing the order of King Nanda entered the house and said, ‘Hey Kṛṣṇa! Your father has instructed You to give away thousands of cows to the local brāhmaṇa community.”

sanskrit:
śrutvā pitur giram asau cikuraṃ nibadhya
pītottarīyam api samyag atho viśodhya
translation: “Lucky thread” Webster’s says this word originally comes from the Hindi word kamarband, meaning ‘waistband.’ ācamya ramya-vadano guṇa-ratna-sānū rāmānujaḥ svamanasā vitatāra dhenūḥ “Upon receiving this order, sweet-faced Kṛṣṇacandra, who is a treasure-house of good qualities, bound His hair with a turban and donned His yellow upper cloth. After sipping water for purification, within His holy mind Kṛṣṇa gave away a multitude of cows in charity.”

sanskrit:
goṣṭheśvarīpsitatamo rasavat-prapākaḥ
sampādito bhavati yāvad aneka-pākaḥ
tāvan na soḍhum abhiśaktavatī vilambaṃ
sā prāhiṇot kim api bhoktum athāvilambam
translation: “So Kṛṣṇa wouldn’t have to suffer while waiting for His mother’s delicious cooking to be finished, Yaśodā Mā sent over a little something for Him to snack on.”

sanskrit:
haiyaṅgavīna-dadhi-dugdha-sarādi-bhakṣyam
etat sameta-ghanasāra-rajo ’bhibhakṣya
ācamya ca priya-sakhāṃsa-kṛtāvalambas
tāmbūlamāda madhurānana-candra-bimbaḥ
translation: “After eating the mixture of butter, yogurt, milk and cream sprinkled with particles of camphor, Kṛṣṇa, whose face is bright like the full moon, then sipped water, and while leaning on the shoulder of one of His dear friends, began to chew some tāmbūla.”

sanskrit:
atrāntare vrajapurādhipayā ’napāya-
vātsalya-kalpa-latayā ’tirayān nirdiṣṭā
āgatya kundalatikāntim etad akṣi-
bhṛṅga-pramoda-kṛtaye kṛtinī vyarājīt
translation: Meanwhile, by the order of Yaśodā Mā, who is an inexhaustible desire-fulfilling creeper of parental love, the clever Kundalatā arrived just to brighten Rādhā’s beelike eyes by taking Her to Nandālaya.

sanskrit:
anyonya-darśana-samudgamana-smitāḍhya-
śastānuyoga-rabhasonnati-sīdhu-vṛṣṭiḥ
sadyo babhūva yata eva tadā tad-āli-
vṛndaṃ nananda sama-sauhṛda-hṛdya-rociḥ
translation: When Rādhā and Kundalatā saw each other, they immediately began to smile and ask of each other’s welfare. Sprinkled by this shower of nectar, the sakhīs, who are always radiant with affection, became filled with joy.

sanskrit:
vrajapura-parameśvarī-prasādaṃ
mayi sakhi! vyakti tavodayo hy akasmāt
na śiśira-rucinā vinaiva pūrvāṃ
diśam adhi rātri sameti kāpi lakṣmīḥ
translation: Rādhikā said to Kundalatā, “Hey Sakhī! Your unexpected arrival can only be Vrajeśvarī’s mercy upon Me. Without the moonrise at night, the eastern sky cannot reveal its inexpressible beauty.”

sanskrit:
tad aham anumime nideśa-dambhāt
kim api kṛpāmṛtam eva sā vyatārīt
yad idam anupalabhya yan mamātmā
svam api sakhedam avaity anātmanīnam
translation: “I think that under the guise of an order, Vrajeśvarī has granted Me the nectar of Her compassion. Without this mercy, my mind becomes depressed and turns against Me.”

sanskrit:
ajani rasavatī-vidhāpanārthā
rasavati! te gatir ity avaimi nūnam
atha kim itarathā javād ayāsīḥ
prathamato ’nunayanty amūṃ mad-āryām
translation: “Hey Rasavatī! I know you’ve come to get Me for cooking, but still, you must first quickly go and persuade My mother-in-law.”

sanskrit:
iti sudṛg-uditāmṛtaṃ pibantī
smita-subhagaṃ nijagāda kundavallī
tad ayi sakhi! vidhehi tatra yātrām
akṛta-vilambam itaḥ sahāli-vṛndā
translation: The home of Nanda and Yaśodā O clever one! After drinking in these nectarous words of beautiful-eyed Rādhā, Kundavallī smiled blissfully and replied, “Ayi Sakhī! Since You know what’s going on, then without delay, let’s leave for Nandālaya with all Your friends!”

sanskrit:
kim iha gurujanāvaler anujñā-
grahaṇa-vidhāv aṇumātram asti kaṣṭam
yad atula-dhana-dhenu-dhānya-varṣair
akṛta vaśāṃ svayam eva tāṃ vrajeśā
translation: “Besides, getting permission from Your elders is easy because Vrajeśvarī has enchanted them with a shower of incomparable wealth, cows and grains.”

sanskrit:
nirupadhi-parama-priyo ’su-koṭer
api nikhilasya janasya goṣṭha-bhājaḥ
vrajapati-tanayaḥ samīhate yat
param iha vipratipattir asti kasya
translation: “Moreover, all the Vrajavāsīs are fond of Kṛṣṇa, even Your elders. He is more precious to them than millions of their lives, so who will not give Him whatever He wants?”

sanskrit:
sakhi! kim api na veda tat savitrī
tad atula-rocaka-vastu saṃjighṛkṣuḥ
ucitam anucitaṃ sva-lābha-hānī-
nija-para-bhāva-bhidā yaśo ’yaśo vā
translation: “Sakhī! Mother Yaśodā is so eager to collect tasty ingredients for cooking that she doesn’t even consider what is proper or improper, her own gain or loss, her state of mind or anyone else’s, or even fame or infamy.”

sanskrit:
pacasi yad api yaś ca tasya bhoktā
sa ca tirayaty amṛtaṃ sadaiva divyam
iti nikhila-pureṣv atiprasiddhis
tava sakhi! kaṃ na camatkaroti bāḍham
translation: “Sakhī! Whatever You cook is so delicious that it makes even the flavor of heavenly nectar seem insignificant. Who in all of Vraja-maṇḍala is not amazed by Your great fame?”

sanskrit:
yad avadhi kalayāṃ babhūva sā tvāṃ
munivara-datta-varāṃ varāmbujākṣi!
tad avadhi tava pāṇi-saṃskṛtānnā-
śana-viratiṃ kvacanāhni nāsya cakre
translation: “Most beautiful of the lotus-eyed ones! Ever since Vrajeśvarī heard about Durvāsā Muni’s blessing upon You that whatever You cook by Your own hand becomes more delicious than nectar, and that whoever eats this food will have a long life, be very powerful and conquer all his enemies, She hasn’t even once stopped her son from eating as much of Your wonderful cooking as He wants.”

sanskrit:
jayati yad atighora-daitya-yūthaṃ
mṛdula-tanuḥ svaparābubhūṣum eṣaḥ
tvad amala-kara-pakva-bhakta-bhukter
aparam iyaṃ manute na hetum atra
translation: “Yaśodā Mā firmly believes that the only reason delicate Kṛṣṇa always easily defeats those terrible, belligerent demons is that He eats the pure food cooked by You.”

sanskrit:
śṛṇu paramayi tattvam atra rādhe
yad avagataṃ sahasāntaraṃ mayāsyāḥ
pratidinam avalokanaṃ vinā te
śaśi-mukhi! khidyati sā yathā svasūnoḥ
translation: “O Rādhā! Now listen to another secret truth that I unexpectedly discovered about Vrajeśvarī’s heart: Just as she feels unbearable grief whenever Kṛṣṇa is away, she feels the same way if she can’t see You every day.”

sanskrit:
sutanur abhidadhe ’vadhehi vijñe
sakhi! tad idaṃ na vadasy ayuktam ittham
api tu kulavatīti vāda-bhājāṃ
sphuṭam aparāṅgana-gāmitety ayuktam
translation: Kundalatā’s words filled Śrīmatī’s heart with joy, but externally She was careful not to show it. She replied, “O wise friend of Mine! What you have said is not unreasonable, but please consider this: Is it advisable for one known as a virtuous girl to walk into someone else’s courtyard?”

sanskrit:
tataḥ sāsādya jaṭilāṃ
snuṣāyāṃ kuṭilām api
śrāvayāmāsa sandeśaṃ
vrajeśvaryā vicakṣaṇā
translation: After that, the wise Kundalatā went to Jaṭilā and delivered Vrajeśvarī’s message, even though Jaṭilā was always very deceitful concerning her son’s wife (Rādhā).

sanskrit:
ākarṇya sājñāṃ vrajarāja-rājñyāḥ
kṛṣṇāt snuṣāyām api śaṅkamānā
vicintya śikṣām atha paurṇamāsyās
tāṃ kundavallīṃ praṇayād avādīt
snuṣeyaṃ me sādhvī guṇa-garima-mādhvīka-madhurā
janaś chidrānveṣī sa khalu capalo nanda-tanayaḥ
na cājñāvajñeyā vrajapati-gṛhiṇyā bhagavatī-
vacaḥ pālyaṃ vatse! naṭati hṛdayaṃ kiṃ nu karavai!
translation: Though Jaṭilā was very concerned about keeping Rādhikā away from Kṛṣṇa, when she heard Vrajeśvarī’s order, Paurṇamāsī’s advice came to mind, so she began to speak affectionately to Kundalatā. “Dear girl, my daughter-in-law is very chaste, and has a nature as sweet as honey wine. But the local people are prone to fault-finding, and that Nandanandana is a restless boy! Paurṇamāsī told me ‘You must never neglect the order of the Queen of Vraja,’ and those words will protect me. But my mind is reeling! What should I do?”

sanskrit:
mātaḥ! satyaṃ vadati bhavatī kiṃca gopendra-sūnur
nāyaṃ jñeyaḥ khala-samudayair yādṛśaḥ śrāvito ’sti
kintu prodyad-dyumaṇir iva sad-dharma-padme khalālī-
ghūke cāyaṃ vṛjina-timire ghoṣa-santoṣa-koke
translation: Then Kundalatā said, “O Mother! What you have said is no doubt true, but Nandanandana is not as mischievous as some malicious persons have claimed. Just as the rising sun causes the lotuses to bloom, blinds the owls, and invokes the pleasant warbling of the cuckoos, in the same way, Kṛṣṇa enlivens the pious, confuses the wicked, and brings joy to the village of cowherds. Therefore, He can surely also bring happiness to your virtuous daughter-in-law.”

sanskrit:
mādhuryaṃ tūnmadayati jagad-yauvataṃ tasya tasmād-
bhītir nītis tava nava-vadhū-pālanaṃ cāpi yuktam
māśaṅkiṣṭhās tad ayati yathā dṛk-pathaṃ nāsya sādhvyāś
chāyāpy asyāḥ svayam aham imāṃ drāk tathā te ’rpayāmi
translation: “Look…Kṛṣṇa’s natural sweetness drives all the girls in the world crazy. That’s just the way it is, so it’s quite understandable that you would have some apprehension about Rādhā’s safety. But you have nothing to worry about because I’ll personally arrange it so not even the shadow of your chaste daughter-in-law comes within the range of Kṛṣṇa’s sight, and then I’ll promptly return Her to you.”

sanskrit:
tvaṃ putri! sādhvī prathitāsi goṣṭhe
tvayy arpiteyaṃ saralā vadhūs tat
sa lola-dṛṣṭiḥ kila nanda-sūnur
naināṃ yathā paśyati tad vidheyam
translation: Then Jaṭilā replied, “Kundalatā, my daughter! Among the local people everyone respects you as a righteous young girl. Therefore, I’m placing my innocent daughter-in-law into your hands, but you must make certain that that restless-eyed Nandanandana doesn’t get to see Her.”

sanskrit:
vadhūm athāhūya jagāda vatse
vrajālayān nanda-vadhū-samīpam
niṣpādya tasyāḥ priyam ehi tūrṇaṃ
sahānayaivādya ravis tvayārcyaḥ
translation: After calling for Rādhikā, Jaṭilā then said, “My child, go with Kundalatā to Vrajeśvarī’s home. When You get there, greet her sweetly and then go immediately inside and begin Your sūrya-pūjā.”104

sanskrit:
rādheti diṣṭā hṛdi sābhinanditā-
py anicchuvad gantum uvāca tāṃ sakhīm
astīha kṛtyaṃ na ca me yiyāsutā
gṛhaṃ gṛhaṃ neṅgati yat kulāṅganā
translation: Even though Śrīmatī was overjoyed to get this order from Jaṭilā, She feigned reluctance and said, “Kundalatā, I have housework to do, and I really have no desire to go there. And anyway, a respectable girl should never just ramble from house to house.”

sanskrit:
vrajapati-gṛhiṇī-giraṃ cirābhyar-
thana-vinayānunayānubaddha-mūlām
kati nirasitum atra śaknumas tat
tava bhagavān harir eva rakṣitāstu!
Jaṭilā then declared, “Rādhikā, how many times can I decline Vrajeśvarī’s humble
translation: request? You don’t have to worry about anything, because Bhagavān Hari will surely protect You.”

sanskrit:
avati jagad idaṃ svadharma-pālīḥ
kim iha satīḥ sa jahāti lokanāthaḥ?
iti kila bhavatīṃ tadīya-pāṇau
Worship of the sun god
sumukhi! samarpya nirākulā bhaveyam
translation: “Sumukhī! Lokanātha Hari protects the whole world; why would He neglect those chaste young girls who so carefully protect their religious principles? Having considered this, I place You in His hands without any worry.”

sanskrit:
iti guru-jaratī-girā samudyat-
smita-lava-saṃvṛti-peśalāḥ sakhīḥ svāḥ
vikasad asita-netra-koṇa-bhaṅgyā
kim api nigadya babhūva sāpi tūṣṇīm
translation: Detecting the hidden meaning in Jaṭilā’s words, the sakhīs struggled to conceal the smiles that appeared on their faces. Seeing this, Rādhā’s dark eyes first opened widely in alarm, and then, with a subtle squint, She fired a silent reproach in Her friends’ direction.

sanskrit:
kṛtāgrahoccaiḥ punar āryayāsau
kaundyā babhāṣe kṛta-hasta-karṣam
bhītāsi kiṃ sādhvy aham asmy avitrī-
ty uccālitā phulla-tanuḥ pratasthe
translation: When Kundalatā saw how insistent Jaṭilā was, she took Rādhikā’s hand and said, “O chaste one, why are You afraid? I’ll protect You!” Hearing this, Śrīmatī beamed in delight and then set out for Nandālaya.

sanskrit:
kṛṣṇasya prātar-āśāya
saṃskṛtaṃ laḍḍukādikam
ādāya lalitā-mukhyāḥ
sakhyo ’py anuyayuḥ sakhīm
translation: Holding laḍḍus and other foods prepared for Kṛṣṇa’s morning meal, Lalitā and all the sakhīs followed close behind Rādhā as She walked along.

sanskrit:
atha nija-bhavanād-viniryatī sā
tanu-vasanābharaṇa-cchavi-cchaṭābhiḥ
vyadhita maṇi-vicitra-śātakaumbhīṃ
pura-viśikhāṃ surabhī-kṛtākhilāśā
