translation: As Rādhikā left Her own home, the luster of Her beautiful body, clothing and ornaments transformed the narrow village pathways into streets of gold and precious jewels. Her ambrosial fragrance perfumed the air in all directions.

sanskrit:
One with a pretty face
jana-nivaha-gatāgati-pravṛttau
daravimukhī saraṇeḥ śritaika-pārśvā
avanata-dṛg-avācakāsya-padmo-
pari pariguṇṭhana-mādhurī prapede
translation: As Śrīmatī encountered the local people coming and going along the path, She avoided them by turning Her face away, lowering Her eyes and remaining silent. Covering Her lovely lotus face with a veil, She walked on the side of the road.

sanskrit:
vīkṣyādhvani parānanda-
calad-vakṣaḥ-paṭāñcalām
savayasyāṃ kundavallī
premṇā parijahāsa tām
translation: As Rādhikā ecstatically walked along with Her friends, the edge of Her cloth began to slip from Her chest. Seeing that, Kundalatā began to lovingly tease Her.

sanskrit:
mūlyānītopasaryās tri-catura-divasān proṣya sandhyāgatas te
bhartā gobhiḥ svagoṣṭhe ghaṭayitum akhilāṃ rātrim eva nyavātsīt
vakṣaḥ prodyan nakhāṅkāvali-citam adharaḥ spaṣṭa-danta-kṣato yat
tat sādhvyās te satītvaṃ samucitam adhunā vyaktam ullālasīti
translation: “O Rādhā! Your husband Abhimanyu went away for three or four days to buy some estrual cows. He returned last evening but spent the entire night in the pasture trying to get them to mate with his bulls. In spite of that, Your breasts are covered with nail marks, and on Your lips, bite marks are clearly seen. Today, Your chaste nature as a virtuous girl is shining brightly.”

sanskrit:
antar-gūḍha-smitotphulla-
kiñcit-kuñcita-locanām
svasakhīṃ lalitālokya
kundavallīm athābravīt
karaka-phala-dhiyāsyāḥ kānane dhṛṣṭa-kīraḥ
stanam anuviniviṣṭaḥ pakva-bimba-bhrameṇa
adaśad adharam uccais tan-nakhācoṭitaṃ tad-
dhṛdayam idam amuṣyāḥ kiṃ vṛthā śaṅkase tvam
translation: Noticing that Rādhā widened and then slightly squinted Her lotus eyes, while trying to hide Her inner delight, Lalitā remarked to Kundalatā, “In the forest yesterday some overly bold parrot thought Rādhā’s breasts were pomegranates, so He tried several times to land on them. And mistaking Her lips for a ripened bimba fruit, He bit them over and over. Because of that, Her breasts have nail scratches and Her lips have bite marks. Why do you uselessly suspect that something different may have happened?”

sanskrit:
sakhī-vacaḥ-smārita-kṛṣṇa-saṅga-
līlocchalat-kampa-taraṅgitāṅgīm
tāṃ vīkṣya padmākaram īkṣamāṇā
jagau punaḥ kundalatā sahāsam
ānanda-kampottaralāsi mugdhe!
kiṃ bho vṛthā padmini! kundavallyāḥ
na devaras tvāṃ madhusūdano ’sau
bhrāmyan punaḥ pāsyati bhukta-muktām
translation: When Śrīmatī heard Lalitā’s words, She immediately began to remember Her pastimes with Kṛṣṇa, and waves of delight rippled through Her trembling body. Seeing this, Kundalatā looked toward a lotus pond and remarked with a smile, “O lotus flower! O enchanted one! Why are you trembling with joy like that? It’s worthless, you know. Some madhusūdana (honeybee), who is the brother-in-law of the kundavallī (jasmine creeper), has enjoyed the sweet taste of your nectar, then left you and wandered away.”

sanskrit:
karṇa-śarmada-san-narma-
bharma-kuṇḍala-nirmitau
karmaṭhāṃ kundavallīṃ tāṃ
viśākhāha vicakṣaṇā
svene ’nurāgaṃ param udvahantī
phullāpi mṛdvī bhramarāt sulolāt
sat-padminīyaṃ sakhi kundavallī-
bhṛṅgānujād bhī-taralā cakampe
translation: Then the wise Viśākhā said to Kundalatā, who is expert in crafting golden earrings made of funny jokes, “O Sakhī! Even though this beautiful and delicate lotus flower blooms in affection for her husband, the sun, she still trembles in fear of that restless bumblebee whose older brother always dallies in the jasmine creeper.”107

sanskrit:
kvacana ca pathi nirjane kadācit
sphuṭam itaretara-vāg-vilāsa-raṅgaiḥ
yadi calati tadā kutaḥ kva yāmī-
ty api na hi vedana-gocarī-karoti
translation: In this way, as Śrī Rādhikā walked along the lonely road joking with Her friends, She lost all sense of where She’d been or where She was going.

sanskrit:
rasāla-panasārjuna-kramuka-nārikelāsanaiḥ
palāśa-vaṭa-parkaṭī-khadira-bilva-jambvādibhiḥ
madhūka-girimallikā-bakula-nāga-punnāgakair
aśoka-baka-pāṭalī-kanaka-campakaiś campakaiḥ
tamāla-navamālikā-kanakayūthikā-yūthikā-
kuraṇṭaka-lavaṅgikā-damanakātimuktādibhiḥ
api sthalasarojinī-vicakilādibhiḥ kandalī-
priyaṅgu-tulasī-mukhair api vicitra-vīrudgaṇaiḥ
translation: “Nandīśvara abounds with many varieties of trees, creepers and bushes, such as mango trees, jackfruit, arjuna, betel, coconut, asana, palāśa, banyan, fig, catechu, wood-apple, rose- apple, licorice, hill-jasmine, bakula, nāga, punnāga, aśoka, baka, trumpet flower, golden campaka, and campaka. Everywhere we look we find tamāla, nava-mālikā, golden yūthikā, yūthikā, yellow amaranth, clove, damanaka, atimuktā, land-lily, vicakila, kandalī, priyaṅgu and tulasī.”110

sanskrit:
sitāsita-vilohitotpala-saroja-kahlārakai
rathāṅga-baka-sārasaiḥ kurara-haṃsa-kāraṇḍavaiḥ
virājita-taraṅgakair vimala-vāribhir vāpikā-
taḍāga-sarasī-mukhaiḥ parivṛtāni toyāśayaiḥ
translation: “Look, there are white, blue and red lotuses and water lilies, as well as herons, cranes, storks, ospreys, swans, ducks and other birds. Nandīśvara is surrounded by many ponds, pools and lakes filled with pure water adorned with sparkling waves.”

sanskrit:
hambāravair iha gavām api ballavānāṃ
kolāhalair vividha-vandi-kalāvatāṃ taiḥ
sambhrājate priyatayā vrajarāja-sūnor
govardhanād api gurur vraja-vanditād yaḥ
translation: “The whole area resounds with the bellowing of cows, the shouting of the cowherds, and the songs and noises of eulogists and other musicians and artists. This Nandīśvara is more dear to Nandanandana than even Govardhana Hill, which is praised throughout Vraja.”

sanskrit:
sakhi! nija-purato vidūram āgā
vrajapati-sadma samīpa-varti vṛttam
tad ayi nayana-cātakābhilāṣaḥ
phalati tavāśv iti samprati pratīhi
translation: “Rādhā! You have come a long way from Your home and are now close to the house of Nanda Mahārāja. You can be sure that the cherished desire of those sparrow-like eyes of Yours will very soon be realized.”

sanskrit:
iti nigadita-mātrataḥ svasakhyā
sapadi savepathu-jāḍya-viplutāṅgīm
prasabham abhidadhāra cetayantī
kim api jagāda ca tāṃ tadaiva kaundī
sumukhi! kim adhunaiva viklavābhūr
nayana-pathāmilite ’pi kṛṣṇacandre
avagamam akhilaṃ satītvam āptaṃ
tava savayaḥ sada eva yat pramāṇam
translation: As soon as Śrīmatī heard this, Her body began to tremble and She looked dazed and confused. Seeing Her condition, Kundalatā shook Her back to partial consciousness and said, “Sumukhī! Why have You become so agitated without even seeing Kṛṣṇacandra? Now I truly understand Your chastity, and Your sakhīs certainly already know all about it.”

sanskrit:
dhṛtim iha hṛdi dhartum īśiṣe no
yad api tad apy abale! kṣaṇaṃ dadhīthāḥ
giri-yuga-bhara-dhāraṇāya yat te
giridhara eva mayādya yojanīyaḥ
translation: “O feeble one! Even though You’ve lost all composure, please, just for a moment, try to be patient. If You’re distressed because of the heavy weight of those mountains on Your chest, then I’m going to help You out. Today I’m going to employ Giridhārī to hold them up for You. He’s good at that because of His experience with Govardhana Hill.”

sanskrit:
giridhara-diśa eva śaṅkayā yā-
jani vidhurādya sakhī mahāsatīyam
parivadasi balād imām avijñe!
tad api niyokṣyasi hā punas tam asyām
Lalitā retorted, “Hey, foolish Kundalatā! If our virtuous girlfriend even looks in
translation: Giridhārī’s direction, Her heart is stricken with fear. Why are you saying these slanderous things about Her and trying to unite Her with that rascal Kṛṣṇa?”

sanskrit:
tvayi muhur iyam arpitāryayā yat
tad ucitam eva vidhitsase ’dya bhadram
svam iva sakhi! paraṃ janaṃ na viddhī-
ty uditavatī lalitā punas tayoce
translation: “Today, venerable Jaṭilā entrusted Rādhikā to your hands, but are you trying to do what is proper and auspicious? Sakhī, you shouldn’t think that all girls are like you.”

sanskrit:
alam alam anayā girāvidūre
kalaya puraḥ puratoraṇopakaṇṭhe
sphaṭika-ghaṭita-ratna-citritāsthā-
ny-abhinava-kuṭṭima-gaṃ hṛd-eka-kāmyam
translation: Kundalatā replied, “Lalitā! We don’t need any more of this useless talk. Rādhā, there in the courtyard by the main gate, sitting on a bench of gem-bedecked crystal, is the only object of your heart’s desire.”

sanskrit:
sarasam uṣasi dugdha-naicikīkaḥ
saha-savayāḥ kṛta-malla-raṅga-keliḥ
avagata-bhavad-āli-yāna-vārttā-
kṣubhita-hṛdāgata eṣa bhāti paśya
translation: “Having joyfully milked the cows and wrestled with His friends, Your beloved waits there with an anxious heart, knowing that You and Your sakhīs will soon arrive on the path.”

sanskrit:
vrajapura-lalanā-kulonmadiṣṇu-
karaṇa-paṭu-cchavi-maṇḍalopagūḍhaḥ
madhurima-dhurayaiva kiṃ tribhaṅgī-
kṛta-tanur uccala-dāma-māditālīḥ
translation: “O Rādhā! Your sweetheart has maddened all the girls of Vraja by embracing them within the halo of His splendor. It seems as though His body has curved in three places under the weight of His abundant sweetness. Even the bumblebees are intoxicated by the aroma of His swinging garland of forest flowers.”

sanskrit:
śrita-mṛdutara-gaṇḍa-kuṇḍalādhyā-
pana-para-tāṇḍava-paṇḍitākṣi-yugmaḥ
pavana-dhuta-paṭāṅga-gaura-nīla-
dyuti-laharī-stimitī-kṛtākhilāśaḥ
translation: “The sparkling earrings touching His soft cheeks have learned the art of dance from His naturally restless eyes. The waves of luster from His golden, wind-blown cloth and deeply bluish body spread tranquility in all directions.”

sanskrit:
priya-sakha-bhuja-śīrṣṇi rājad udyat-
karikara-nindaka-dhāma-vāma-bāhuḥ
nija-ruci-vijitābja-ghūrṇanaika-
vyasana-vaśetara-pāṇir eṣa īṣṭe
translation: “Look! Your charming lover stands there with His left arm, more beautiful than an elephant’s trunk, resting upon the shoulder of His dear friend Subala. His right hand is more lustrous than the lotus it twirls just to enchant all the young girls.”

sanskrit:
iti giram atha rūpa-mādhurīṃ tāṃ
yadi caṣakī-kṛta-karṇa-netra-yugmā!
apivad adara-mohatas tadā tat
prasṛmara-saurabham āśv abodhayat tām
translation: Drinking the honeywine words of Kundalatā through Her ears and the sweet form of Kṛṣṇa through Her eyes, Rādhikā became spellbound. But when Mādhava’s bodily aroma wafted gently into Her nostrils, its familiar fragrance immediately revived Her again.

sanskrit:
pulaka-nivaha-kampa-sampad-aśru-
sruti-kalilāpi dhṛtiṃ dadhaty avādīt
sakhi! kim aparam asti vartma pādau
na mama puraś calato ’sya kiṃ karomi
translation: Even though Śrīmatī’s body trembled and was covered with goose bumps and teardrops, She somehow regained Her composure and said, “Sakhī! Is there another way to enter Nandarāja’s house? My feet won’t move another inch! What can I do?”

sanskrit:
guru-paravaśataiva doṣa-dūrī-
karaṇa-paṭus tava kiṃ bhiyā hriyā vā
sapadi savayaseti bodhyamānā
laghu laghu gantum iyeṣa sā tad agre
translation: Lalitā replied, “Rādhikā! Your obedience to Your elders will protect You from all fault, so why should You be afraid or shy?” 111 Consoled by these words, Śrīmatī began to slowly walk on the path toward Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit:
kim idam iti parasparāvaloko-
cchalita-mahāmadhurimṇi yat tayos tāḥ
translation: Śrīmatī’s elders had instructed Her to take that path, so they wouldn’t likely criticize Her for doing so. svam atula-tarasi nyamajjayann ā- laya iti varṇayituṃ na gīr apīṣṭe When Rādhā’s astonished eyes met Kṛṣṇa’s, a wonderful and powerful wave of sweetness arose from Their bodies and bathed all the nearby sakhīs. Even the goddess of speech herself could not fully describe such an astounding scene.

sanskrit:
agha-damana-cakora-candrikās tāḥ
śaśi-vadanāpi papau muhuḥ pipāsuḥ
giridhara-mudiroparīha cāta-
ky atanu-rasaṃ pravavarṣa seti citram
translation: Aho! How amazing! Moonfaced Rādhā began to thirstily drink in the moonlight beaming from the cakora bird (Agha-damana Kṛṣṇa), and the cātakī bird (Rādhā) showered the dark cloud (Giridhārī Kṛṣṇa) with drops of Cupid’s nectar.

sanskrit:
atha nija-nija mūrdhni savya-haston-
namana-kalā-kalitāvaguṇṭhanās tāḥ
avanata-nayanāñcalī-vilīḍha-
priya-caraṇābja-sudhā yayus tad agrāt
translation: Then, using their left hands, Rādhā and each of the gopīs gracefully pulled their veils atop their heads. As they walked in front of Kṛṣṇa, through the corners of their lowered eyes they licked the nectar from His lotus feet.

sanskrit:
harir api parivṛtya tan-nitamba-
dyuti-nihitekṣaṇa-paṅkajo ’vatasthe
varatanu-tatir apy atītya tad-go-
puram avaguṇṭhanam īṣad asyati sma
translation: When these beautiful girls had gone a short distance, Hari turned toward them and fixed the gaze of His lotus eyes upon their splendid derrieres. After the gopīs had passed through the village gate, they allowed their veils to slip slightly from their heads.

sanskrit:
sakhi! bhavad avaloka-jāta-harṣaṃ
sapadi sa campaka-mālayā baṭus tam
sukhinam akṛta yat tad iṅgita-jñā
bhavasi na vety uditāha sā svasakhyā
Sarasvatī Devī
translation: Ordinarily the cakora bird drinks moonlight and the dark cloud rains upon the cātakī bird, but in this instance, just the opposite occurred! tvam asi khalu yathā tathānvamāsīr nija-dṛśīr yatase parā vidhitsuḥ iti dara-vikasat-smitā bhramad-bhrūs tvaritam avāpa mahāpurāntaraṃ sā In a joking voice, Tuṅgavidyā said to Rādhā, “Sakhī! Noticing Kṛṣṇa’s joy at seeing You, Madhumaṅgala quickly adorned Him with a campaka garland. You know what that means, don’t You?”114 Understanding Tuṅgavidyā’s words, Rādhikā replied, “Sakhī! Just because you think you’re so beautiful resting on that lover boy’s chest like a garland, it doesn’t mean everyone wants that.” With a slight smile and a movement of Her eyebrows Śrīmatī then quickly entered Nanda’s great house.

sanskrit:
sphaṭika-ghaṭita-kuḍyam īḍya-bharmoj-
jvala-paṭalaṃ pavi-kīlakaṃ kavāṭam
maṇimaya-lalanā-dhṛta-pradīpa-
vratati-naga-dvija-rāji-rājita-dvāḥ
translation: Within that beautiful home are rooms with walls of crystal, ceilings of gold and doors with diamond bolts. On each side of the doors are jeweled statues of women holding jeweled lamps, and sitting upon jeweled trees intertwined with jeweled creepers are jeweled birds crafted from the most precious of gems.

sanskrit:
dyumaṇi-kiraṇa-dīpta-ratna-kumbha-
dhvaja-naṭa-keki-vṛtāgra-pauraṭāṭṭam
suravara-pura-nindi yatra śaṃ-daṃ
vilasati mandira-vṛndam indirāḍhyam
translation: At the top of the golden watchtower sits a jeweled water pot illuminated by the rays of the morning sun. Atop that water pot waves a flag bearing the image of a dancing peacock. All the rooms within Nanda’s home are very pleasant and even more elegant than Amarāvatī, the abode of Indra.

sanskrit:
masāra-prācīraṃ marakata-gṛhaṃ hema-paṭalaṃ
pravāla-stambhāli-sphaṭika-vṛti-vaidūrya-vaḍabhiḥ
mahānīlendrāṭṭaṃ vimala-kuruvindopala-mahā-
pratīhāraṃ nānākṛti jita-vimānāvali-puram
translation: In Nanda’s abode the walls are made of sapphires and emeralds, the ceilings of gold. Everywhere are coral pillars, crystal fences and turrets of lapis lazuli. There are watchtowers made of sapphires and enormous doors made of sparkling rubies. Nanda’s palace is the most magnificent in all of Vraja.

sanskrit: kuḍye yasya maṇi-praveka-racite śilpa-kriyā-kalpitaiḥ
translation: This was a signal that They would soon meet. pratyāsajya śukaiḥ samaṃ gṛha-śukeṣv āsādita-sthemasu saprāṇāḥ kim amī ime kim atha vety unmīlataḥ saṃśayād- dātuṃ dāḍima-bījakāni suciraṃ muhyanti mugdhāṅganāḥ Also upon those beautiful, jeweled walls are exquisitely crafted paintings of parrots, so apparently real that even the household parrots like to perch near them for companionship. When the gopīs saw them, they thought, “Are these alive, or is it those?” They were so bewildered that for a long time they were unsure as to whom they should offer some pomegranate seeds.

sanskrit:
mukhya-prakoṣṭhe catur ālaye ’syā
bhāṇḍāra-gehaṃ varuṇasya diśyam
śrī-kṛṣṇa-vāsaḥ śubha-dakṣiṇa-sthaḥ
śrī-rāma-dhāmottara-diśy udeti
translation: The main courtyard of Nanda’s palace is surrounded by four rooms. On the western side lies his treasury, on the auspicious southern side, Kṛṣṇa’s room, and on the northern, Balarāma’s room.

sanskrit:
prācyāṃ gṛhaṃ tādṛśam eva yatra
prācyāṃ sa yasyānyatara-prakoṣṭhe
svaputra-bhadrāya nijeṣṭadevaṃ
nārāyaṇaṃ sevate eva nandaḥ
translation: On the eastern side of the main courtyard lies Nandarāja’s room, which is similar to Kṛṣṇa’s. In another room to the east, Nanda Bābā worships his personal deity Lord Nārāyaṇa for the welfare of his son.

sanskrit:
koṣālayasyānvita-dakṣiṇāṃśe
kṛṣṇasya dhāmnaḥ śubha-paścime ’sti
yā pākaśālā-dvaya-madhya eva
viśrāma-dhāmānuru rādhikāyāḥ
translation: Adjoining the treasury room on the south and Kṛṣṇa’s room on the west is the palace kitchen. Between the kitchen and Kṛṣṇa’s room is a small room for Rādhā to rest in when She tires from cooking.

sanskrit:
kṛṣṇasya dhāmno ’nvita dakṣiṇāṃśe
pākālayasyāpi virājamānaḥ
ārāma āste sarasī ca yatra
raho manojñaṃ bahu-geha-vedi
translation: Just to the south of Kṛṣṇa’s room and the kitchen lie a beautiful flower garden and lake, where many rooms and benches are the scenes of Rādhā-Mādhava’s secret meetings.

sanskrit:
atha samupaseduṣīṃ sakhībhir hari-
jananī nija-veśma bhāsayantīm
amanuta bhuvana-trayaika-lakṣmīm
uditavatīṃ muditā ’rka-mitra-putrīm
translation: When Rādhikā and Her sakhīs arrived, Yaśodā Mā was overjoyed, thinking that the most beautiful goddess in all the three worlds had appeared to illuminate her home.

sanskrit:
tatrāgatāṃ caraṇayoḥ praṇatāṃ svadorbhyām
utthāpya tāṃ hṛdi nidhāya mukunda-mātā
āghrāya mūrdhni muditā jananī parārdhā
snigdhā cucumba mukham aśru-mukhī tato ’syāḥ
translation: When Śrīmatī offered obeisance to her lotus feet, Yaśodā joyfully lifted and embraced Her, smelled Her head, and with tearful eyes, began to lovingly kiss Her face.

sanskrit:
pratyekam āliṅgya ca tad-vayasyāḥ
papraccha sā ’vyāhata-bhavyam asyāḥ
vyagrā sutasyāśana-sādhane drāk
sasneham etāḥ punar āvabhāṣe
translation: In this way, Yaśomatī embraced each of Rādhikā’s sakhīs and inquired of their well- being. Then, eager to have her son’s meal prepared, she began to speak to Rādhā with great affection.

sanskrit:
na sutāsi kīrtidāyāḥ
kintu mamaiveti tathyam ākhyāmi
prāṇimi vīkṣya mukhaṃ te
kṛṣṇasyeveti kiṃ trapase?
translation: “My child, why are You so bashful? The truth is, You’re really my daughter, not Kīrtidā’s. Seeing Your face gives me the same joy as seeing Kṛṣṇa’s. You two are the wellsprings of my life!”

sanskrit:
madhura-mṛdula-modakādi kiñcit
samam upaveśya sakhī-janair balāt tām
druta-hṛdayā dhaniṣṭhayāśayitvā
bhṛśam upalālya nināya pākaśālām
translation: Then, her heart softened by love, Vrajeśvarī invited Śrīmatī and Her sakhīs to sit down to relish some soft, delicious sweetmeats, served to them by Dhaniṣṭhā. Caressing the girls affectionately, she then led them all to the kitchen.

sanskrit:
vividha-madhura-bhakṣyotpādane labdha-varṇā
vraja-bhuvi kila yūyaṃ viśrutā miṣṭa-hastāḥ
tad iha kuruta putryaḥ! sādhu bhakṣyāṇi yatnād
dara-rucir api vatsaḥ saspṛhaṃ me yathātti
translation: “My children! Because of your delicate hands, so expert in preparing many kinds of delicious foods, you have all become very famous in Vraja-maṇḍala. Therefore, even though my son has little appetite, please carefully prepare some excellent dishes so He’ll be eager to eat His meal.”

sanskrit:
upalāvaṇikaṃ tv ekāḥ
kāścit kuruta dādhikam
sārpiṣkam aparā yūyaṃ
vatsāḥ śārkarikaṃ parāḥ
translation: “One of you prepare foods with a salty taste, while others prepare foods made with yogurt, or cooked in ghee, or containing sugar.”

sanskrit:
sarasa-rasavatī-satprakriyā-paṇḍitāsi
tvam iha rasavatīṃ me yāhi rādhe! prayatnāt
janani! bala-jananyādhiṣṭhitāṃ miṣṭam annaṃ
racaya saha tayaiva vyañjanāny uttamāni
translation: “Rādhikā, You know all the best methods in the world for cooking delicious meals. Therefore, O tender one, meet with Baladeva’s mother in the kitchen and together carefully prepare the finest of sweets and vegetable dishes.”

sanskrit:
vaṭakam amṛta-keliṃ sādhayātiprayatnāt
sarasa-masṛṇam anyaṃ putri! karpūra-kelim
madhuram amṛta-koṭer yatra kṛṣṇaḥ satṛṣṇas
trijagati na hi kaścit tvām ṛte yasya vettā
translation: “My daughter! Please make the soft, juicy sweet-cakes called amṛta-keli and karpūra-keli, which are more delightful than nectar, so Kṛṣṇa won’t be able to resist. Other than You, no one in the three worlds knows how to make such delicacies.”

sanskrit:
yasyām uccair lālasāḍhyaḥ suto me
tāṃ pīyūṣa-granthi-pālīṃ ca kṛtvā
karpūrailādy-anvita-pānake tvaṃ
yatnād vatse! dhehi pañcāmṛtākhye
translation: “Dear child! My son loves that nectar drink called granthi-pālī, so please carefully prepare it for Him. Then make some pañcāmṛta mixed with camphor, cardamom and other spices.”

sanskrit:
tvaṃ vidhehi lalite ’mba! rasālāṃ
tvaṃ ca ṣāḍavam ihāśu viśākhe!
tvaṃ ca bhoḥ śikhariṇīṃ śaśilekhe
putri campakalate! mathitaṃ tvam
translation: “Lalitājī, you please make some rasālā. Viśākhā, you quickly prepare the drink called ṣ ā ḍ a v a . Śaśilekhā, you make śikhariṇī, and Campakalatā, you please make some buttermilk.”115

sanskrit:
āmikṣāṃ tvaṃ putri! saṃsādhya tasyās
tat-tad-dravyair yoga-pāka-prabhedaiḥ
tat-tad-bhedān tuṅgavidye! vidhehi
tvaṃ matsyaṇḍī-pānakāny amba! citre!
translation: “Tuṅgavidyā, my daughter! After making curds and whey, mix them with the appropriate ingredients and cook several different kinds of foods. And Citrā, you prepare cold drinks made of sugarcane juice.”

sanskrit:
tvaṃ khaṇḍa-maṇḍāni ca raṅgadevi!
tvaṃ kṣīra-sārān vividhān sudevi!
vāsanti! śubhrā mṛdu-phenikās tvaṃ
tvaṃ maṅgale! kuṇḍalikāṃ vidhehi
translation: “Raṅgadevī, you make some delicious cakes, and Sudevī, you please prepare different kinds of creams and butters. Vāsantī, you make some soft, white phenikās, and Maṅgalā, you make kuṇḍalikās.”116

sanskrit:
kādambari! tvaṃ kuru candra-kāntīs
tvaṃ lāsike! taṇḍula-cūrṇa-piṇḍīḥ
tvaṃ śaṣkulīḥ kaumudi! bhūri-bhedās
tvam indu-piṇḍāni madālase ’mba!
translation: “Kādambarī, you make candra-kāntī, and Lāsikā, you prepare rice-flour laḍḍus. Kaumudī, you please make many kinds of śaṣkulī, and Madālasā, you make indu-piṇḍa.”117

sanskrit:
śaśimukhi! vaṭakāni tvaṃ vidhehi prayatnād
dadhi-vaṭaka-mukhāni prājya-mādhurya-bhāñji
praṇaya sumukhi! ramyāḥ śarkarā-paṭṭikās tvaṃ
maṇimati! bahu-bhedāṃs tvaṃ ca piṣṭānna-pūpān
translation: “Śaśimukhī, you carefully prepare sweet cakes made of pulse mixed with yogurt. Sumukhī, you make delicious sugar tablets, and Maṇimatī, you bake various kinds of sweet cakes made of rice flour.”

sanskrit:
vidhatsva bhoḥ kāñcanavalli! vatse!
godhūma-cūrṇodbhava-laḍḍukāni
manoharākhyāni manorame! tvaṃ
tvaṃ mauktikākhyāni ca ratnamāle!
translation: “Kāñcanavallī, my child! You prepare laḍḍus made with wheat flour cooked in ghee and then formed into strings. Manoramā, you make the laḍḍus known as manoharā, and Ratnamālā, you make the tiny pearl-like laḍḍus called mauktika.”

sanskrit:
subhṛṣṭa-nistuṣa-tilair
modakān kuru mādhavi!
tathā tila-kadambākhyāḥ
satilāḥ khaṇḍa-paṭṭikāḥ
translation: “Mādhavī, you make sweetballs with huskless sesame seeds, as well as the sweet called tila-kadamba, made of pieces of candied sugar mixed with sesame.”

sanskrit:
lājān dhānāṃś ca saṃbhṛṣṭān
pṛthukān ghṛta-bharjitān
kṛtvā vindhye! sitā-kvāthaiḥ
samudgān kuru modakān
translation: “Vindhyā, you prepare sweetballs made of parched rice, fried barley, flattened rice and kidney beans fried in ghee, all mixed together with a thick sugar solution.”

sanskrit:
rambhe! karambhaṃ kuru śātakumbha-
kuṇḍyāṃ surambhā-phala-śarkarādyaiḥ
niṣpīḍya pakvāmra-rasaṃ manojñe!
sitā-ghana-kṣīra-yutaṃ vidhehi
translation: “Rambhā, you mix ripe bananas, sugar solution, yogurt and farina in a golden pot. And Manojñā, you squeeze some fresh mango juice and mix it with sugar and condensed milk.”

sanskrit:
utthāpitaṃ yat tu mayā mathitvā
prātaḥ sugandhā-payaso dadhīni
tad iṣṭa-gandhaṃ navanīta-piṇḍaṃ
haiyaṅgavīnaṃ kuru bhoḥ kilimbe
translation: “Kilimbā, this morning I churned some butter from the milk of the cow named Sugandhā. Now please take this fragrant butter and make ghee.”

sanskrit:
svayaṃ dugdhvā vrajendreṇa
prahitaṃ dhavalā-payaḥ
pānārtham ambike mandaṃ
tvaṃ śṛtaṃ kuru vatsayoḥ118
translation: “Ambikā, Vrajarāja personally milked the cow named Dhavalā and has sent the milk here. Now please lightly boil that milk so Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma can drink it when They return from the pasturing grounds.”

sanskrit:
ṛjīṣa-darvī-nivahaiḥ parītāṃ
mṛd-dāru-kuṇḍy-ādika-bhājanaiś ca
cullī-cayāḍhyāṃ mama sikta-liptāṃ
tad-dugdha-śālāṃ vrajatāśu bālāḥ
translation: “All of you girls go quickly to my milk kitchen, which has been washed with water and cow dung. There you’ll find lots of ovens, clay and wooden bowls and pots, and various kinds of ladles and frying pans for cooking all your preparations.”

sanskrit:
nānopakaraṇāni tvaṃ
tāni tāni dhaniṣṭhike!
niṣkāsya tat-tad-bhāṇḍebhyaḥ
pātreṣv ādhāya dāpaya
translation: “Dhaniṣṭhikā, you collect all of those implements from their storage places and distribute them to the appropriate cooks.”

sanskrit:
tat-tat-padārthāṃs tvaritaṃ tulasyā
sahānayā raṅgaṇamālike tvam
ānīya koṣālayato ’smadīyād
dāsī-gaṇair dāpaya tatra tatra
translation: “Raṅgaṇamālikā, you and Tulasī 119 quickly go with the maidservants to our storeroom to get all the necessary ingredients and then place them wherever they’re needed.”

sanskrit:
āmrātakāmra-phalapūra-karīra-dhātrī-
limpāka-koli-rucakādi-phalāni kāmam
taile ciraṃ salavaṇe kila sandhitāni
mūlāny athārdraka-mukhāni ca rocakāni
matsyaṇḍikā-rasa-ciroṣita-pakva-ciñcā-
dhātrī-rasāla-badarī-śakalāni tadvat
niṣkāsya bhos tvam iha manthanikā-kulebhyaḥ
kṛtvānayendumukhi! kāñcana-bhājaneṣu
translation: “Indumukhī, you bring the different kinds of pickle (ācāra), made of hog plum, mango, lemon, bamboo shoots, āmalaka, lime, jujube and other tasty fruits soaked in sesame oil and salt for several days. Also remove from their pots the pieces of cooked tamarind, āmalaka, mango and jujube that have been soaking in sugarcane juice and bring them here in a golden vessel.”

sanskrit:
śande śubhe bharaṇi pīvari miṣṭa-haste
cullīcayopari-dhṛtātula-manthanīṣu
dugdhāni bhārika-gaṇopahṛtāni goṣṭhād
vatsāḥ! śanaiḥ śrapayatāśu nidhāya yūyam
translation: “Śandā, Śubhā, Bharaṇī, Pīvarī and Miṣṭahastā, all of you get the milk brought from the pasturing grounds by the load bearers, pour it into the pots sitting atop the stoves and begin to slowly stir it.”

sanskrit:
kānta-bhuktāvaśiṣṭaṃ saṃ-
bhujya tu jāta-śarmikām
āyātāṃ sva-samīpe tāṃ
rādhām āha salālanam
sarasija-mukhi! kīrtidaikakīrte!
pacana-kalā-caturā kṛtāsi dhātrā
tad ayi rasavatīṃ praviśya pākaṃ
kuru lalitādi-sakhī-kṛteti kṛtyam
translation: Then Rādhikā sat down near Yaśodā to joyfully eat some remnants of Kṛṣṇa’s food. Yaśodā gently caressed Her and said, “O lotus face, You who bring fame to Your mother Kīrtidā, O Rādhā, God has given You great skill in the art of cooking. Please go into the kitchen now and get started. Lalitā and Your other friends will help You with everything.”

sanskrit:
goṣṭheśvarīṃ samabhivādya viśeṣa-namrā
tat-pāṇi-padma-dhṛta-pāṇir atīva kamrā
āsādya rāma-jananīṃ praṇanāma yātām
adhyakṣatāṃ pacana-karmaṇi sābhijātā
translation: After the beautiful Rādhikā humbly offered Her respects to Mother Yaśodā, Yaśodā Mā took Śrīmatī’s right hand and led Her to Mother Rohiṇī, who was in charge of all the cooking. Rādhā then also offered respects to her, the mother of Balarāma.

sanskrit:
tābhyāṃ mahānasam upetya ca pāka-śālā-
pālīḥ smitena mṛdunā vacasā ca bālā
sammānya mānya-caritā mumude mitāni
pāka-kriyopakaraṇāni vilokya tāni
translation: Then young Rādhikā entered the kitchen with Mothers Yaśodā and Rohiṇī, where She respectfully greeted the kitchen staff with sweet words and a gentle smile. When She saw that all the necessary ingredients and implements for cooking had already been properly placed, She became very happy.

sanskrit:
kuṣmāṇḍakālu-kacu-mānaka-kanda-tumbī-
vārttāku-mūlaka-paṭola-phalāni śimbī
ḍiṇḍīśa-vāraṇa-buṣāma-phalāny anīcā-
rambhā-viśeṣa-nava-garbha-navīna-mocāḥ
vāstūka-māriṣa-paṭola-śikhāḥ kalāya-
vallī-śikhāś caṇakāgra-śikhāḥ pradhāya
Moon face
tumbī-śikhāś ca mṛdulāḥ saha-podikāgrā-
ṇy ālokya saikṣata sakhīḥ sarasāḥ samagrāḥ
translation: Looking at all the different kinds of pumpkins, potatoes, arums, turnips, bottle gourds, eggplants, radishes, cucumbers, kidney beans, lady fingers, green bananas, plantain flowers, spinach, chickpeas, etc., Rādhikā assigned each of the clever gopīs an appropriate tasty dish to prepare.

sanskrit:
yad yena yena vidhinā ruciratvam etya
yad vyañjane yad upayujyata ity avetya
tābhir mahānasa-carībhir amūni tāni
tat-tat-prakāram atha kuṭṭita-karttitāni
translation: Knowing just which vegetables were suitable for each of the different dishes to be prepared, the kitchenmaids began to cut and chop them all up in the proper ways.

sanskrit:
elā-lavaṅga-maricārdraka-jāty-ajājī-
jātīphala-tvaca-sulāṅgali-sasya-rājīḥ
siddhārtha-taṇḍula-niśā dalitāṃś ca māṣān
kecij janāḥ pipiṣur abja-dṛśām aśeṣān
Meanwhile, the vraja-sundarīs ground cardamom, cloves, black pepper, ginger, nutmeg,
cumin, mace, cinnamon, coconut pulp, black mustard seeds, white mustard seeds, rice,
turmeric and dal beans. (Kṛṣṇāhnika-kaumudī 2.89)
translation: elā-lavaṅga-maricārdraka-jāty-ajājī- jātīphala-tvaca-sulāṅgali-sasya-rājīḥ siddhārtha-taṇḍula-niśā dalitāṃś ca māṣān kecij janāḥ pipiṣur abja-dṛśām aśeṣān Meanwhile, the vraja-sundarīs ground cardamom, cloves, black pepper, ginger, nutmeg, cumin, mace, cinnamon, coconut pulp, black mustard seeds, white mustard seeds, rice, turmeric and dal beans.

sanskrit:
piṣṭvā suvarṇa-puṭikāsu śubha-prabhāvair
ācchāditāsv anucarī-ghaṭayā śarāvaiḥ
susthāpitāni vasanopari pāka-līlā-
rambhe cakāra hṛdayaṃ niravadya-śīlā
translation: After grinding the various substances, they carefully poured them into golden cups, covered them with tight-fitting lids and placed cloths over the tops. Then the pure-hearted Rādhā began to intently focus on the work of cooking.

sanskrit:
āvaśyakābharaṇa-veśa-lasat-pratīkā
dhautāṅghri-pāṇi-kamalā saha-rohiṇīkā
babhrāja sā vara-mahānasa-vedikāyāṃ
śraddhāya kautukavatī pacana-kriyāyām
Putting aside any unnecessary ornaments and clothing, beautiful Rādhā washed Her
translation: lotus hands and feet. Then, with great respect and eagerness, She joined Rohiṇī Mā at the best of kitchen tables to begin cooking.

sanskrit:
dīptāsu rāma-jananīṅgitato ’nalena
cullīṣu cārutara-dāru-samujjvalena
ārūruhann akhila-locana-citta-jaitrīs
tās tāmra-rīti-rajatācita-pāka-pātrīḥ
translation: At Rohiṇī Mā’s signal, the girls placed nicely shaped pieces of wood into the fires, and atop the ovens they set artistically crafted cooking pots of copper, brass and silver.

sanskrit:
jajjvāla sa svayam aphut-kṛti-vīta-dhūmam
agniḥ svayaṃ jalam abhūd anabhūma-bhūma
yad yatra yatra lavaṇaṃ ca tathā pramāṇaṃ
tat tatra tat kara-tale ’kuruta pramāṇam
translation: The fire produced no smoke and flamed brightly without any need for fanning. Only a little moisture sizzled from the burning wood. Whenever salt was needed for the various dishes, the dāsīs placed the appropriate amount into the palm of Rādhikā’s hand.

sanskrit:
aguru-sarala-devadāru-dāru-
jvalana-pariśrita-cullikā-cayāgre
nihita-vividha-pātra-rāji-rājad-
bahuvidha-temana-sādhu-sādhanārtham
translation: The many ovens blazed with sticks of fragrant aguru, sarala and deodar wood. In front and on each side of the ovens, the girls had placed pots full of various sauces and condiments to be used in cooking.

sanskrit:
jvalana-kalana-pātra-dhāraṇonna-
ty-avanati-mūrchana-darvi-cālanādyaiḥ
trivali-kuca-bhujāṃsa-kampa-celoc-
calana-vaśād udapādi yas tadā ’syāḥ
madhurima-bharam acyutaḥ svasaudha-
sphurita-gavākṣa-dhṛtekṣaṇaḥ pibaṃs tam
madana-madam udañcitaṃ vivṛṇvan
kim api jagāda paṭur baṭuṃ miṣeṇa
translation: While tending the fire, lifting pots, bending over, adding ingredients, stirring with a ladle, and so on, Rādhikā’s three-lined belly, Her breasts, arms and shoulders shook, and Her clothing loosened. When Kṛṣṇa suddenly noticed Her through a small window in His room, He began to savor Her sweetness with His eyes. Excited with passion, He pretended to say something to Madhumaṅgala just to attract Śrīmatī’s attention. (Kṛṣṇa-bhāvanāmṛtam.- 65) Yaśodā Mā Enters the Kitchen and Looks Over the Different Preparations Aguru is aloe wood, sarala is a type of pine, and devadāru (deodar) is a type of cedar.

sanskrit:
prahitya taṃ sātha mahānasaṃ gatā
kiṃ kiṃ tvayā sādhitam etayā saha
sarvaṃ tad etan mama temanādikaṃ
saṃdarśayety āha balasya mātaram
translation: Then Mother Yaśodā entered the kitchen and asked Mother Rohiṇī, “What kinds of sauces and vegetables have you and Rādhikā prepared? Please show me.”

sanskrit:
tām āha sammārjita-vedikāntare
navīna-mṛd-bhājana-paṅkti sambhṛtam
sā darśayantī kṛta-temanādikaṃ
rādhāṃ praśaṃsanty atha tāṃ ca rohiṇī
translation: While praising Rādhikā’s cooking talents in various ways, Rohiṇī Mā pointed out the curries and other ingredients kept in new clay pots sitting upon a freshly cleaned table.

sanskrit:
sumadhuraṃ śaśito ’pi susaṃskṛtaṃ
nipuṇayā pacane mṛdu rādhayā
pravara-manthanikāsu susambhṛtaṃ
sumukhi! paśya puraḥ sakhi! pāyasam
translation: Rohiṇī said, “My lovely friend, there in front of you is a large clay pot filled with sweet rice made by Śrī Rādhā, so gentle and talented. Just like the moon, it is very cool and white, and its taste is sweeter than nectar!”

sanskrit:
bala-puṣṭi-karaṃ hṛdyaṃ
madhuraṃ mṛdulaṃ sati!
manthanī-sambhṛtaṃ paśya
saṃyāvam anayā kṛtam
translation: “And Sati, in this pot, there are very tender, sweet, tasty and nourishing wheat cakes that Rādhikā cooked.”

sanskrit:
rambhā-sīrī-kṣīrasāraiḥ
śaṣkulīr vividhāḥ sakhi!
paśya piṣṭa-vikāraṃś ca
nānā-bhedān susaṃskṛtān
Chaste One
translation: These cakes are called saṃyāva and are made of wheat flour fried with ghee and milk and made up into an oblong form with sugar and spices. (Monier-Williams) “Over here are various kinds of cakes made with plantain, coconut and butter, as well as many other kinds of delicious preparations made from flour.”

sanskrit:
pīyūṣagranthi-karpūra-
kelikāmṛtakelikāḥ
anayā saṃskṛtāḥ paśya
yad vidhir me na gocaraḥ
translation: “Śrī Rādhā has also made pīyūṣagranthi, karpūra-keli, amṛta-keli and other preparations that even I don’t know how to make!”

sanskrit:
kevalo mathita-klinno
maudgo ’yaṃ vaṭako dvidhā
sitā-lavaṇa-saṃyogān
māṣasyāpi catur-vidhaḥ
translation: “She has also prepared four different kinds of moist, round bean cakes. One is made of crushed kidney beans dipped in pure sugar, one made of kidney beans dipped in salt, one of dal beans dipped in sugar, and one of dal beans dipped in salt.”

sanskrit:
ciñcāmrātaka-cukrāmrais
tat tad dravyādi-yogataḥ
īṣan-madhura-gāḍhādi-
bhedād amlo dviṣaḍ-vidhaḥ
translation: “Śrīmatī also mixed tamarind, hog plum, sorrel and mango together with other ingredients, and then added varying degrees of sugar to prepare twelve different kinds of sour foods.”

sanskrit:
baddha-rambhā-navya-garbha-
tan-navya-mukulāṃśayoḥ
māna-kandāmbu-kacvīnāṃ
mukhāṃśasyālukasya ca
kuṣmāṇḍa-ḍiṇḍiśāṇāṃ ca
cakrābha-khaṇḍa-jālakam
caṇaka-kṣoda-paṅkāktaṃ
ghṛta-bhṛṣṭaṃ pṛthak pṛthak
translation: “Then She cut plantain fruits and buds, the top parts of arums, sweet potatoes and water roots, as well as potatoes, pumpkins and lady’s fingers into circular pieces, dipped them in ground chickpea batter and fried them individually in ghee.”

sanskrit:
caṇaka-kṣoda-vaṭakān-
yājya-bhṛṣṭāni kevalam
aparāny amla-sat-takra-
kvātha-klinnāni lokaya
translation: “And look! There are also ground chickpea cakes fried in ghee and then soaked in a mixture of sour curds and buttermilk.”

sanskrit:
caṇaka-kṣoda-piṇḍānāṃ
svinnānāṃ kvathitāmbhasi
khaṇḍāni dravya-pākādi-
bhedān nānā-vidhāni ca
translation: “There are many other kinds of delicious preparations made of boiled chickpea balls cooked with various kinds of delectable ingredients.”

sanskrit:
vaṭikā phala-mūlānāṃ
pṛthak saṃyoga-bhedataḥ
trijāta-maricādyais tu
prakārān bahudhā-kṛtān
translation: “There are many kinds of foods consisting of round cakes made of fruits and roots mixed in different ways with nutmeg, cinnamon and cardamom.”

sanskrit:
karkāru-jyotsnikālābu-
phalāny āli pṛthak pṛthak
rājikā-dadhi-yogena
saṃskṛtāny anayā śubhe
translation: “My auspicious friend, Rādhikā also prepared different kinds of rāyatās made of pumpkin, cucumber and gourd mixed with black mustard and yogurt.”

sanskrit:
vatsepsita-prasūnāni
ghṛta-bhṛṣṭāni kevalam
ghṛta-bhṛṣṭā dadhi-klinnāḥ
kalikāḥ kovidārajāḥ
translation: “She also prepared a type of flower bud fried in ghee only that your dear boy Kṛṣṇa really likes, as well as the buds of golden kovidāra flowers cooked in ghee and then soaked in yogurt.”

sanskrit: ghṛta-bhṛṣṭā dadhi-klinnāḥ
translation: One Sanskrit commentary mentions that some people call this flower a baka-puṣpa, which is said to resemble the heron in shape. prasūna-vaṭikā dvidhā paṭolasya phalāny ājya- bhṛṣṭāni ruci-dāny alam “There are also two other kinds of round cakes made of flower buds fried in ghee and soaked in yogurt, as well as very tasty cucumbers fried in ghee.”

sanskrit:
vṛddha-kuṣmāṇḍa-vaṭikāḥ
kacvī-mānālu-kandakaiḥ
tikta-lālita125 -cūrṇāḍhyāś
cavikāḍhyāḥ parāḥ kṛtāḥ
translation: “There are round cakes made from full-grown pumpkins as well as potatoes, arum and other vegetables mixed with bitter jute leaf flour.”

sanskrit:
sitailā-maricair yogād
dugdha-tumbī-kṛtānayā
tad-yogād aparaṃ miṣṭaṃ
kṣīra-kuṣmāṇḍa-nāmakam
translation: “Śrī Rādhikā has also mixed sugar, cardamom and black pepper with the dugdha-tumbī gourd to make a sweet preparation called kṣīra-kuṣmāṇḍa.”

sanskrit:
dadhi-śūraṇakaṃ miṣṭaṃ
dhātrī-śūraṇakaṃ param
dadhnaikaṃ bharjitaṃ cānyaṃ
kāravilva-phalaṃ dvidhā
translation: “There is arum cooked in ghee and mixed with yogurt, sugar and myrobalan, as well as wood-apple mixed with yogurt and sugar in two different ways.”

sanskrit:
mṛdu-rambhā-garbha-khaṇḍa-
vṛddha-kuṣmāṇḍa-khaṇḍayoḥ
sitā-dadhi-yutaḥ pāko
madhurāmlaḥ suśītalaḥ
translation: “She also cooked soft pieces of plantain and pumpkin, and then mixed them with yogurt and sugar to make a very cooling sweet-and-sour dish.”

sanskrit:
nālīta-methī-śatapuṣpikā-miśī-
paṭola-vāstūka-vitunna-māriṣāḥ
prakāra-saṃyoga-vibhedato ’nayā
śākāḥ sudhā-garva-hṛtaḥ susaṃskṛtāḥ
translation: Other versions of this word are nālīta and nālitā. “She has combined two kinds of spinach, jute leaves, fenugreek, water lily stalks, anise, cucumbers and coriander in various ways to produce dishes that steal the pride of nectar.”

sanskrit:
kalambī pakva-ciñcāyā
rasa-pakvā ruci-pradā
kṛṣṇa-nālīta-śāko ’yam
āmāmra-phala-yuk śubhaḥ
translation: “She has cooked mouth-watering spinach in ripe tamarind juice, as well as a very attractive dish made from dark jute leaves combined with pieces of raw mango.”

sanskrit:
mayuṣṭhakasya mudgasya
māṣasyāpy adhunā mayā
trividho ’yaṃ sudhākūpa-
nibhaḥ sūpo vipācyate
translation: “And look here, my friend! From three different kinds of beans, I’ve prepared three kinds of soup that are like wells full of nectar.”

sanskrit:
paṅkaiḥ sumana-cūrṇānāṃ
dāsībhir bhṛśa-marditaiḥ
pūrṇendu-maṇḍalākārāḥ
kriyante roṭikā mayā
translation: “With wheat flour finely ground by the servant girls, I have made roṭikās shaped like the full moon.”

sanskrit:
kṛtāni kriyamāṇāni
kartavyāni tu kānicit
ity anna-vyañjanāni tvaṃ
saṃsiddhāni pratīhi nau
translation: “Yaśodā, all these rice and vegetable preparations we’ve been working on are almost finished.”

sanskrit:
saurabhya-sadvarṇa-manoharaṃ tat
sā vīkṣya sarvaṃ muditā babhūva
jijñāsamānām atha tad-vidhānaṃ
tāṃ rohiṇī vismaya-pūrvam āha
sāmagrī saiva sāmānyā
pākasya prakriyāpy asau
kintv apūrva-guṇe hetur
gāndharvā-hasta-sauṣṭhavam
Seeing all the aromatic, colorful and mouth-watering dishes, Yaśodā Mā became very
translation: happy. She asked, “How have you made all this so beautiful?” Surprised, Rohiṇī Mā replied, “All the ingredients and methods of cooking are available to anyone. But the extraordinary quality of these preparations can only be due to the skillful touch of Rādhikā’s graceful hands.”

sanskrit:
sā tāṃ rādhām anna-saṃskāra-saktāṃ
prasvidyantīṃ lajjayā namra-vaktrām
dṛṣṭvā rājñī sneha-viklinna-cittā
dāsīm asyā vījanāyādideśa
translation: Yaśodā Mā’s heart melted with affection when she saw Rādhā intently engaged in cooking, Her body covered with perspiration, Her head bowed in shyness. So Yaśodā directed one of the servant girls to begin fanning Her.

sanskrit:
vyāptāyāṃ vasanena bhojana-bhuvi śrī-ratna-pīṭhāgratas
tat-tad-vyañjana-ratna-ratna-puṭikā-paṅktiḥ krameṇābhitaḥ
miṣṭābhīṣṭa-supiṣṭakaugha-puṭikā-paṅktis tu tāsāṃ bahiḥ
samyag bhavya-sugavya-hema-puṭikā-paṅktiś ca tāsāṃ bahiḥ
ity evaṃ kramato ’rdha-maṇḍalatayā paṅkti-krameṇādbhute
svālībhiḥ puru-cāru-citra-racanād vaividhya āpādite
anyonyāvyatiṣakta-sūkṣma-surabhi-ślakṣṇair ghṛtācyotanair
madhye hemamayī vyadhāyi rucirā pātrī śubhair odanaiḥ
translation: Then, atop a beautiful, cloth-covered, jeweled table in the dining room, Śrīmatī’s sakhīs placed a row of begemmed vessels containing various types of curries. Outside that was a row of dishes containing delicious sweet cakes of many types, and beyond that a row of golden bowls filled with the finest of dairy products. In this way, the sakhīs very artistically arranged the vessels in rows of half-circles. Then in the middle of the table, they placed beautiful golden bowls filled with delicate, aromatic and tender boiled rice sprinkled with ghee.

sanskrit:
sauvarṇīṃ tala-pātrikāṃ ghṛta-puṭī-limpāka-khaṇḍādibhiḥ
sandhānārdra-rasāla-khaṇḍa-sahitaiḥ satkāsamardādibhiḥ
yuktāṃ dakṣiṇato nidhāya nikaṭe tasyāś ca bhṛṅgārakān
karpūreṇa suvāsitena payasā pūrṇān vyadhāt kānakān
translation: On the right side, different kinds of pickles made of lemon, ginger and mango pieces were placed on a golden plate, and near that were golden pitchers filled with camphor- scented water.

sanskrit:
tasyāḥ pāka-sukauśalaṃ bahu-vidhaṃ dṛṣṭvā vrajeśa-priyā
tāsāṃ tatpariveṣa-citra-racanāṃ cātisphurad-vismayā
ānetuṃ prajighāya vatsala-manāḥ kṛṣṇaṃ ca rāmaṃ ca sā
dhātreyīm atha tau samīyatur atiśraddhā-vaśād añjasā
translation: Vrajeśvarī was amazed to see the result of Śrī Rādhikā’s many cooking skills, as well as the artistically arranged table set by the sakhīs. Filled with motherly affection, she then sent her wet nurse to fetch Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, who, because They both loved and respected her, arrived there with great haste.

sanskrit:
natvā mātaram ājñayā saha-balas tasyāḥ samullāsanaḥ
premṇā bālaka-dāsikā-kṛta-padāmbhoja-dvayī-dhāvanaḥ
ācamyopaviveśa sammukhatayā cārv-annapātrī-puraḥ
sarvaṃ tat-tad-avekṣya vismita-manā babhrāja pītāmbaraḥ
translation: Dressed in radiant yellow cloth, Śrī Kṛṣṇa bowed down before His mother, and by her order, He and Balarāma allowed the young maidservants to lovingly wash Their feet. After sipping water, He sat down in front of a beautiful plate, and when He saw all the wonderful foods before Him, He was astonished!

sanskrit:
śrīdāma-subalau vāme
puro ’sya madhumaṅgalaḥ
dakṣiṇe śrī-balaś cānye
paritaḥ samupāviśan
translation: Śrīdāmā and Subala sat on Kṛṣṇa’s left, Madhumaṅgala in front of Him, and Balarāma to His right. His other friends surrounded Him in all directions.

sanskrit:
mātṛbhyāṃ krama-darśitena hi pathā bhoktuṃ samārabdhavān
yad yad bhoktum upakramaṃ sma kurute tyaktuṃ na tat soḍhavān
bhoktuṃ tat tad aśeṣam apy abhilaṣan sāmarthyavāṃś ca svayaṃ
kiñcit kiñcid abhukta vīkṣaka-bhiyā durvāda-bhītyāpy ayam
translation: Śrī Kṛṣṇa began to eat according to the way He had been taught by Mothers Yaśodā and Rohiṇī. They had told Him that whatever He begins to eat, He must finish. And even though He may want to eat everything there, and feel quite competent to do it, still, to avoid the criticism of others, He must eat just a little at a time.

sanskrit:
vyākhyādbhiḥ saha-bhojibhiḥ saha-balaiḥ pākasya tat-kauśalaṃ
svāduṅkāram adann avāg api hṛdā so ’pi praśaṃsann alam
ādau pāyasam āśa kiñcid apara-prācurya-paryāptatāṃ
vīkṣya vyañjana-ratna-yatna-gaminā lobhena bhūmnā citām
And then take some more.
translation: As Balarāma and the other young gopas praised the wonderful foods, Kṛṣṇa thought to Himself, “Wow! This is really good!” He began with just a little bit of sweet-rice, because He saw there were so many other tasty dishes, and He wanted to have room for them too.

sanskrit:
śākādi-kramato ’bhitoṣa-vaśataḥ sarvāṇi sad-vyañjanā-
ny ādan mātṛ-mude bhaved api yathā paktrī-manorañjanā
tān sarvān saha-bhojinaḥ sarasayā vācā hasan hāsayan
bhuñjadhvaṃ na parityajeta kim apīty ekāntam āhlādayan
translation: To please His mother and Śrī Rādhikā, Kṛṣṇa started with the vegetables and then finished off all the delicious preparations before Him. Laughing and joking with His friends, He would say, “Eat, eat! Make sure you don’t leave even a crumb!” Bantering like this, they were all having a great time together.

sanskrit:
sva-sva-saṃskṛta-miṣṭānnaṃ127
prātar-āśopayogi yat
upajahrus tayāhūtā
mātre gopyo mudānvitāḥ
translation: Summoned by Mother Yaśodā, the gopīs each joyfully brought the savory dishes they had prepared, which were just right for the morning meal, and gave them to her.

sanskrit:
śrī-rādhayā yatnata eva gehād
ānīta-khaṇḍodbhava-laḍḍukāni
gaṅgā-jalākhyāny atha raṅgadevī
tad-iṅgitenopajahāra mātre
translation: Then, at Śrī Rādhā’s signal, Raṅgadevī gave to Yaśodā all the pieces of the laḍḍu known as gaṅgā-jala that Śrīmatī had brought from home.

sanskrit:
tāni mātā balādibhyo
vibhajya snehato dadau
prakīrṇa-svarṇa-pātreṣu
vinidhāya pṛthak pṛthak
translation: Yaśodā Mā spread the laḍḍus upon a golden platter and then affectionately distributed them amongst Balarāma and the other boys.

sanskrit: Another reading is pakvānnam.
translation: A sweet made of coarsely ground gram or other pulse, or of corn-flour, mixed with sugar and spices, and fried in ghee or oil. (Monier-Williams) āsvādayantaṃ ghṛta-pakvam annaṃ sunarmabhis tān api hāsayantam ālokayantaṃ nayanāñcalena rādhānanaṃ taṃ dadṛśur mudālyaḥ While Śrī Kṛṣṇa ate the different ghee-cooked foods, He laughed and joked with His friends, and occasionally sneaked a sidelong glance at the face of Śrī Rādhā. When Śrīmatī’s sakhīs saw this, they were filled with joy.

sanskrit:
ado bhadram idaṃ miṣṭam
etat snigdhaṃ sucāru tat
tarjanyā darśayanty ambā
bhuṅkṣva vatsety abhāṣata
translation: With her forefinger, Yaśodā Mā pointed out the different foods and said, “My child, eat some of these. That one is very healthy, and this one here is very sweet. That one has a mild taste, and that one, oh, it’s delightful.”

sanskrit:
yad yad iṣṭaṃ bhaved yasya
jñātvā jñātvā hasan hariḥ
tasmai tasmai dadau tat tat
svapātrāt prakṣipan muhuḥ
translation: Because Śrī Kṛṣṇa knew which foods each of His friends liked best, He began to take those foods from His own plate, and with a big smile, give them to the appropriate boys.

sanskrit:
vīkṣya yatnānvitām ambāṃ
mandam aśnantam acyutam
parihāsa-paṭus tasmin
vrajeśām avadad baṭuḥ
ayaṃ ced bhūri nātty amba!
dehi me sarvam admy asau
mayaivāliṅgitaḥ puṣṭo
bhavitā bhūri-bhojinā
nāsya manda-ruceḥ śaktir
ghṛta-pakvānna-bhojane
tad asmai laghu-rāddhānnaṃ
vyañjanāny amba! dāpaya
translation: When the jokester Madhumaṅgala noticed how diligently Kṛṣṇa’s mother was working to serve the food, and how Kṛṣṇa was not eating very much, he said to Yaśodā, “Mother! Since Kṛṣṇa’s hardly eating anything, why not give all the food to me? I’m a big eater! Then, after I’ve eaten, I’ll give Him a hug and that will cause His body to be nourished too. Because of His sluggish appetite, He’s not able to digest foods that have been cooked in ghee. But for me, that’s not a problem, so you please just put them all right here.”

sanskrit:
atha kṛṣṇaḥ svapātrastha-
pakvānnāñjalibhir hasan
pañca-ṣaiḥ pūrayāmāsa
bhuṅkṣveti baṭu-bhājanam
translation: Laughing at Madhumaṅgala’s words, Śrī Kṛṣṇa took five or six handfuls of food from His plate and filled Madhu’s plate, saying, “Eat!”

sanskrit:
tato vāma-kaphoṇiṃ svaṃ
vādayan vāma-pārśvake
samyag bhoktuṃ kṛtārambhaḥ
prahṛṣṭo baṭur āha tam
vayasya! paśya bhakṣye ’ham
ity aśnan kavala-dvayam
mātar me dadhi dehīti
prāhiṇot tāṃ tadāhṛtau
translation: Then Madhumaṅgala slapped his left elbow against his side (making a funny sound) and began to eat all the food. Delighted, he said to Kṛṣṇa, “Friend! I’ll eat; You watch.” Then he ate two big mouthfuls and said, “Mother, please give me some yogurt,” and sent her after some.

sanskrit:
gopāḥ paśyata nṛtyatīha capalaḥ pakvānna-labdhāśayā
kīśeśo dadhi-lampaṭo ’yam iti tān kṛtvonmukhāṃs tad-diśi
teṣāṃ bhojana-bhājaneṣu śanakair nikṣipya bhakṣyaṃ nijaṃ
sarvaṃ bhuktam idaṃ mayeti sa punar garvāyamāno ’vadat
translation: After Yaśodā Mā had gone, Madhumaṅgala said, “Hey look, guys! That restless monkey king over there is greedy for yogurt, so he’s dancing around hoping he’ll get some food.” When they raised their heads and looked in that direction, Madhu very quietly took all the food from his plate and put it on theirs. Then he boasted, “See, I’ve eaten everything!”

sanskrit:
tathāgatāṃ tāṃ dadhi-pātra-hastām
uvāca paśyāmba! vinaiva dadhnā
mayopabhuktaṃ drutam eva sarvaṃ
tat pāyasaṃ dāpaya bhūri mahyam
Yaśodā Mā then arrived, carrying a bowl of yogurt. “Mā, look! Even without yogurt, I ate
translation: everything on my plate,” Madhumaṅgala said. “Now please give me a whole bunch of sweet rice.”

sanskrit:
haimeṣu pātreṣu nidhāya rādhayā
navīna-rambhā-dala-manda-mārutaiḥ
śītīkṛtaṃ sve pariveśitaṃ kare
tebhyo dadau pāyasam āśu rohiṇī
translation: Then Rohiṇī Devī began to personally serve them sweet rice that Śrī Rādhikā had placed in a golden bowl and made cool by gently fanning it with plantain leaves.

sanskrit:
ānīyānīya gāndharvā-
dattāni vyañjanāni sā
śākādīny amla-śeṣāṇi
tebhyo ’dāt kramaśaḥ śanaiḥ
translation: After that, one by one, Rohiṇī Mātā began to serve all the remaining preparations made from leafy green vegetables that Rādhikā brought to her.

sanskrit:
rambhodarastha-cchada-varṇa-lāghavāḥ
saṃmṛṣṭa-godhūma-sucūrṇa-roṭikāḥ
ghṛtābhiṣiktāḥ pariveśitās tayā
tebhyo ’nya-pātreṣu nidhāya sā dadau
translation: Then, from another platter, she served the boys roṭikās, which were very light, made of clean, finely ground wheat flour, whitish in color like the inner leaves of a banana tree, and moistened with ghee.

sanskrit:
kṛṣṇaḥ satṛṣṇo naivātra
balaḥ kavala-mātra-bhuk
śrīdāmā nāma mandāśī
subalo ’su-balojjhitaḥ
A kind of thin, saucer-shaped bread
translation: This verse was written by the compiler of the book, Śrī Siddha Kṛṣṇa Dāsa Bābājī, as an introduction to some verses from Śrī Kṛṣṇa-bhāvanāmṛtam concerning the same līlā as those we just read. Baṭu said, “Kṛṣṇa isn’t very interested in this delicious food, and Baladeva can only eat one mouthful. Śrīdāmā is naturally a slow eater, and Subala eats so little he’s become weak.”

sanskrit:
kvaiṣāṃ bhakṣyaikatānatva-
rāhityam avidagdhatā
kvaitad annaṃ sudhā-nindi
svayaṃ lakṣmyaiva sādhitam
translation: “H ā y ! How can they be so indifferent toward food such as this, which has been personally prepared by the Goddess of Fortune and is tastier than nectar?”

sanskrit:
kāvyaṃ viphalatāṃ kiṃ na
yāti sat-kavi-nirmitam?
yatra goṣṭhyāṃ tad-āsvāda-
lolupatvaṃ na vartate
translation: “Just as it is useless to recite fine poetry in an assembly where there are no connoisseurs, in the same way, how can it not be useless to offer fine delicacies in a place where there are no gourmets?”

sanskrit:
catur-varga-phalam mūrtaṃ
etad-annaṃ catur-vidham
ahaṃ kevalam eko ’sya
pātram ity avadad baṭuḥ
translation: “These four kinds of food are the embodiment of the four goals of human life, and only I am a qualified receptacle for them.”

sanskrit:
śrīdāmovāca piṇḍībhiḥ
piciṇḍaṃ pūraya drutam
yad eva tava sarvasvaṃ
yad arthaṃ baṭutām adhāḥ
translation: Śrīdāmā said, “Just go ahead and quickly fill your belly with food, which means everything to you, and is the purpose for which you became a brāhmaṇa.”

sanskrit:
baṭur ākhyad are mūrkha!
gopas tvaṃ kiṃ nu vetsyasi?
rasāsvādaṃ svadharmārthaṃ
gā roddhum aṭavīm aṭa
Baṭu is another name for Madhumaṅgala, meaning a brāhmaṇa boy.
translation: Baṭu retorted, “Hey blockhead! You’re a cowherd boy! What could you possibly know about the enjoyment of subtle flavors? Go do your own duty! Go to the pasturing grounds and herd your cows.”

sanskrit:
paśyaiṣo ’ham anūcāno
vipro yair man-mukhe hutam!
tair iṣṭaḥ sarva-yajñena
bhagavān eva kevalam
translation: “Look! I’m a highly learned brāhmaṇa. Whoever merely feeds me gets the result of having worshipped Bhagavān by all the different kinds of sacrifices.”

sanskrit:
śrīdāmoce śruti-smṛtyor
vartmāpi śata-janmasu
tvayā paricitaṃ naiva
vipratve sūtram eva te
translation: Śrīdāmā replied, “Baṭu, even after hundreds of births you don’t know anything about śruti and smṛti. The only thing brahmanical about you is your thread.”

sanskrit:
kṛṣṇaḥ prāha baṭor asti
rasa-śāstre ’nuśīlanam
vyañjanāneka-tātparya-
lakṣaṇābhijñatā yataḥ
translation: Kṛṣṇa declared, “Baṭu has studied the rasa-śāstras. That’s where he learned about the characteristics of so many types of foods.”132

sanskrit:
baṭur āha ṣaḍ evātra
rasā na tv aṣṭa man-mate
ṣoḍhaiva nyāyya āsvādo
yat ṣaḍ evendriyāṇi naḥ
translation: Baṭu said, “Sometimes it’s said there are eight rasas (flavors), but I think there are only six. It’s only logical because we have six senses with which to taste them.”

sanskrit: rasā hy aṣṭāv iti prāhur
translation: The term vyañjanāneka in this verse can be divided as either vyañjana aneka (many types of spicy dishes) or vyañjanā aneka (many types of figurative speech). So another reading could be: “That’s where he learned how to speak in such colorful ways.” The five senses and the mind ye te ’pi vyañjanāśritāḥ vyañjanābhijñatā-leśo ’py eṣāṃ kintu na vidyate “Those who say there are eight rasas depend upon vyañjanā (ornamental language), but they don’t know anything about this kind of vyañjana (spicy foods).”134

sanskrit:
vihāya śāka-sūpādīn
vihāyas te dhayanti yat
tan nīraṃ prakaṭaṃ hitvā
dhāvanty eva marīcikām
translation: “Those who give up the tangible rasa of vegetables, soup and other delicious foods to taste something ethereal (the erotic sentiment, etc.) are like people who reject pure water just to chase after a mirage.”

sanskrit:
kāraṇaṃ rasa-niṣpattau
carvaṇeneti taj jaguḥ
carvan tu paricoṣyanti
na pitur janma-koṭibhiḥ
translation: “They say that the way to extract rasa is by chewing, but even in millions of births they’ll never completely get the juice just by chewing.”135

sanskrit:
rāmaḥ prāha rasāsvāde
ke ’nubhāvā bhavan-mate
ke vā sañcāriṇaḥ ko vā
sthāyī sa svādyate katham
translation: Balarāma asked, “Concerning the tasting of rasa, in your opinion, what are the a n u b h ā v a s ? What are the sañcārīs, and what is the sthāyī-bhāva? How may they be experienced?”136

sanskrit:
baṭur ūce yad aprāptyā
pūrvam evāśru me bhavet
prāptyā tu vyañjanasyāsya
pulakāsya-prasannate
translation: Or, if we use vyañjana/vyañjanā differently, “Even though these paṇḍitas are so dependent on food, they sure don’t seem to know much about it.” The word carvaṇa primarily means ‘chewing’, but it can also mean ‘tasting, or relishing’, which would be the meaning used by literary connoisseurs. But here Madhumaṅgala is cleverly using it as ‘chewing’, noting that the kind of rasa the litterateurs are after is ethereal, and there’s no way to chew something that has no tangible form. Anubhāvas are physical expressions of internal feelings, such as tears, frowning, sighs, etc. Sañcārīs are passing sentiments, and the sthāyī-bhāva is the dominant mood. Baṭu replied, “If I don’t get my delicious food, there’s a good chance I’ll cry. If I get it, my skin erupts in goosebumps and my face becomes tranquil.”

sanskrit:
varṇasya snigdhatā-tṛptyā
vaivarṇyaṃ tac ca paśya me
bhuñjāna eva yad vacmi
svaro me tena bhidyate
translation: “When eating, I become so satisfied that my complexion becomes smooth and radiant. See, that’s the vaivarṇyam, or color change. And when I try to talk, my speech becomes broken and indistinct.”137

sanskrit:
stambho me bhūri miṣṭānna-
bhojanāśakti-duḥkha-jaḥ
prasvedaḥ prakaṭo ’nte tu
pralayo bahu-bhakṣaṇāt
translation: “When I’m unable to eat copious amounts of sweetmeats, I feel miserable and can’t move my limbs. After eating a huge meal I break out in a sweat and finally just pass out.”

sanskrit:
ālasya-cintā-svāpādyāḥ
spaṣṭāḥ sañcāriṇo ’tra naḥ
svādyatvenaika evāpi
sthāyī tu vividhābhidhaḥ
translation: “The temporary moods of lethargy, anxiety and sleepiness are also clearly evident within me. But the primary mood is simply enjoyment, though it is known by various names.”

sanskrit:
ājyābhyaktāni bhaktāni
manye kāñcana-vāriṇā
snapitānīva saurabhyaṃ
yeṣāṃ saulabhyam abhyagāt
godanta-kṛtta-ghāsādi-
ghrāyiṇyāṃ gopa-saṃsadi
kṛta-puṇyasya me bhūri-
bhoga-bhājaḥ prasaṅgataḥ
translation: “Due to my piety, I am able to enjoy great amounts of delicious foods. I think that because these gopas, who are accustomed to smelling the grass cut by the grazing cows, have had my association, they too are able to relish the delectable aroma of these ghee-smeared foods, which appear as though they’ve been bathed in golden water.”

sanskrit:
vane viprās tapasyanti
patra-mūla-phalāśanāḥ
baṭos te nādhikāro ’sti
bhoge yāhi tapaś cara
translation: Śrīdāmā replied, “Brāhmaṇas practice austerity in the forest by eating only leaves, roots and fruits. They have no right to engage in sense enjoyment. You should go and perform austerities.”

sanskrit:
satyaṃ bho yaiḥ purā taptaṃ
patra-mūla-phalādibhiḥ
pariṇamya januṣy atra
vyañjanatvena tair mama
bhauma-svarga-juṣaḥ sādhu
pratyakṣī-bhūyate ’nvaham
iti jānīta bhogo ’yam
atapta-tapasaḥ kutaḥ
translation: Baṭu responded, “Ah, Śrīdāmā, what you say is true. In a previous lifetime I performed such tapas as only eating leaves, roots and fruits. Now, in this life, they have been transformed into delicious curries. The most exalted residents of earth and heaven appear before me daily. Thus, you should understand that such enjoyment cannot come to someone whose austerities have not been fulfilled.”

sanskrit:
evaṃ cet prathamaṃ prāptum
arhanty ete valīmukhāḥ
vāgvyaya-śramiṇo ’trāpi
januṣy ete tapasvinaḥ
translation: When Mother Rohiṇī arrived with Madhumaṅgala’s sweet rice, Subala said, “These monkeys deserve to be fed first because, like Baṭu, they are also weary of talking and are ascetics by nature.”

sanskrit:
śītoṣṇa-vāta-sahanāḥ
patra-puṣpa-phalāśanāḥ
jāti-smarāḥ kathaṃ na syuḥ
ko ’mīṣāṃ vetti vijñatām
translation: “These monkeys live in the forest, enduring heat and cold, wind and rain, eating only leaves, flowers and fruits. How can we say they don’t remember their previous births? Who knows how much wisdom they may have?”

sanskrit:
kṛṣṇaḥ prāha sakhe! viprā
brahmopāsana-tatparāḥ
kīśāḥ kukṣimbharā eṣāṃ
dvayeṣāṃ mahad-antaram
translation: Then Kṛṣṇa said, “Subala, My friend! The brāhmaṇas are devoted to worshipping God, while these monkeys are only interested in filling their bellies. There is a big difference between the two.”

sanskrit:
asya kīśasya cāvaimi
na kim apy antaraṃ hare!
naratvaṃ vānaratvaṃ vā-
nayor bhede na kāraṇam
Subala replied, “Hey Kṛṣṇa! Personally, I don’t see any difference between this brāhmaṇa
translation: and that monkey. There’s no reason to divide them according to manhood or monkeyhood.”

sanskrit:
kiṃ ca khyāpayatā tena
loke ’pūrvāṃ svavijnatāṃ
bṛhattvād bṛṃhaṇatvāc ca
svakukṣir brahma manyate
translation: “Moreover, he is propagating his own strange ideas, unheard of in this world. He considers his own belly as Brahman because of its vastness and continuous expansion.”

sanskrit:
atas triṣavaṇaṃ tasya
dhyāyatā pūrti-sādhanam
sa evopāsyate ’nena
naiṣṭhika-brahmacāriṇā
translation: “Because of this, three times a day this naiṣṭhika-brahmacārī138 meditates upon satisfying his belly, and in this way Brahman is worshipped.”

sanskrit:
kadācid bhūri-pakkānna-
grasanāveśa-saṃbhramaiḥ
kīśāyitaṃ syāt pāṇibhyāṃ
bhuñjānasyāsya lāghavaiḥ
translation: “Sometimes, when he’s absorbed in eagerly eating big mouthfuls of food, he uses both hands, just like a monkey!”

sanskrit:
Celibate religious student
ity uktvājīhasat sarvān
subalas tān baṭuḥ sa tu
hasan bhuñjāna evoccaiḥ
kāśaiḥ śoṇa-mukho ’bhavat
translation: When Subala said this, all the boys began to laugh, including Baṭu, who was still eating. His laughing (with food in his mouth) caused him to cough loudly until his face became a bright red.

sanskrit:
goṣṭheśāha baṭo! tiṣṭha
kṣaṇaṃ mā bhuṅkṣva mā hasa!
sthairyam āpnuhi mā jalpa
mainaṃ hāsayatārbhakāḥ
translation: Seeing this, Yaśodā Mā said, “Baṭu, be still for a moment! Don’t eat, don’t laugh, don’t talk; just calm down. And you boys, stop making him laugh!”

sanskrit:
dhaniṣṭhayā yal-lalitādi-saṃskṛtaṃ
tat-tad-rasālādikam āhṛtaṃ puraḥ
kṛtvā pṛthak pātracaye vrajeśvarī
sasneham ebhyo dadatī mumoda sā
translation: Then Dhaniṣṭhā placed the rasāla and other foods prepared by Lalitā and the others upon separate plates and brought them there. Feeling great joy, Vrajeśvarī affectionately served the preparations to all the boys.

sanskrit:
hṛdaya-dayita-mukha-vīkṣaṇa-hṛṣṭās
tad atimadhura-mṛdu-kānti-vikṛṣṭāḥ
mumudur udita-pṛthu-bhāva-vihastā
ramaṇa-bhavanam adhi tāḥ puru-śastāḥ
translation: There, in Kṛṣṇa’s home, those greatly fortunate gopīs, bewildered by their deep love and drawn helplessly by His sweet and gentle charm, rejoiced when they saw the face of their beloved.

sanskrit:
annānyatho tāni catur-vidhāni te
pīyuṣa-sārodbhava-vikriyā iva
āsvādayanto madhurāṇi saspṛhaṃ
taṃ hāsayanto jahasuś ca narmabhiḥ
translation: While Kṛṣṇa’s friends eagerly tasted those four kinds of delicious foods, which seemed to be transformations of the essence of nectar, they all joked and laughed, and made Him laugh too.

sanskrit:
carvanti carvyāṇi mṛdūni kecil
lehyāni cānye caṭulaṃ lihanti
pibanti peyāni pare prahṛṣṭāś
cūṣyanti coṣyāṇy apare vitṛptāḥ
translation: Some of them were chewing soft, tender foods, while others licked up sweet ones. Some were drinking liquids with great delight, and some satisfied themselves by sucking (on mangoes and other fruits).

sanskrit:
svāduṅkāraṃ kamala-nayanaḥ saspṛhaṃ tat tad annaṃ
hasta-sparśād amṛta-madhuraṃ manda-mandaṃ priyāyāḥ
tad vaktrābja-prahita-nayana-prānta-bhṛṅgo nigūḍhaṃ
prāśnann ambā-manasi nibiḍaṃ sa pramodaṃ vyatānīt
translation: As the lotus-eyed Śrī Kṛṣṇa leisurely enjoyed the delicious food, made sweeter than nectar by the touch of His lover’s hand, He cast a secret sidelong glance at Śrīmatī’s face, His dark eyes like black bees flying to a lotus flower. Seeing this, Yaśodā’s mind was filled with great joy.

sanskrit:
prahita-cakita-netra-prānta-dṛṣṭi-praṇālī-
milita-tad-atilāvanyāmṛtāsvāda-puṣṭā
prasarad-akhila-bhāvollāsam ācchādayantī
dayita-hṛdayam uccai rādhikāpy ājahāra
translation: Nourished by the sweet wine of Kṛṣṇa’s charm that flowed through the channel of His timid sidelong glances, Śrī Rādhikā, struggling to conceal Her delight, also forcefully attracted the heart of Her lover.

sanskrit:
atha bala-jananīṃ tām antarākṛtya nṛtyan-
madakala-madirākṣīm arpayantīṃ kare ’syāḥ
mṛdu mṛdu madhurānnaṃ preyasīṃ prekṣya kṛṣṇaḥ
ślatha-rucir aśane ’bhūd unmanā nāgareśaḥ
translation: With Rohiṇī Mā between Them quietly serving the delicious foods, Nāgareśa Kṛṣṇa again looked toward His beloved Rādhā. Seeing Her lovely eyes, dancing like drunken wagtails, He soon lost all taste for eating and became disoriented.

sanskrit:
sāmibhuktaṃ kiyat tena
kiṃca tryaṃśāvaśeṣitam
bhakṣyaṃ vīkṣyāśane mandaṃ
taṃ cāsīd vyākulā prasūḥ
King of philanderers
translation: Seeing that Kṛṣṇa had only half-eaten some foods, and left a third of others untouched because of His weak appetite, Mother Yaśodā became anxious.

sanskrit:
yatnāt saṃskṛtam annādi
sarvaṃ tyaktaṃ kathaṃ suta!
kṣudhito ’si kiyad bhuṅkṣva
śapathaḥ śiraso mama
translation: Yaśodā said, “My child! Why have You left all this food, which was so carefully prepared? If You’re hungry, You must at least eat a little. Otherwise, a curse will fall upon my head!”

sanskrit:
ānāyya yatnād vṛṣabhānu-kanyakāṃ
saṃskāritaṃ sarvam idaṃ sutānayā
annādi miṣṭaṃ ca sudhā-parārddhatas
tathāpi nāśnāsi karomi kiṃ hatā
translation: “Child! With great endeavor I had the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu brought here to make all these preparations, which are more delicious than nectar. But still, You don’t eat! I’m baffled; what can I do?”

sanskrit:
atha sā rohiṇīm āha
paśya rohiṇi! cañcalaḥ
durbalaḥ kṣudhito ’py eṣa
kim apy atti na manda-bhuk
translation: Then Yaśodā said, “Look at this, Rohiṇī! This restless boy is weak from hunger, but still, because He has such a feeble appetite, He’s hardly eaten anything.”

sanskrit:
tataḥ sneha-parītāṅgī
lālayanty agha-mardanam
pralamba-hantur ambeyaṃ
babhāṣe taṃ puraḥsthitā
yatnād annaṃ sādhitaṃ vatsa! miṣṭaṃ
mallī-mṛdvyā rādhayedaṃ mayā ca
kṣut-kṣāmo ’si tvaṃ ca nāśnāsi tat tām
ambām etāṃ māṃ ca kiṃvā dunoṣi
translation: Rohiṇī Mā, the mother of the killer of Pralamba, came before Kṛṣṇa, the destroyer of Agha, and began to very affectionately caress Him. She said, “Child! This delicate jasmine Rādhikā and I have very carefully prepared all these savory dishes, but even though You are emaciated with hunger, still You don’t eat! Why do You make Your mother, Rādhā and me suffer like this?”

sanskrit:
jananī tava paśya khidyate
suta! nirmañcanam atra yāmi te
bhramato bhavitā vane śramaḥ
kiyad aśnīhi vidhehi mad-vacaḥ
translation: “Child! Just look at how depressed Your mother is. Please cheer her up! She thinks that You must be tired from wandering in the forest, so do what I say and eat a little something.”

sanskrit:
bhuktaṃ mayā bhūri gatā bubhukṣe-
ty uktvā niyamyocchalitaṃ vikāram
taṃ vīkṣya mandaṃ punar apy adantaṃ
nanandatur nanda-sutaṃ jananyau
translation: Kṛṣṇa replied, “Mā, I’ve eaten plenty! I’m not hungry anymore.” Restraining the emotion that arose from seeing Rādhikā, He slowly resumed eating. His two mothers were pleased to see this.

sanskrit:
idam idam atimiṣṭaṃ vatsa! bhuṅkṣveti mātā
saśapatham atha tat-tad-darśayanty aṅgulībhiḥ
sakalam abhilaṣantī kartum aśru-plutākṣī
tad udara-gatam annaṃ sātmajaṃ vāvadīti
translation: Still determined to get Kṛṣṇa to eat everything, Yaśodā, with teary eyes, pointed to each of the foods and very firmly said, “Child! All these foods are delicious. You must eat!”

sanskrit:
rasālā-pakvāmra-drava-śikhariṇī-ṣāḍava-payaḥ-
karambhāmikṣā-vyañjana-dadhi-phalāpūpa-vaṭakān
kṛtāmreḍā netra-stanaja-payasā klinna-sicayā-
py atṛptā taṃ tṛptaṃ muhur atha sutaṃ prāśayad iyam
translation: Even though Kṛṣṇa was already satisfied, Yaśodā Mā, whose dress was moistened by her tears and breast milk, was not. She repeatedly served Him rasālā 141 , ripe mango juice, śikhariṇī142, sweetmeats, milk, farina mixed with yogurt, spicy vegetables mixed with curd, yogurt, fruitcakes and other kinds of round cakes.

sanskrit:
bhakṣyaṃ bhojyaṃ bahutara-miṣṭaṃ
lehyaṃ peyaṃ mṛdu-madhuraṃ te
bhuktvā pītvā rasabhara-tṛptāḥ
sarve ’bhūvan vana-gamanotkāḥ
Curds mixed with sugar and spices
translation: Another dish of curds mixed with sugar and different spices After chewing, sucking, licking and drinking many delicious, delicate and savory foods, all the delighted and thoroughly satisfied boys became eager to leave for the forest.

sanskrit:
sarve suvāsita-mṛdā mukha-pāṇi-padmā-
ny āmṛjya sādhu mṛduleṣikayā ca dantān
dāsaiḥ praṇīta-kanakādika-kuṇḍikāsu
tair datta-vāribhir athācamanaṃ vyadhūs te
translation: Then, after cleansing their lotus hands and faces with fragrant clay, the boys brushed their teeth with tender twigs and rinsed their mouths with water brought by the servants in golden vessels.

sanskrit:
elā-lavaṅga-ghanasāra-vimiśritābhir
jambūla-datta-vara-khādira-golikābhiḥ
śītojjvalābhir adhivāsya mudā mukhaṃ te
savyena pūrṇam udaraṃ mamṛjuḥ kareṇa
translation: After that, the boys freshened their mouths with a cool and invigorating mixture of cardamom, cloves, camphor and little balls of catechu given to them by the servant named Jambūla. Then they all happily began to rub their full bellies with their left hands.

sanskrit:
rasāla-kara-saṃskṛtopahṛta-nāgavallī-sphurat-
supakva-dala-vīṭikāḥ sukham adanta evotsukāḥ
tataḥ śatapadāntarālaya-viśāla-palyaṅkikā-
kuleṣv atha viśaśramuḥ parijanair amī vījitāḥ
translation: As each happily chewed a quid of excellent tāmbūla prepared by the servant named Rasāla, they eagerly walked about a hundred steps over to a group of rooms filled with large couches, where they rested while being fanned by the servants.

sanskrit:
tam iha viśramitaṃ paricārakāḥ
śikhi-dala-vyajanaiḥ samavījayan
avadalayya dalaṃ mṛdu-vīṭikāḥ
prabhum athādayati sma vilāsakaḥ
translation: The servants helped relieve Kṛṣṇa’s fatigue by cooling Him with a fan made of peacock feathers. Then the servant named Vilāsaka broke another betel leaf, prepared some tender tāmbūla and gave it to his master.

sanskrit:
niṣkramya dhautāṅghri-karāṃ mahānasād
dāsī-gaṇais tāṃ vyajanair upāsitām
rādhāṃ prakoṣṭhāntara-gāṃ sakhī-janair
vilokayantīṃ ramaṇaṃ gavākṣataḥ
ānandaja-sveda-jalair vrajeśayā
pratīyamānāṃ śrama-karṣitety alam
bhoktuṃ prayatnād upaveśya sā mudā
balāmbayānnāni gṛhād adāpayat
translation: Along with Her sakhīs, Śrī Rādhā then went from the kitchen into another room where the servant girls washed Her hands and feet and fanned Her as She peered through a window at Her beloved. The ecstasy of seeing Kṛṣṇa caused Śrīmatī to perspire heavily, but Vrajeśvarī thought, “She must be sweating because of all the cooking She did.” Then Yaśodā asked Rohiṇī to carefully bring food from the house, and with great delight, she had Rādhikā sit down to eat.

sanskrit:
tayā nidiṣṭā ghṛta-saṃskṛtānnaṃ
dātuṃ dhaniṣṭhā hari-bhukta-śeṣaiḥ
saṃmiśrya gūḍhaṃ ghṛta-saṃskṛtānnair
gṛhāt tadānīya dadāv amūbhyaḥ
translation: When ordered by Yaśodā Mā to serve the ghee-cooked preparations, Dhaniṣṭhā secretly mixed them with the remnants from Kṛṣṇa’s meal, then brought them from the house and distributed them to Śrīmatī and Her sakhīs.

sanskrit:
anaśnantīṃ hriyā vīkṣya
vastrāvṛta-natānanām
rādhikām avadat kṛṣṇa-
mātā vātsalya-viklavā
janani! mayi jananyāṃ kiṃ nu lajjedṛśīyaṃ
suta iva mama cetaḥ snihyati tvayy atīva
ayi tad apanayaināṃ yāmi nirmañcanaṃ te
śiśiraya mama netraṃ bhuṅkṣva paśyāmi sākṣāt
translation: Seeing that Rādhā wasn’t eating anything, Her face downcast in shyness, Yaśodā was overcome by motherly affection. She said, “Mother! I love You as I do my own son. There’s no need for You to be shy, so please give it up. I’d do anything for You. Please soothe my eyes by letting me see You eat a little something.”

sanskrit:
yūyaṃ ca me stha tanayās tv anayā hriyā kiṃ
putryaḥ kurudhvam aśanaṃ lalitādayas tat
ity āgrahāc chapatha-dāna-śataiś ca mātā
miṣṭānna-miṣṭa-vacanaiḥ samabhojayat tāḥ
translation: Addressing Lalitā and the others, Yaśodā Mā said, “You are all just like daughters to me! Why are you being so shy? Please eat something!” Pleading repeatedly with such sweet words, she finally persuaded them to eat.

sanskrit:
hṛdy udgataiḥ suta-kara-grahaṇābhilāṣais
tad bhūṣaṇaiḥ subahuśaḥ saha yāni yatnāt
niṣpādya tan navavadhū-pratirūpakāṇi
snehād dhṛtāni sadane vara-sampuṭeṣu
Dreaming of Kṛṣṇa’s future wedding day, Yaśodā previously had many beautiful
translation: ornaments carefully created that would be worthy of His bride, and She had lovingly kept them in fine jewelry boxes at home.

sanskrit:
tair bhūṣaṇair atha dhaniṣṭhikayopanītais
tāmbūla-candana-navāmbara-nāgajaiś ca
ālī-vṛtāṃ nava-vadhūm iva tāṃ vrajeśā
sammānya hārda-valitā muditā babhūva
translation: Filled with affection, Yaśodā joyfully honored Śrī Rādhā with those ornaments, as well as tāmbūla, candana, new clothing and sindūra brought by Dhaniṣṭhā, as though She were a new bride surrounded by Her girlfriends.

sanskrit:
rādhā-hṛtaṃ yan niśi tad viśākhā
dhaniṣṭhayādāt subalāya gūḍham
pītottarīyaṃ subalo ’pi tasyai
nīlāmbaraṃ kṛṣṇa-hṛtaṃ tayaiva
translation: The previous night, Rādhā had taken Kṛṣṇa’s yellow upper cloth by mistake, and Kṛṣṇa had worn Rādhā’s blue cloth. So now Viśākhā gave Kṛṣṇa’s cloth to Dhaniṣṭhā, who secretly slipped it to Subala, and Subala returned Rādhā’s cloth to Viśākhā in the same way.
